Much as Sacramento’s original Public Market at the corner of 13 & J Streets, the Midtown Bazaar enlivens the centralized Midtown Sacramento corner. Embracing Midtown’s avant-garde personality, the market promotes community while providing artisans, musicians, local and organic farmers, small businesses and eateries an opportunity to engage with customers. title: Citizens Academy
description:
Meet your public safety leaders, officials, officers and experts. Learn about racial profiling, gang and hate crimes, in-car cameras, internal affairs, “three strikes” and more. Lunch with judges, tour the county jail and communication center and see a taser demonstration.

The Sacramento County District Attorney’s Office, the Sacramento Police Department, and the Sacramento Sheriff’s Department are proud to announce its 11th Citizens Academy course. In an effort to improve communication, relationships, and provide a better understanding between ethnic and cultural communities and the criminal justice system, District Attorney Jan Scully formed the Citizens Academy.

Since the start of the academy in 2002, there have been ten graduating classes with more than 500 participants. In partnership with the Sacramento Police Department and Sacramento Sheriff’s Department, Jan Scully has brought this program to the community to provide an overview of the criminal justice system (law enforcement roles, responsibilities, and challenges) and to engage citizens from all backgrounds in communication, participation and mutual learning about issues within the criminal justice system. The course continues to make a great impact on multicultural and multi-ethnic sensitivity within the criminal justice community.

Representatives from the DA’s office, the judiciary, public defense, law enforcement, and community organizations answer community questions, address their concerns and demonstrate a commitment to building, bridges between the criminal justice system and the various ethnic, racial and faith-based communities. Citizens Academy is hosted by the District Attorney’s Office in partnership with the Sacramento Police Department, and Sacramento Sheriff’s Department.

title: Jewish Voices Concert with Rebecca Plack
description:
Local soprano Rebecca Plack will perform songs originally composed or performed by Jewish performers in a solo concert of classical, opera, traditional folk melodies, and Broadway show tunes titled, Jewish Voices: Songs from the Old World, Tunes from the New. Joined by Greg Mason on piano, Plack will highlight Jewish composers ranging from Gustav Mahler to George Gershwin to Stephen Sondheim. She will also showcase the work of Lotte Schöne, the reigning diva of the Berlin State Opera, until she was forced to flee Nazi Germany in 1933.

The first half of the program highlights songs that were composed, performed, and recorded by Jewish musicians before World War II. It begins with songs of Gustav Mahler (1860-1911) and continues with songs of Alexander Zemlinsky (1871-1942), a Viennese Jew whose lyrically beautiful compositions are virtually unknown today. The first half concludes with repertoire of soprano Lotte Schöne (1891-1977).

The concert’s second half features the works of Jewish lyricists and composers who emigrated to America and Israel after the war. These include generations of writers for the American musical theater, such as George Gershwin, Dorothy Fields, and Stephen Sondheim whose Broadway songs are now well-known theatrical standards. The program concludes with Hebrew and Yiddish songs.

With her vibrant voice and her musical knowledge, Plack has performed across the United States, Canada, and Europe. She has given solo recitals for the International Great Romantics Festival in Hamilton, Canada, the ATERForum Festival in Ferrara, Italy, and the Franz Liszt Museum in Budapest. Locally, she has sung at the Mondavi Center for the Performing Arts, the Sacramento Opera, and the Chamber Music Society of Sacramento. Rebecca recently joined the faculty at the San Francisco Conservatory of Music, where she did postgraduate work. She holds degrees in musicology and voice from Princeton University, Manhattan School of Music, and Cornell University. Plack maintains private voice studios in Sacramento and Davis.

The concert will be held at the Center at Twenty-Three Hundred, Sacramento’s newest multi-use venue with state-of-the-art lighting and sound. The concert will help raise funds for the purchase of a new grand piano for the Center at Twenty-Three Hundred and benefit Mosaic Law Congregation’s general fund.

title: Rockin' Geology
description:
The Discovery Museum Science & Space Center celebrates our 60th Anniversary with a year-long retrospective of science milestones of the last six decades. In April, we celebrate great science of the 1960s.

Did you know earthquakes, volcanic activity, mountain-building, and oceanic trenches are all the result of plate tectonics? The idea of plate tectonics was defined in 1967. Cindy Pridmore, geologist with the California Geological Survey, will talk about why and where we have earthquakes in our state. There'll be fault blocks, the liquefaction box, the new state fault map, and a make and take fault activity map. You can use the amazing Make-A-Quake machine and create an earthquake using the force of your body. Everyone gets a free geologic map of California postcard!

title: Indian Arts & Crafts Market
description: Native artisans come from all over California to participate in this event. Enjoy shopping for artwork, baskets, gourds, jewelry, soapstone & elkhorn carvings, drums, and much, much more. Free with museum admission.

title: Cinderella
description:
The classic tale of love, wickedness, and sibling rivalry explodes on the B Street stage in this antic, musical romp. A comedy for children ages 4 and older.

description:
The Fairytale Town Troupers are back with their first show of the season, The Frog Princess. Belazar Jette’ is labeled the “Crown Prince of College Basketball” by sportscasters everywhere. It is chock-full of outlandish episodes, as the two outcasts, fleeing down the Mississippi on a makeshift raft, yield to a current that brings a new view of their society and, finally, themselves.

description:

title: Gene Oldfield and Friends: Cybernetic
description:
During the month of April, Axis Gallery will host an exhibition titled Cybernetic by Gene Oldfield and friends. Oldfield’s show references Norbert Wiener’s Cybernetics: or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine (published in 1948 with a 2nd edition in 1961) which was reviewed as “seminal” in the NY Times. The ideas presented in the book spanned C.P. Snow’s two cultures of the literary and scientific circles (even with advanced mathematical sections!). The Cybernetic show at Axis Gallery will present pieces that show some of these ideas in symbolic and physical form, with the hope of spanning the art and scientific cultures of today.

The language of mathematics is used to advance the math-on-the-walls approach done at Oldfield’s two Pierogi gallery shows in NY. His goal was, and is, to capture beauty in both the hieroglyphic look and the ideas cast by the equations. Some may read these equations and find some poetry. Cybernetic topics: entropy, information theory, feedback, computer lingo, and robotics, are some of the sources of symbols and equations used in the work. The imaginary number i (the square root of negative one), the base of the natural logarithm e » 2.7, along with a triangle (read as “change in”) are also part of the vocabulary used to find some beauty (scope/simplicity?) in mathematics, physics, and cybernetics.

Sensors, motorized gadgets, circuits, displays, video, and computers will be used to construct an installation of kinetic and interactive pieces. David Bliss and Pat Fleming will help with the constructions and also present cyber-pieces. The 2nd Saturday Reception will have some of the electric rides that Oldfield has been building. Perhaps a “jump” of Robocycles will dance on Thursday’s Preview Reception.

Gene Oldfield states: “I have a science and art background with masters in Math and Physics, Robot Navigation PhD dissertation, and teach math at CSUS. I sat in on the “45 to the Present” classes by John Fitzgibbon and Wayne Thiebaud while at school. In the '60s I shot and edited film while working at the Berkeley Rad Lab with a Nobel Prize-winning group. I also worked as a process engineer in Silicon Valley.”

Axis Gallery is a cooperative gallery featuring cutting edge contemporary art from local, national and international artists.

title: Art Studio Trek: Art and Chocolate
description:
Come out to the 5th Anniversary of Art Studio Trek! Enjoy the combined efforts of 19 artists at 13 studio locations in the Roseville, Rocklin, and Granite Bay area. Celebrate this free weekend event and share in the artists’ personal creative endeavors. There will be a vast array of talent, art, and even an opportunity for you, the guest! Visitors will be eligible for door prizes and original art. It will be a time of creative celebration in this artist community as artists demonstrate art techniques and offer their artwork for sale.

Download a map.

title: Free Family Concert Series
description:
The Free Family Concert Series is designed to introduce people of all ages to classical music in a fun, informative, and casual format.

Enjoy an Instrument Petting Zoo with new Activity Funshops, Hands-on workshops where kids "make stuff to take home" are offered by Very Special Arts. Following the activity period is a Family Concert.

title: Space Days
description:
The Discovery Museum Science & Space Center celebrates our 60th Anniversary with a year-long retrospective of science milestones of the last six decades. In April, we celebrate great science of the 1960s.

On July 21, 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed on the moon. We celebrate this space milestone, and future space milestones, with our Space Day activities. Kids launch bottle rockets, create their own “first step” on our simulated moon surface, and learn about living in space in our Astronaut Training Center.

Planetarium shows at 1pm and 3pm are included with admission (ages 4 and above only); live animal shows at Noon and 2pm are for all ages.

title: Between the Buried and Me
description:
Between the Buried and Me is a heavy metal band from Raleigh, North Carolina. They have released five studio albums since 2000, as well as a cover album and a live DVD/CD. Their follow-up to Colors, titled The Great Misdirect, was released in October 2009.

The band's name is derived from a section of lyrics in the Counting Crows song, "Ghost Train."

Also playing:
Job for a Cowboy
Cephalic Carnage
The Ocean

title: Before TV: Zoetropes, Thaumatropes, and Cycloramas
description: Children will explore old fashioned animation techniques utilizing persistence of vision. They will create their own thaumatropes, zoetrope strips, and cyclorama scenes.

title: California Celebration & Arts
description: Come to the Sacramento Zoo for a day of cultural entertainment, art, music, dance, and information from the rich cultural diversity that defines California. Art will be on display and for purchase from local and distinguished artists. Local museums, historical societies, genealogy groups, plus arts and crafts for great family fun all included with regular Sacramento Zoo admission.
address: Land Park Drive and Sutterville Road

title: California Theatre Center: The Ugly Duckling
description:
Enjoy California Theatre Center's adaptation of the classic Hans Christian Andersen tale The Ugly Duckling.

Repeatedly recognized as the top professional theater for young American audiences, California Theatre Center creates quality experiences for youth (grades K-5) and families alike.

Sponsored by AT&T.

title: Public Art Tour: Spring Beyond the City Center: Bradshaw & Beyond
description:
Learn about recently installed public artworks at the Animal Care Center and County Recycling Center.

Tour meets at the entrance to the Animal Care Center.

title: Race for the Cure
description:
In 2011, Komen Sacramento Race for the Cure will be celebrating 15 years of raising awareness and funds for breast cancer and breast health. The Susan G. Komen Race for the Cure Series, the largest series of 5K runs/fitness walks in the world, raises significant funds and awareness for the fight against breast cancer, celebrates breast cancer survivorship, and honors those who have lost their battle with the disease. Since its inception in 1983, the Komen Race for the Cure series has grown from one local Race with 800 participants to a global series of more than 120 Races with more than 1 million people expected to participate in 2011.

The Komen Race for the Cure is a unique event, designed and implemented to promote positive awareness, education, and early detection of breast cancer. It has proved to be an enormously effective way to reach many women and men with the message that breast cancer is not necessarily fatal if mammography and breast self-exam become routine. As well as being a road race for runners, the Komen Race for the Cure is an emotionally charged event that attracts many first timers and recreational runners. The Komen Race for the Cure is an opportunity for thousands of women, men, and their families, running or walking, to spread the breast cancer message within their communities.

Up to 75 percent of the funds raised at the Race remain here in the Komen Sacramento Valley Affiliate to provide breast health research, diagnostics, screening, treatment, services and education for uninsured or underinsured women. The remaining 25 percent goes to fund national research to discover the causes of breast cancer and, ultimately, its cures.

title: Premier Pops Concert: Star Wars Suite
description: The Sacramento Youth Symphony, the area’s most prestigious group of young classical musicians, will perform John Williams’ Star Wars Suite as part of Premier Pops. The Premier Orchestra, under the direction of Maestro Michael Neumann, is composed of over 80 of the area’s most talented high school and college students. Featured works to be performed on this final concert of this season include favorites from stage and screen including music from Oklahoma and Titanic in addition to Star Wars. Please come dressed as your favorite Star Wars Character.

title: East Sac Garden Tour
description:
View spectacular gardens in the Fabulous 40s neighborhood. Enjoy a variety of garden styles with your family and friends on Mother’s Day weekend. This tour is an easy stroll from one garden to the next along the tree lined streets and past the older architecture found in this well established Sacramento neighborhood.

Plan to attend the lovely buffet luncheon, catered by Gönül's J Street Cafe. Shop at the boutique located at David Lubin Elementary School, which offers a wide variety of beautiful items such as things to savor, accoutrements for the garden, and everything in between. All proceeds benefit the David Lubin students.

Garden tours are self-guided and begin from any location. Maps are provided on each ticket and with the program. Boutique is located at David Lubin Elementary School. Luncheon takes place at the Sutter Lawn Tennis Club.

title: A Grand Night for Singing
description: Tony-nominated for best musical, this exhilarating revue takes the best known songs of Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein II and shows how truly timeless and universal their music is. Whether it’s a sultry Andrews Sisters-esque “I’m Gonna Wash That Man Right Out-a My Hair,” a swingin’ “Honeybun,” or a jazzy “Kansas City,” this California Musical Theatre premiere of the Broadway musical will leave no question about how terrifically up to date Rodgers & Hammerstein are. Featuring songs from all 11 R&H musicals from Oklahoma! to The Sound of Music to Cinderella!

title: The Belle of Amherst
description:
A captivating look at the life and words of Emily Dickinson, William Luce's wonderful one woman show offers us a window into the mind of one of America's most intriguing poets. Luce's script makes use of a great deal of Emily Dickinson's poetry, using her words as a portal into this fascinating woman's world. Janis Stevens directs a production that promises to capture the ethereal nature of Luce's celebrated text and of Emily Dickinson herself.

The Belle of Amherst is presented by special arrangement with Samuel French, Inc. Appropriate for middle school age and up. This performance is on the Pollock Stage.

title: Roseville Strawberry Festival
description:
We will celebrate the Strawberry at the Strawberry Festival. We won’t ship in any Strawberries. Local farmers will harvest extra strawberries next year just for us. These are certified organic and local from Placer County and some bordering counties such as Sacramento, El Dorado, Yuba, and Sutter Counties. They will also pre-sell Strawberries to the vendors of the festival to insure all Festival Strawberries are local grown. All Strawberries are sold by the Farmers themselves.

This event takes place at the All American Speedway on the Placer County Fairgrounds.

title: Sacramento Antique Faire
description: 300 vendors from Sacramento, San Francisco, Berkeley, the Central Valley, Chico, Redding, Oregon, Nevada, and beyond set up shop at 21st Street between W & X Streets in Midtown, Sacramento to sell antiques and collectibles of all eras! Furniture, vintage clothing and accessories, architectural items, garden, art, jewelry, textiles, paper, lighting, and collectibles of all kinds are there for the taking. A HUGE treasure hunt! Food and coffee are available. Come join the fun!

title: Mother's Day Brunch
description: Give her time with the whole family. Join the Hyatt Regency for a scrumptious buffet fit for a queen.

title: Paws, Pals, and Putts Golf Tournament
description:
Join the Sacramento SPCA for its 2nd Annual Paws, Pals, and Putts Golf Tournament. Proceeds from the tournament, which is presented by Hank Fisher Properties, will benefit the Sacramento SPCA’s Senior Services program providing services to ensure the continued relationship between Sacramento area seniors and their pets.

Don’t miss this unique opportunity to spend a day golfing on one of the oldest and most renowned golf courses in Sacramento. The Club's 18-hole park-style golf course challenges amateurs and professionals alike. The beautifully renovated golf course features five sets of tees offering a challenge to players of all levels.

Paws, Pals, and Putts will feature an 18-hole golf scramble, lunch, awards dinner, and live auction. The day will also feature an exciting Helicopter Ball Drop. Purchase a ball (or two) and be entered into the exciting Ball Drop drawing--with a guaranteed winner.

title: Sneak Preview of One Second Art Opening
description: This show is a sneak preview of prototype 1/6 the size of upcoming large scale sculpture made up of recycled plastic bottles.

title: Mad Hatter's Tea Party
description:
Don't be late for this very important date with your children. Join the CSD for a special 'unbirthday' celebration with hats, tea, and activities.

Children must be accompanied by a paying adult. Children must be age 3 and up.

title: 2011 JAMMIES
description:
The JAMMIES is a two-day concert series (Night of Contemporary Music and Evening of Classical Music) showcasing some of the finest high school musicians in the Sacramento area.

It's no secret that funding for our public school music programs is in jeopardy. With the current state budget cuts, high school music programs for our children are rapidly declining. In light of this, and to further our commitment to music in our schools, the JAMMIES gives the community an opportunity to experience the extraordinary talent of our young performers and show support for our schools.

The 2011 Jammies will take place:
May 7: Evening of Classical Music at the Mondavi Center - Jackson Hall, UC Davis
May 13: Night of Contemporary Music at the Crest Theatre, Sacramento

The News & Review is pleased to invite student classical & contemporary musicians to participate in the 9th annual Jammies Young Artist competition. The winners will perform during our Evening of Classical Music and the Night of Contemporary Music. To apply, take a look at the Classifieds for more information on Classical Music (Deadline: Feb 21) & Contemporary Music (Deadline: Feb 14).

title: Hands on History: Spring Has Sprung! Fun on the Frontier
description: Everyone needs to have fun. Long before computers and video games, imaginative games and contests helped lift spirits, encourage a sense of community and fun, and brought people together. Pioneer games gave people a chance to get together, helped children develop, and build lasting friendships or lead to courtship and marriage. This day is dedicated to fun and games of skill, such as barrel hoop races, the game of Graces, tug-o’-war, jump rope, even marbles and parlor games. Lots of games and fun toys will be for sale in our trade store. Everyone who plays will win a prize!

title: Fight For Air Walk
tickets: No entry fee; walkers collect pledges and donations
description:
Held in communities across the state, Fight For Air Walk events bring together people who want to improve life, one breath and one step at a time. The Fight For Air Walks are designed as education and community awareness events. By educating the public about how poor air quality impacts their health and the steps or actions they can take to improve air quality, we can help people make the transition to becoming part of the solution.

The Sacramento Fight For Air Walk will take place at Howe Park, in the Meadow Area near the baseball field. Activities include a 3-mile walk, food, music, kid’s events, and the Fight For Air Fair with vendors and educational booths for participants to learn what the American Lung Association (ALA) is doing to impact lung health in our community!

title: Auto 101
description:
This workshop, sponsored by Surf City Garage, is for students ages 14–16 and their adult buddy and includes an audio visual presentation and hands-on demonstrations that focus on the following topics: how cars are made; safety, basic maintenance inside, and out; and simple checks and repairs.

This workshop meets auto-related patch/badge requirements for Boy Scouts (ages 14 and older) and Junior Girl Scouts.

title: Senator Steinberg's 10th Annual Passport to Summer Youth Fair
description: The Passport to Summer Youth Fair is a wonderful event for parents, young adults, and children, as it highlights a wide-range of opportunities for healthy summer and after school activities. We will be featuring programs offered by the local parks and recreation departments, as well as opportunities provided by a number of other community organizations, including the Boys and Girls Clubs, Sacramento Youth Symphony, Crocker Art Museum, Sacramento State Campus, and YMCA. More than 400 organizations have been invited to participate. Learn about the many great summer enrichment programs for children and youth. There will be free medical screenings for children and youth. Enjoy live entertainment, children activities, snacks, and a raffle.

title: Take Steps for Crohn's and Colitis
description:
At more than 100 walk sites across the country--including in Sacramento--thousands of people will gather this spring and summer to join the fight against Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. Together we’ll raise money for crucial research and raise awareness of these painful and unpredictable digestive diseases that afflict millions of people.

After only three years, CCFA’s Take Steps Walk has raised more than $20 million for research and patient service programs. Our goal is even higher in 2011. We’re committed to help transform the lives of those impacted by these diseases to one of a brighter future based on well-funded, cutting-edge scientific research. Join us now--register today and take a step toward a future free from Crohn’s and colitis!

Anyone can participate in Take Steps for Crohn’s & Colitis, including people of all ages and fitness levels. Participants are encouraged to form teams of co-workers, friends, and family to build a united front and raise funds. Thousands of walkers, teams, and sponsors will participate in more than 50 cities throughout the country. In 2011, the Sacramento Take Steps walk is expecting nearly 1,000 walkers!

title: 3 on 3 Improv Tournament
description:
Two, 3-person improv teams, will each get 20 minutes to do an improv show. The audience and guest judges will choose the winner and that team will continue in the tournament. The Ultimate 3 on 3 Champion will win $150!

-May 14: Finals

title: Sail Away: Spring Concert
description: Sacramento Children's Chorus presents their spring concert, Sail Away. The concert will feature all five choirs with music from the Paific Rim and guest dancers with the group Sinag-tala.

title: 2nd Annual Natomas Duck Pluck Festival
description:
The Natomas Duck Pluck Festival is a community wide, fun-filled event to primarily support arts and sports programs in local schools.

There will be over 40 booths, including food vendors, carnival-like games, arts, sports, and education activities, which will serve the interest of all ages and all family members. The culminating event of the day will be the Duck Pluck itself, which gives participants a chance to win $10,000.

$10,000? Yes! The Duck Pluck is a raffle that gives participants a 500 to 1 chance of winning $10,000 cash! Purchase a raffle ticket for $100, get a rubber ducky placed in a swimming pool with no more than 500 other ducks. If your duck is plucked at the end of the day, you win $10,000. There is also a second and third place prize of $2,500 and this year we've added three third place prizes of $1,000.

title: The Baroque Chamber with Judith Linsenberg
description:
World-renowned recorder player Judith Linsenberg joins Sacramento Baroque Soloists to perform selected works for recorder, strings, and continuo.

Performance Listing:
Concerto by Georg Philip Telemann
Concerto in A minor, RV 108 by Antonio Vivaldi
Trio Sonata Op. 1 No. 2 by Arcangelo Corelli
Telemann - Chamber Cantata
Vocal selections of A. Scarlatti

title: Cirque De Soleil: Quidam
description: A young girl fumes; she has already seen everything there is to see, and her world has lost all meaning. Her anger shatters her little world, and she finds herself in the universe of Quidam. She is joined by a joyful companion as well as another character, more mysterious, who will attempt to seduce her with the marvelous, the unsettling, and the terrifying.

title: Pow Wow Days
description: Pow Wow Days is a historic, calendar-packed event complete with a parade down Greenback Lane, a special “Kids Korner” day with fun-filled activities, and a carnival full of rides. Add to that the great carnival food we all love and live entertainment round the clock, and it’s the place to be!

title: Just Between Friends Spring/Summer Sale
description:
Be a part of the Nation’s leading children’s and maternity consignment sales event at the Just Between Friends Spring/Summer Sale. Your budget goes further when you shop our savings extravaganza. You will find baby gear, nursery equipment, riding toys, toys, puzzles, games, books, electronics, children's furniture, cribs, bassinets, exersaucers, bicycles, play gyms, pack n plays, and so much more.

Shop and get unbelievable deals on all you need. Sell your items as a consignor and earn 65%, 70%, or more. Volunteer and shop before the public to get the best deals first! Unsold donated items benefit Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services.

Sunday is our half price sale day! Most items without a star are 50% off! Kids look cute and you save big!

title: Sail Away: Spring Concert
description: Sacramento Children's Chorus presents their spring concert, Sail Away. The concert will feature all five choirs with music from the Paific Rim and guest dancers with the group Sinag-tala.

title: 107.9 The End's EndFest
description: Ke$ha, T-Pain, Far East Movement, and The Ready Set will perform at the 2011 EndFest, presented by 107.9 The End.

title: 2011 Amgen Tour of California
description:
World-Class Professional Cycling Race on the Streets of Sacramento for Stage 2 of the race!

One of the longest stages of the race, Stage 2 has “sprinter” written all over the race route. Starting at the site of the 1960 Winter Olympics and one of the largest ski resorts in the U.S., Squaw Valley, the riders will head north to the town of Truckee and then west past the infamous and rugged Donner’s Pass. At 7,100’, this will be the only KOM of Stage 2. From here it will be a more than 7’000’ of descending to the State’s Capitol (elev. 25’). The route will pass through Nevada City, California (last year’s official Start City) and after working its way west for several miles, the peloton will turn south and head through one of the country’s premier military installations, Beale Air Force Base. From there it will be a fast ride through the suburbs of Sacramento. Entering the circuit just past the finish line in Sacramento, the riders will begin the first of two circuit laps with a finish at the State Capitol building. You can expect the crowds in Sacramento to be some of the largest for the entire race.

Click here for a detailed route map.

There will be a Free Lifestyle Festival  sponsored by MBT footwear at the Capitol in conjunction with the finish.

title: Golf & Guitars: Pro-Am Tournament & Children's Charity Concert
description:
Country superstars like Jack Ingram, Clay Walker, Chuck Wicks, and Jimmy Wayne may be busy with national tours and more, but they're never too busy to help those in need. These country stars can always be counted on to bend their schedule to lend a hand. As such, the Golf & Guitars Celebrity-Am Tournament and Charity Concert--hosted by Jack Ingram--is set at the legendary Alister MacKenzie Golf Course at Haggin Oaks, held in conjunction with KNCI 105.1 FM Hot Country.

This year's event includes a celebrity golf tournament, silent auction, and concert. The event kicks off that morning as tournament participants enjoy a tournament round with a major label country music act or sports celebrity. The evening will continue with the chance to bid on an astounding array of celebrity items and one-of-a-kind event packages. Topping the evening is a performance by all of our artists (nearly 4 hours of music).

What is Golf & Guitars? Golf and Guitars is a celebrity pro-am golf tournament and concert featuring nationally recognized & major label country music artists that raises money for two key children's charities here in Sacramento. Each golfer in the tournament gets to play with one of the celebrities and then gets a seat next to the stage where these artists put on a tremendous concert underneath the beautiful golf course sky. Each artist will play 18 holes with a foursome in this scramble event. It’s one of the rare opportunities to spend several great hours with a great musician in a relaxed atmosphere.

Who gets the money? 100% of the net funds are donated between two non-profit charities. The mission of the Morton Golf Foundation, a 501(c)(3) charity, is to provide golf programs that provide exercise in a healthy outdoor environment, to create a recreational environment that builds lasting personal development, and that seamlessly introduces life’s core values of the great game of golf to the youth, disabled, and underserved communities in the Sacramento region. The Keaton Raphael Memorial, is also a 501(c)(3) charitable organization that supports children with cancer and their families by providing emotional, educational, and financial support, while increasing awareness and funding research toward a cure.

title: Kids Acting Workshop: Wizard of Oz
description:
Study at the Studio offers year-round acting workshops for children and young adults. Our goal is to offer a professional and exciting learning venue for youth who are eager to be involved in live theatre. Programs are designed for beginning students and also those with previous acting experience.

Michael Peters will teach the basics of acting while the class rehearses the original comedy about a group of children attempting to put on The Wizard of Oz.

title: Celebrate Sacramento
description: The inaugural Celebrate Sacramento Festival is a semi-annual celebration hosted by Assemblymember Roger Dickinson. The goal of the festival is to celebrate the rich diversity that makes Sacramento a wonderful place to live. Celebrate Sacramento will feature live musical performances and demonstrations in addition to local cuisine, kids' activities, bounce houses, arts & crafts, and booths representing local businesses and organizations.

title: Farms, Friends, & Fairytales
description: Celebrate agriculture awareness at the fourth annual Farms, Friends, & Fairytales event! Arrive early to watch the twin Babydoll sheep, Lucy & Ethel, get sheared, then watch as a wool spinner spins the wool into thread using an old fashioned spinning wheel. Enjoy agriculture-themed hands-on activities, a mini-farmer's market, and visit with local area farms and organizations to learn more about California's rich agricultural history.

title: Sherlock Holmes: The Final Adventure
description:
Sherlock Holmes: The Final Adventure is a play by Steven Dietz, based on the original 1899 play by William Gillette and Arthur Conan Doyle. Watch Holmes sleuth his way to adventure, peril, and even romance! “The game’s afoot!”

Appropriate for middle school age and up. This performance is on the Main Stage.

title: Glee Live! In Concert!
description:
Calling all Gleeks! The cast of Fox's smash show Glee are returning to concert stages this May for a blockbuster cross country tour

On the heels of blockbuster ratings for the post-Superbowl episode Sunday night, Twentieth Century Fox Television and Glee co-creator Ryan Murphy are pleased to announce that the critically acclaimed Glee Live! In Concert!, starring the television show’s cast, will return to North American concert stages this spring.

The North American engagement of Glee Live! In Concert!, is a unique concert experience once again conceived by Murphy that will include live performances of some of the show’s most memorable musical numbers from seasons one and two including “Empire State of Mind,” “Toxic,“ “My Life Would Suck Without You,” “It’s My Life,” and of course, the show’s anthem, “Don’t Stop Believin’.”

title: Children's Choir Program
description: 4th-6th grade students are invited to participate in a free South Sacramento area community children's choir. The 10-week program concludes with a free public concert May 22. Refreshments will be served at rehearsals. Parents may stay for rehearsals. Directing the choir is local educator & choral director Dr. May Tuan Tucker.

title: 19th Annual Pacific Rim Street Festival
description:
Taking place in Old Sacramento and the Westfield Downtown Plaza, for years the festival has displayed the richness and diversity of many Pacific Rim cultures through cultural programs, entertainment, art and food. The event also enhances the community's knowledge of Asian/Pacific Island cultures in a fun and positive environment.

The street fest is planned and staged by volunteers from more than 15 Asian Pacific community groups. Their goals are to broaden the awareness and understanding of the Asian Pacific heritage, to showcase the many positive contributions to the community at large, and to lend support to cultural endeavors in the form of grants and scholarships. 

Each year we feature an aspect of Asian culture as the theme of the festival. For the year 2010, the theme is 'Spice'.

"We live in a multicultural world. The Asian Pacific Rim is just a small part of such diversity, that we live today. Like the spices and herbs that we put on our food each country takes on a flavor of its own. Many groups of explorers of all ethnicity fought many centuries ago and discovered and traded many spices. Many lives were lost because of the spice wars and trade that they tried to get all for their own. Anywhere from Africa to Arabian traders, each one had their ultimate origin in Southeast Asia." ~Randall Ishida

The program for this event can be downloaded from the website. Please visit the website for more info and a full listing of sponsors.

title: SVCC on the Air!
description: Join Sacramento Valley Concert Choir for SVCC on the Air!--a revival of favorites that drew families 'round their treasured radios in the 1920s, 30s, and 40s. "Swinging on a Star," "Boogie Woogie Bugle Boy," "Get Happy," "It's a Grand Night for Singing," "This Joint Is Jumpin'," "What Is this Thing Called Love?" And more! Followed by audience sing-along and light refreshments.

title: Adult Pottery Workshop
description: Adult Pottery with Dave Wilkerson. This is an adult pottery class to explore new visions, dreams, and ideas while working with clay. Basic and intermediate lessons for sculpture, hand building, and wheel activities. Discussions of artistic ideas, glazing techniques, kiln-firing techniques, along with specific areas of interest to the students are addressed.
venue: Allied Ceramics Art Institute Studios & Gallery

title: UC Davis Film Festival
description:
Presented by the Davis Varsity Theatre, this annual festival features a wide array of student films including animation, comedy, drama, commercials, documentaries, music videos, and other art films.

View videos from previous festivals.

title: Magic Circle Storytime: A Program for Children with Autism
description: This half-hour program will consist of books, music, and sensory activities appropriate for those at the toddler/preschool developmental level. Behaviors and noise are most welcome, and siblings may attend.

title: Fred Garbo Inflatable Theater Co.
description:
Bring the entire family for an afternoon of inflatable vaudeville and sheer pneumatic entertainment. They bounce, they juggle, they mime…in life-sized balloon suits.

The New York Times calls it “Helium light and hilarious.” and “Skillful…joyful…buoyant entertainment!”

title: Usher: OMG Tour
description:
By overwhelming popular demand, multi-platinum recording artist Usher has added a second North American leg to his acclaimed OMG Tour. Presented by AEG Live’s Concerts West and Atlanta Worldwide Touring, the concert will feature Usher’s signature brand of hit-filled R&B-infused pop as well as special guest superstar Akon. The announcement comes hot on the heels of Usher’s triumphant appearance at the 53rd Annual Grammy Awards, where he scored two awards (Best Male R&B Vocal Performance and Best Contemporary R&B Album), and performed an electrifying version of his hit “OMG” alongside protégé Justin Bieber.

Also performing:
Akon

title: Hansel and Gretel
description: Children will love this adaptation of the classic fairytale.

title: Dirty Rotten Scoundrels
description:
The Sacramento Community premiere of Dirty Rotten Scoundrels! Two hilarious con men attempt to "out-con" each other on the French Riveria!

Based on the 1988 film, Dirty Rotten Scoundrels centers on two competing con men living on the French Riviera. At first, the suave and experienced Lawrence Jameson takes the rookie con man, Freddy, under his wing. But soon, Freddy tries to compete directly with Lawrence. The competition comes to a peak when they agree that the first con man to extract $50,000 from the female heiress, Christine Colgate, wins and the other must leave town forever.

This show will be performed with a live orchestra. Director: Bob Baxter. Musical Director: James Lohman. Choregrapher: Darryl Strohl.

title: Sacramento Jazz Festival & Jubilee at the Railroad Museum
description:
The 38th annual Sacramento Jazz Festival takes place throughout Sacramento for four days. The California State Railroad Museum will be open daily during the Festival, with jazz musicians performing inside the Museum and complimentary admission offered to Jazz Festival badge holders.

Special Free Children’s Stage and activity area located just outside Museum (on adjacent “1849 Scene”) during the Jazz Festival, and several event music venues are located in close proximity to the Railroad Museum. Steam-powered Sacramento Southern Railroad excursion trains depart on the hour Sat-Mon (regular ticket prices apply). Jazz musicians perform aboard the trains this weekend as well!

title: Sacramento County Fair
description: The 2011 Sacramento County Fair will celebrate 75 years of Fair Memories and Magic at Cal Expo! Carnival, food, barn animals, music, shopping, and the popular demolition derby will entertain you, your friends, and your family for hours.

title: 38th Annual Sacramento Jazz Festival & Jubilee
description:
Every Memorial Day Weekend since 1974, Old Sacramento and other downtown venues have drawn a horde of jazz fans to the Sacramento Jazz Jubilee, the top jazz festival in the West. Sponsored by the Sacramento Traditional Jazz Society, the event features a lineup that this year includes about 60 bands from all over the USA and Canada.

In 2011, we'll present these bands and more:
-Tom Rigney & Flambeau

-and many more!

title: The Who's Tommy
description: Directed by Granada Artist-in-Residence Mindy Cooper with Music and Lyrics by Pete Townshend and Des McAnuff. This hit musical, winner of five Tony Awards, revolves around a young pinball champion who descends into a catatonic state, then rises to fame and life realizations. It includes the classic rock hits "Pinball Wizard," "Tommy, Can You Hear Me?" and "See Me, Feel Me/Listening to You."
city:
Theatre and Dance Department Main Office
Davis

title: This Means War!: California’s Role in the Spanish-American War
description: History enthusiasts and the community-at-large are invited to tour the California State Capitol Museum to see the exciting and new This Means War!: California’s Role in the Spanish-American War exhibit. title: "Beyond the Locomotive" Award Winning Photographs
description:
As part of a special display, the California State Railroad Museum is proud to showcase award-winning photographs recently given prestigious honors as part of an annual Creative Photography Awards Program competition organized by the Center for Railroad Photography & Art. With a compelling “Beyond the Locomotive” theme, a record-setting 700 photographs were submitted as entries this year by more than 200 photographers around the world.

A first time entrant, Brandon Robert Smith of Norman, Oklahoma, received the Center's 2010 top prize for Creative Photography. A California-based photographer named Steve Crise was also honored in the annual competition, which has international appeal.
Judged by Kimberly Parker, Director of the O. Winston Link Museum in Roanoke, Virginia, the competition this year was extremely competitive due to the sheer number of entries. “Those that combined the human element with the industrial setting called out and yet some of the strongest are those where we feel the peace and tranquility of a tree falling in the forest,” explained Parker. “Does the train make a sound if no one is there to hear it pass? I found my interests drawn to the photos that had more to the story.”

This special photography exhibit will remain on display at the California State Railroad Museum through June 30, 2011, joining the Museum’s regular lineup of permanent and changing exhibitions, along with special events. In addition to being showcased in the special exhibit at the Railroad Museum, the award-winning photographs will be featured in an upcoming issue of Railfan & Railroad magazine.

More information about the competition and the Center for Railroad Photography & Art can be found at www.railphoto-art.org.

title: American Sabor
description:
Latino musicians have had a profound influence on traditional genres of music in the United States, including jazz, R&B, rock ‘n’ roll, and hip-hop. At the same time, their experiences living in the United States triggered the creation of new musical traditions, such as mambo and salsa. “American Sabor: Latinos in U.S. Popular Music,” a traveling exhibition from the Smithsonian, presents the musical contributions of U.S. Latinos from the 1940s to the present, exploring the social history and individual creativity that produced stars like Tito Puente, Ritchie Valens, Celia Cruz, Carlos Santana and Selena.

The exhibition was created by Experience Music Project (EMP) and organized for travel by the Smithsonian Institution Traveling Exhibition Service (SITES). “American Sabor,” its national tour, and related programs are made possible by Ford Motor Company Fund. The exhibition will travel to 13 cities through 2015.

EXHIBITION HIGHLIGHTS

Divided into 5 sections, “American Sabor” explores the influence of Latino musicians in post-World War II America through the lens of major centers of Latino music production—New York, San Antonio, San Francisco, Miami and Los Angeles.

Based on the 5,000 square foot exhibition of the same name created by EMP in partnership with the University of Washington, “American Sabor: Latinos in U.S. Popular Music” is a 2,500 square foot experience designed for smaller museums and cultural centers

Two films made specifically for the exhibition bring Latino music and dance to life. Each short film features performance footage and filmed interviews with artists and experts, and the narratives examine key events in the history of post-World War II Latino music. The Palladium Ballroom tells the story of New York’s mythic 1950s dance hall, and the worldwide mambo craze created by the club’s performing stars, like Tito Puente and Tito Rodriguez. A second film, also called American Sabor, features exclusive, highly illuminating interviews with stars of the Latin music scene, including salsa legends Johnny Pacheco and Willie Colón, virtuoso guitarist Carlos Santana, pop icon Herb Alpert, and the musicians who created San Antonio’s famed Westside Sound.

Guided listening stations allow visitors to listen closely to key artists and genres—from salsa and Santana to San Antonio rhythm and blues. Expert commentary identifies elements such as ethnic roots, rhythmic patterns, form, texture, instruments, vocal style, and lyrics.

The exhibition comes with a fully operational juke box so that visitors can dance to their favorite rhythms.

description: Boys and girls in the 5th-9th grade and their adult buddy can find out in this 3 hour hands-on class. Kids get to take apart a Briggs and Stratton one cylinder engine and learn how solids, liquids, and gasses interact to make it run. Then fire up a variety of engines to see how each gets their specific job done. There is no driving or riding involved, and you won’t get greasy (although we do promise lots of noise and smoke).

title: Hot Summer Nights Concert Series
description:
Bring your family out to these free musical events. Bring a blanket or low lawn chair and enjoy live music in the beautiful outdoor amphitheater.

Concert schedule:
August 5: Road 88 (New Country)
August 12: Mother Mayhem (Northern CA Dance Band)
August 19: Pan Extasy (Reggae)
August 26: Solsa (Sizzling Latin and R&B)

title: Screen on the Green Movie Series: Toy Story
description:
Come join us for a free movie and family fun at the Screen on the Green movie series, featuring Toy Story (Rated G).

"Woody," a drawstring cowboy doll (Tom Hanks), is jealous of new-toy-in-town, spaceman action figure "Buzz Lightyear" (Tim Allen) in this computer-generated fantasy of an eclectic assortment of toys and their comical misadventures. Woody and Buzz must ban together to survive when they find themselves in the outside world in the first ever feature-length computer animated film.

title: Farmers' Market
description:
Make the market your Wednesday night destination all summer long to shop, dine, and play. Buy fresh, California-grown produce at Elk Grove's certified farmers' market. 1st Wednesdays include the Economic Stimulus Sale Swap Meet.

Vendor spaces, sponsorship opportunities, and produce selling spots available.

title: History Live
description: A vibrant interactive historical experience; meet the pioneers who left their homes and braved the journey to Sutter’s Fort at the dawn of California’s Gold Rush. Hands on activities with docents in period clothes, meet and talk to those who made California what it is today.

title: Sacramento Antique Faire
description: 300 vendors from Sacramento, San Francisco, Berkeley, the Central Valley, Chico, Redding, Oregon, Nevada, and beyond set up shop at 21st Street between W & X Streets in Midtown, Sacramento to sell antiques and collectibles of all eras! Furniture, vintage clothing and accessories, architectural items, garden, art, jewelry, textiles, paper, lighting, and collectibles of all kinds are there for the taking. A HUGE treasure hunt! Food and coffee are available. Come join the fun!

title: Women's Empowerment's 10th Anniversary Celebration of Independence Gala
description: Community members are invited to the 10th Anniversary Celebration of Independence Gala that benefits Women’s Empowerment, a local nonprofit helping homeless women find homes and jobs so they can support their families. The event, which honors the group’s most recent graduates, will feature a formal dinner, live and silent auctions, live music, and presentations from the graduates and local community leaders.

title: Native American Day
description: This annual event, sponsored by the State Native American Liaisons of California, is held on the grounds of the State Capitol. Speakers include California Indian leaders. Music and dancers are on hand to honor the spirit and contributions of the State’s indigenous people.

title: Excursion Train Rides
description:
The first weekend in April marks the opening weekend for the 28th operating season of the Railroad Museum’s excursion train service on the Sacramento Southern Railroad! Beginning this weekend, and continuing every weekend through September, experience the sights, smells, and sounds of a real, working steam locomotive as your train rolls along the levees of the Sacramento River.

Excursion trains depart on-the-hour from the Central Pacific Freight Depot in Old Sacramento near Front and K Streets. Climb aboard for a relaxing 40-minute six-mile roundtrip route atop the levees of the Sacramento River in the vintage passenger coaches and converted freight cars. Or upgrade to First Class service on the El Dorado where you will enjoy being treated as a VIP aboard this beautifully restored 1920s lounge-observation car, which offers large picture windows, plush seating, and air conditioning!

title: Sing Along with Mister Cooper
description:
Sing and learn with Mister Cooper for 30 minutes of pure entertainment, on the last Tuesday of every month from April through September! For children ages 3 to 7 and their families.

NOTE: Because this program begins before the library's open hours, please enter the library through the community room door, far left of the main entrance.

title: Urban Cow Half Marathon
description: The Urban Cow Half Marathon, Half Marathon Relay, and 5K Fun Run & Walk will begin at the northeast corner of William Land Park, across from Sacramento City College. The Half Marathon is limited to the first 4,200, the 5k Run/Walk is limited to 1,400, and the Half Marathon Relay is limited to 150 teams. The loop course is flat, fast, and very scenic.

title: Sacramento Antique Faire
description: 300 vendors from Sacramento, San Francisco, Berkeley, the Central Valley, Chico, Redding, Oregon, Nevada, and beyond set up shop at 21st Street between W & X Streets in Midtown, Sacramento to sell antiques and collectibles of all eras! Furniture, vintage clothing and accessories, architectural items, garden, art, jewelry, textiles, paper, lighting, and collectibles of all kinds are there for the taking. A HUGE treasure hunt! Food and coffee are available. Come join the fun!

title: Acorn Day
description: Join us for an educational and fun-filled day for the entire family! Observe the time-honored tradition of preparing acorn for food and learn Native arts & crafts-making. Sample Native foods, and spend the afternoon helping us celebrate the acorn harvest season!

title: The Mansion After Dark
description: Visitors can see the Governor’s Mansion State Historic Park in a whole new light--“Lights Out.” Following in the tradition of many of the families that lived in the mansion, the volunteers at the Governor’s Mansion are using contemporary decorations to make the home ready for the Halloween event. These unique open-house style tours will feature tales of ghosts, bats, great pumpkins, coffin corners and Halloween adventures in the decorated darkened rooms of the mansion. Storytellers will captivate visitors with tales of the season; fortune tellers will predict interesting futures.

title: The Haunted Fort
description: Sutter’s Fort, once a portal for weary pioneers, again serves as the gateway to their restless spirits, who return to tell the tales of their lives and melancholy deaths at this special family friendly event.

title: Spookomotive Train Rides
description: Halloween-themed “Spookomotive” trains decorated for the season depart on-the-hour from the Central Pacific Railroad Freight Depot in Old Sacramento. Join our “skeleton crew” for a fun and delightful (but not frightful) 40-minute ride along the Sacramento River!

title: Boo at the Zoo
description:
Two nights of ghoulish family fun, rain or shine. Kids can safely trick-or-treat around the lake at 17 different candy stations! Other activities include magic shows, costume dance party, ghoulish crafts, and lots of family fun. You can also ride the Spooky Train or Creepy Carousel for an additional fee.

Please note: Only the front half of the Zoo will be open during this event. The spookiness is appropriate for children under 10 years of age.
address: Land Park Drive and Sutterville Road

title: Convoy of Hope
description:
The Sacramento Convoy of Hope is a collaborative effort between dozens of local churches, businesses, social service organizations, local government, and Convoy of Hope, Inc. a 501(c)(3) non-profit humanitarian organization, serving in the United States and around the world, providing food for the hungry and relief for people in crisis.

The outreach will provide people with a tangible message of hope, free groceries, lunch, haircuts, medical, dental, prescription glasses, family potraits, kids' carnival, crafts, live music, clothing, job fair, and lots more. All goods and services are provided to guests free of charge. There is free parking as well.

title: Military Family Day
tickets: 50% off Zoo Admission for military personnel, veterans, and their families.
description: In appreciation for our troops, all military personnel, veterans, and their families receive a 50% discount with a valid military identification card.
address: Land Park Drive and Sutterville Road

title: Sacramento Antique Faire
description: 300 vendors from Sacramento, San Francisco, Berkeley, the Central Valley, Chico, Redding, Oregon, Nevada, and beyond set up shop at 21st Street between W & X Streets in Midtown, Sacramento to sell antiques and collectibles of all eras! Furniture, vintage clothing and accessories, architectural items, garden, art, jewelry, textiles, paper, lighting, and collectibles of all kinds are there for the taking. A HUGE treasure hunt! Food and coffee are available. Come join the fun!

title: Harvest Festival Original Art & Craft Show
description: A family destination, the Harvest Festival showcases unique handmade products by American artists and crafters. Harvest Festival Original Art and Craft Show is the largest indoor arts and crafts show on the West Coast. Attendees can meet and buy directly from top artisans, enjoy entertainment, and satisfy their taste buds with delicious festival cuisine.

title: Small Train Holiday
description: Get into the spirit of the season when the California State Railroad Museum presents a “Small Train Holiday." Visitors will be dazzled by roving musical entertainment, fun interpretive handcar rides, amazing scale and model toy train display, story time with Mrs. Claus, and much more – all happening inside the Museum!

title: Hands on History: Candle Light Tours
description: Darkness lends mystery to the Fort, a romantic aura that disguises the harsh reality of pioneer life. Candlelit tours offer glimpses into the private lives of those who uprooted their families for a better life in early California. A behind the scenes look at the real faces of those who saw opportunity or possible devastation in their new homes, husbands debating with wives, mothers reassuring their children, tradesmen negotiating business, all surrounded by the night which allows us to truly travel back in time.

title: Old Sacramento Underground Tours
description:
Hidden beneath the city for nearly 150 years, Old Sacramento’s underground has long been the capital’s best-kept secret. Today, you can join thousands of residents and visitors in uncovering the facts behind the legends that lie below our buildings and sidewalks. Explore excavated foundations and enclosed pathways while your tour guide recounts the tales of the devastation, perseverance, and determination that led to California’s only successful street-raising project.

For these hour-long guided walking tours, check in at the Sacramento History Museum before descending below several historic Old Sacramento buildings. Be prepared to walk in areas with uneven surfaces and low ceilings and get ready to learn and have fun all along the way! Due to the popularity of the tours, advance tickets are recommended.

title: Fundamentals of Drawing
description: Learn to Draw!

title: Hands on History: A Simple Emigrant Christmas
description: Join us at Sutter’s Fort to recreate Christmas traditions and customs from many lands. In John Sutter’s day, people from around the world passed through the gates, each with their own customs and traditions for the holiday season. “A Simple Emigrant Christmas” presents several vignettes showing holiday scenes, including foods, music, decorations, and traditions from other cultures. Visitors will be able to dip candles, make cornhusk dolls, create Christmas ornaments, and decorate a tree, creating a new holiday tradition for the family.

title: Christmas Memories
description: Christmas at the Governor’s Mansion was a memorable event for many of California’s first families in years past. Visit the Governor’s Mansion State Historic Park to celebrate “Christmas Memories” with lavishly recreated period décor and costumed docents. An impressive array of live music that changes hourly will entertain the whole family while storytellers captivate imaginations young and old. Let yourself be transported back to the time of the earlier Governors’ families and their Christmas traditions…a very special time of year. Mr. and Mrs. Claus will visit the Mansion and meet with the little ones on both Saturdays.

title: Holiday Magic
description: Why should only humans receive gifts during the holidays? It’s time for Holiday Magic—watch as the animals unwrap their holiday goodies! Please bring a new, unwrapped toy for Toys for Tots, and receive $1 off your Sacramento Zoo admission.
address: Land Park Drive and Sutterville Road

title: Sacramento Antique Faire
description: 300 vendors from Sacramento, San Francisco, Berkeley, the Central Valley, Chico, Redding, Oregon, Nevada, and beyond set up shop at 21st Street between W & X Streets in Midtown, Sacramento to sell antiques and collectibles of all eras! Furniture, vintage clothing and accessories, architectural items, garden, art, jewelry, textiles, paper, lighting, and collectibles of all kinds are there for the taking. A HUGE treasure hunt! Food and coffee are available. Come join the fun!

title: Sacramento Saturday Market
description:
Sacramento Saturday Market is an outdoor, year-round arts & crafts market, held on the 1st & 3rd Saturday of the month. The market offers customers opportunities to meet local artists throughout Northern California and see their one-of-a-kind-pieces, as well as pick up fresh produce from local farmers. A Kids Zone offers face painting, bounce house, and arts & crafts for younger fans. A small section of the market is set aside for vendors selling gently used items (Yard Sale). Live music will be provided by local bands.

The market is located in Parking Lot E at Cal Expo (corners of Ethan & Exposition Blvd).

title: The Asylum: Goth Club
description:
The Asylum, located inside Barcode Nightclub, has been providing Sacramento with the best cutting edge Goth/Industrial/Nu-DarkWave/EBM Dance music for over 12 years. It features resident DJ Bryan Hawk and special guests. Some bands that have partied at the Asylum include: Depeche Mode, Ogher (Skinny Puppy), Hate Department, Leather Strip, and KMFDM.

Asylum is the only 18 and over goth club with two full bars, huge dance floor, outside smoking patio, and the largest state-of-the-art sound system in the area.

title: Walking Tour: The Art of Terra Cotta: An Architecture Tour featuring Gladding McBean
description:
This tour will discuss the history of terra cotta as an architectural art form and will highlight downtown's best examples of this turn-of-the-century technique. This tour emphasizes the contribution of the Gladding McBean studio, one of the region’s best cultural and artistic assets, which has provided terra cotta tiles, pipes, and sculpture for customers worldwide. Based in Lincoln, California, this studio has been in continual operation since 1874, with many downtown buildings showcasing the studio’s early works. This tour will highlight these structures as well as discuss the evolution of this notable clay studio, the process of working with this unique type of clay and the studio’s legacy on the art of terra cotta. Mike Munson leads this tour.

The tour starts from Cesar Chavez Plaza at 9th & J Streets.

title: Improv 1 Class (Continuous)
description:
The Improv 1 class is perfect for people who want to perform at the Comedy Spot and for those people who just want to have fun each week. You will learn all the improv basics: how to find the game of the scene, how to establish a solid foundation, how to accept and build on other players ideas, and be encourage to play at the top of your intelligence!

This style of improv is taught in New York, Chicago, and Los Angeles and is style that many top comedians studied before being on television and in movies. Comedians including: Tina Fey, Amy Poehler, Paul Rust, Aziz Ansari, Paul Scheer, Will Ferrell, Matt Besser, and former Sacramento Comedy Spot cast members performing in Los Angeles including Jeff Sloniker, Toni Ramos, and Betsy Sodaro.

Instructor: Brian Crall

title: Thursday Night Blues Jam
description: Come on down for killer blues in Old Sac’s best kept secret--Vega’s Nightclub & Sports Bar--and enjoy a blues jam open to all jammers. This jam is supported by the Sacramento Blues Society. Come on down and have a blast!

title: Walking Tour: Yesterday, Today, & Tomorrow: K Street Commerce, Growth, and Redevelopment
description:
Beginning in Old Sacramento at Front and K streets, this tour will trace Sacramento’s commercial growth by traveling on foot toward 13th & K. On this walk, see Sacramento’s first commercial district, learn about K Street’s early history as a vaudeville and entertainment hotspot, and be the first to hear future plans for Sacramento’s most talked-about pedestrian mall. Shawn Peter or Mike Munson will lead this tour.

The tour begins in front of the Delta King Riverboat at Front & K Streets.

title: Walking Tour: Structural Stories: Local Examples of Historical Architecture Styles
description:
Stroll through the ages of architectural history right here in Downtown Sacramento. From our Renaissance-style Cathedral of the Blessed Sacrament and the graceful Art Deco shapes of Crest Theatre to Chicago style architecture here in California, we will show you local examples of the world’s finest styles. Shawn Peter leads this tour.

Tour begins from Cesar Chavez Plaza at 9th & J Streets.

title: Walking Tour: Art is All Around Us: A Tour of Sacramento’s Collection of Art in Public Places
description:
Tour Sacramento’s impressive collection of permanently sited works of art integrated into Sacramento’s built and natural environments. See local works by notable local and regional artists. This tour was developed in partnership with Sacramento Metropolitan Arts Commission’s Art in Public Places program. Richard MacGill leads this tour.

Tour starts at the Indo Arch outside of Downtown Plaza at 3rd & K streets.

title: Walking Tour: Tales of the Central City: An Overview of Early Sacramento History
description:
Walk with us down memory lane on a guided tour of one of the oldest cities in California. Learn how Sacramento wrangled the distinction of California’s State Capitol, walk the original route of the famed Pony Express, see the influence of railroad’s "Big Four" on early urban planning and learn why downtown sidewalks are hollow. DSP's Gold Rush era specialist, Mike Munson leads this tour.

Tour begins from Cesar Chavez Plaza at 9th & J Streets.

title: Walking Tour: Kids Meet the City: A Tour of California History Especially for Kids
description:
This tour is specially designed to serve as a fun and interactive way to introduce local history to students of all ages. This unique walk through downtown will explore the Gold Rush, the history and route of the famed Pony Express, John Sutter’s place in California history, and the Big Four of the railroad industry as well as offer an introduction to city government with a visit into City Council Chambers.

Make the most out of your tour with DSP's new Kids Meet The City: Activity Book. Download your free guide here!

Tour begins from the steps of City Hall.

title: Minerva Project Quilts
description:
The quilts are the result of an innovative art program at the Alameda County Juvenile Justice Center established by the Alameda County Board of Supervisors. The quilt project was inspired by First Lady Maria Shriver. Teenage girls detained at the center created their own interpretations of Minerva, the image on the California state seal and the namesake of the Minerva Awards.

The artwork focuses on the Roman goddess’ qualities of courage, strength, and wisdom, and the project encouraged the teens to think about these traits in themselves when creating their quilts. The Minerva Quilts is an example of the potential for arts programs to help young people find the courage, strength, and wisdom to make positive changes in their lives, and to be leaders in their families and communities.

"I believe that each woman is the artist of her own life. My hope is that young girls will be inspired by the Minerva Quilts to develop qualities they wish to see in themselves," First Lady Shriver said.

title: California Canines: Dogs with Jobs
description:
Most of us know dogs best as pets and companions, but for thousands of years dogs have helped people with daily tasks such as herding livestock, hunting for food, or hauling loads. More recently, dogs have been used to help people with disabilities, to assist
in search and rescue missions, and to protect the public in partnership with military and law enforcement units. Some dogs even do unconventional jobs like helping scientists track endangered species, locating ancient burial grounds, or alerting wine grape growers to insect infestations in the vines.

California has been a leader in developing specialized dog training and California dogs have served in many capacities around the nation and the world. Meet a few of them in this exhibit!

title: 1st Saturday African-American Art Tours
description:
The Sacramento African-American Art Collective (SAAAC) hosts and promotes a monthly self-guided tour every 1st Saturday, highlighting the works of Sacramento and Northern California’s African-American artists. These tours showcase the ethnic diversity of Sacramento’s entrepreneurial community, making 1st Saturday a destination and cultural bridge point for the Sacramento art enthusiast community.

SAAAC 1st Saturday venues host established and emerging African-American artists. Art lovers will see creative works in all mediums priced from the affordable to the extravagant. Participating artists are predominantly from Sacramento and surrounding communities, showcasing the wealth of regional African-American talent. People of all ages can enjoy this family-friendly and community event.

Each participating venue will take turns hosting a “Point of Destination.” The Point of Destination is where the participating venues meet up with the artists and welcome the community for a closing reception after each monthly tour.

Participating venues: Carol’s Books, Celebration Arts, Brickhouse Gallery, Kuumba Collective Art Gallery, Evolve the Gallery, Framed by Frankie, Jazzyblues Café, Master Barber and Beauty Shop, Sojourner Truth Multicultural Museum, Studio 14: Ed Nightingale, Studio 33: Kevin Hellon, 40 Acres Art Gallery, and Underground Books.

Point of Destination Locations:
February: The Inaugural 1st Saturday Gala “Point of Destination” will be held at Master Barber & Beauty Shop, featuring Sacramento’s own Garrett Perkins Project and artist Gerry ‘GOS’ Simpson. This event will begin at 9pm and will coincide with the celebration of Black History Month.
April (See complete event listing): 40 Acres Art Gallery, beginning at 6:30pm. Seating is limited and guests are encouraged to arrive early. Fine artist and cultural activist, Milton “510” Bowens presents Food Stamps, Free Lunch, and Fine Art: A Self Portrait. Join us as we artistically flash back to the sixties, seventies, and eighties in a celebration of music, poetry, and memory. A live DJ will spin old school hits and a select ensemble of the Sacramento area’s finest spoken word artist will perform. The evening will include a silent auction with proceeds benefiting Mr. Bowens’ Civil Arts Project.

title: Food & Toy Drive
description:
During the holiday season bring a non-perishable food item or a new and unwrapped toy when you visit the Zoo and receive $1 off your Zoo admission!

All food donations will be given to the Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services. All toy donations will be given to Toys for Tots.
address: Land Park Drive and Sutterville Road

title: Downtown Sacramento Walking Tours
times: Varies *Tours last approximately one hour each
description:
These unique tours through downtown Sacramento introduce visitors to the people, places and events that shaped California history. From John Sutter to Cesar Chavez, these tours cover more than 150 years of state and local history. Topics range from art and architecture to cultural, religious, and urban history.

Tours include:
-Locally Grown, Internationally Known: The History of Sacramento’s Music Scene
-Tales of the Central City: An Overview of Early Sacramento History
-Structural Stories: Local Examples of Historical Architecture Styles
-Art is All Around Us: A Tour of Sacramento’s Collection of Art in Public Places
-Yesterday, Today, & Tomorrow: K Street Commerce, Growth, and Redevelopment
-The Art of Terra Cotta: An Architecture Tour featuring Local Clay Artisans Gladding McBean
-Kids Meet the City: A Tour of California History Especially for Kids

title: Film Frame: Visual Acoustics: The Modernism of Julius Shulman
description: This film celebrates the life and career of Julius Shulman, whose photographs brought modern architecture and progressive architects into American mainstream. Director Eric Bricker will introduce the film and lead a post-screening discussion. Presented in collaboration with SacMod and AIA Central Valley.

title: Lunch & Learn
description: Join us for an in-depth 30-minute talk about one or two works of art on view. This discussion will focus on John Buck. Participants are encouraged to enjoy lunch at the Crocker Cafe before or after the talk. Free with Museum admission.

title: Art Appetizer
description:
On 2nd Saturday, start your evening at the Crocker with a tour of the Museum’s most recent exhibitions. Never the same tour twice, Art Appetizer is a 50-minute experience designed to fulfill your art cravings.

Free with Museum admission.

title: The Vase and Beyond: The Sidney Swidler Collection of Ceramics
description: Given to the Crocker in its entirety, the Sidney Swidler Collection of 20th-century studio ceramics features some 800 vessels by 300 international artists. Ranging from minute to monumental, the collection showcases the wide-ranging, innovative practice of contemporary ceramic artists with a gorgeous array of forms, techniques and glazes. The Swidler Collection proves that even a functional form like the vessel can defy expectations.

title: Meet the Author: Peter Stekel
description:
In October 2005, two mountaineers climbing above Mendel Glacier in the High Sierra find the mummified remains of a man in a WWII uniform, entombed in the ice. The "Frozen Airman" discovery created a media storm which drew author Peter Stekel to investigate and stumble upon the case of a navigation training flight crew missing since 1942. Early attempts at recovery were thwarted due to empty graves, botched records, bad weather, bad luck, and bad timing. Then, in 2007, Stekel himself discovered a second body in the glacier.

Through meticulous research, interviews, and his own mountaineering trips to the site, Stekel uncovered the identities of these four young men. Final Flight explores the story of the ill-fated flight and the misinformation surrounding it for over 60 years. The book is a gripping account that's part mystery, part history, and a personal quest to uncover the truth of the events that occurred on November 18, 1942. In the process, Stekel rewrites the young aviators' last days and takes us on their final flight.

Event is free with museum admission.

title: Classical Concert: William Feasley
description: Inspired by John Buck: Iconography, classical guitarist William Feasley will perform works by American composers Peter Madlem, Robert Beaser, Carlos Jobim, and Thelonius Monk along with the world premiere of “Black Tango” (“Tango Negro”) by the Argentine composer Marcelo Ferraris.

title: Art Mix: Lit Fix
description:
Celebrate Literary Arts Month with a night full of poetry, spoken word, live music, tours, and talks. Don’t miss an open mic session and interactive activities.

Free with Museum admission. Art Mix is part of the program series Thursdays ‘til 9. Sponsored by Bank of America.

title: The Ultra Sensory Tour
description:
Listen to rich descriptions, smell spices, and touch different fabrics during a multi-sensory tour of the Museum’s permanent collection. This program is recommended for visitors who are blind or partially sighted.

Free with Museum admission.

title: Slow Art 2011
description:
Slow Art is a global grassroots arts celebration designed to encourage visitors to slow down and spend quality time looking at artwork, contemplating its subject, material, and technique. This session will focus on three artworks in the Museum’s permanent collection. Immediately following, participants will continue the conversation over lunch at the Crocker Cafe.

Reservations are required. Free with Museum admission.

title: Mudcloth Madness
description:
Organized by the Kuumba Collective Art Gallery this exhibition explores how mud cloth, a hand-woven and hand-dyed textile, developed by the Bande people of Mali, West Africa has inspired local artists in an array of mediums and offers a contemporary twist on a traditional symbol of African culture.

This exhibit is part of the Student & Community Exhibition Galleries.

title: Mudcloth Madness Closing Reception
description:
The artists featured in Mud Cloth Madness come together for a final celebration of this very special exhibition.

Free with Museum admission.

title: Lunch & Learn
description: Join us for an in-depth 30-minute talk about one or two works of art on view. This discussion will focus on Daniel Douke's "Widescreen" (Contemporary American). Participants are encouraged to enjoy lunch at the Crocker Cafe before or after the talk. Free with Museum admission.

title: Educator Evening: Art Workshop for Teachers
description: The Crocker’s teaching artist will guide teachers through a unique art workshop that can be duplicated in the classroom.

title: Playlist: The Rants & Raves of a Broadway Diva
description:
Broadway star and Tony Award nominee Brenda Braxton–who has played the role of Velma Kelly in Chicago on Broadway–shares the ups and downs and hilarious trials of a Broadway actress through stories and music in a special one-night performance.

Playlist is part of the program series Thursdays ‘til 9. Sponsored by Bank of America.

title: 1906 Earthquake Living History Program
description:
Step back in time at the California State Capitol Museum and witness volunteers and staff of the Capitol Museum costumed in the attire of the period re-enacting scenes in response to one of America’s greatest disasters–the 1906 San Francisco Earthquake and Fire.

Meet Governor George Pardee as he receives a telegram from President Theodore Roosevelt offering $1 million for disaster relief. Attorney General Ulysses S. Webb, Secretary of State Charles Curry, and Treasurer Truman Reeves will be on hand to help the refugees, some of whom camped out on the Capitol grounds and at Sutter’s Fort. Meet the women of Sacramento who assisted the San Francisco families to obtain meal tickets, clothing, and blankets.

This glimpse into turn-of-the-20th-century California history is free for everyone.

title: Gottfried Helnwein: Inferno of the Innocents
description: Like a modern-day Goya, Gottfried Helnwein’s art addresses themes of inhumanity, violence and the virtue of personal expression. Over more than four decades, the artist has pursued a singular, radical vision realized in monumental paintings and photographs. With stark and probing psychological intensity, he critiques not only the past, but present-day veneers, jolting us from the comfort of complacency. Such confrontations are informed by his upbringing in post-war Vienna, Austria—an experience that fueled the artist’s passion for truth and tolerance. Today, Helnwein immerses himself in our ever-changing cultural landscape, working from his studio in Los Angeles.

title: Open Art: Artists & The Environment
description:
Impressionists became renowned for their plein air paintings of outdoor landscapes. Get ready for the launch of the “Summer of Impressionism” and explore how contemporary artists working in various media incorporate the environment in their work to create a sense of place and history. Artists Enid Baxter Blader and Ned Kahn will participate in a panel discussion moderated by Shelly Willis, Manager of the Sacramento Metropolitan Arts Commission’s Art in Public Places Program.

This program is presented in collaboration with Sacramento Metropolitan Art Commission. Open Art is a part of the program series Thursdays ‘til 9. Sponsored by Bank of America. Free with Museum admission.

title: 9th Annual Celebrity Chef Challenge
description:
