Paul has also been featured in The Daily Show segment "Second Opinion," in which he skewered the medical profession playing an HMO representative with a less than sympathetic mindset.

title: Ron Hacker
description: Ron Hacker has played every major festival in Northern California, including the Monterey Jazz Festival, the San Francisco Blues Festival, and the Marin County Blues Festival. He has also toured extensively in Europe playing major festivals in Belgium, Holland, Denmark, and Norway.

title: O Street Dub
description:
O Street Dub, named for O Street in Kingston Jamaica, is a Sacramento-based band that lays down soulful, funky instrumental reggae and rocksteady. Working with vocalists to perform both B sides and standards of the Jamaican musical tradition, O Street is sure to get you moving your feet!

Also performing:
Whiskey Avengers

title: N'Dambi
description: N’dambi became especially enamored with the male singers from the '70s and '80s she'd heard and identified with while hanging out with cousins and friends. The funky soul of Bar-Kays' Larry Dodson, the sophisticated syncopation of Earth, Wind & Fire's Maurice White, and the notorious abandon of the Ohio Players' Sugafoot influenced her heavily. Later, the mysterious, uninhibited imagination of Nina Simone and Mahalia Jackson also became musical and cultural touchstones.

title: West of Next
description:
West of Next plays bold, original music inspired by the classic American regional genres. Western swing, Cajun and zydeco, mambos, rumbas, waltzes, blues, Celtic and Appalachian strains, honky tonk, rock, and more all arranged in a daring style coming from a jazz musician’s point of view. Celtic dance tunes and ancient ballads became old time string bands which became bluegrass incorporating jazz-like improvisation and church harmony. Marching bands became early jazz which became swing which became bop. Country and early jazz became western swing. Cajun and blues became zydeco. Country and blues became rock and roll. Gospel mixed with the blues point of view became R& B.

Also performing:
Jay Shaner

title: Young Frankenstein
description:
The classic Mel Brooks movie is ALIVE...and it's headed here! You'll have a monstrously good time at this spectacular new production, winner of the 2008 Outer Critics Circle Award and the Broadway.com Audience Award for best musical! Don't miss the sensational cast delivering all your favorite moments from the classic film, plus brand-new show-stopping numbers for the stage, including "Transylvania Mania," "He Vas My Boyfriend" and “Puttin' on the Ritz."

This wickedly inspired re-imagining of the Frankenstein legend follows bright young Dr. Frankenstein (that's Fronkensteen) as he attempts to create a monster--but not without scary and hilarious complications. The brains behind the laughter is mad genius and three-time Tony winner Mel Brooks himself--who wrote the music and lyrics and co-wrote the book--along with his record-breaking team from The Producers: five-time Tony-winning director and choreographer Susan Stroman and three-time Tony-winning writer, Thomas Meehan.

title: The Edge Performance Festival
description:
This exciting new festival includes Main Stage Dance; a Cabaret featuring graduate and undergraduate students in an evening of music, poetry, and more; stagings of new Undergraduate One Acts; Solo Explorations by graduating MFA acting candidates; and sing-along late night showings of the The Rocky Horror Picture Show movie.

Performances occur in various UC Davis locations including Main Theatre, Arena Theatre, Wyatt Pavilion Theatre.

Davis

title: Chris Karney featuring Justin Worsham
description:
Chris Karney began entertaining the USA when he competed in the first X Games of 1995. Corn-fed and Mother-loved since the bicentennial of our great nation, Karney is a true AmeriCan. Coming from a small Iowa town of 400, young Christopher left home at the tender age of fourteen to join the Mountain Dew Freeflite Bicycle Team. Today Chris Karney draws crowds larger than 400 for his one man show at San Francisco’s Pier 39 Center Stage.

Comedian, Magician, Bike Trickster, Smoker, Escape Artist, and all around Nice Guy, Karney maneuvers his multi-considerable talents into exciting and engaging performances. Before and after a show Christopher is often entertaining guests with card tricks and coin manipulation. His audiences find themselves tickled with laughter as they reach for and secure their wallets and purses.

title: Easter Sunday School at Movies on a Big Screen
description: Break away from your Easter festivities and come to MOBS for a very "special" night! Vintage Christian scare films! Creepy Christian kids shows! Lots of religious video strangeness! We're not giving away too much of what will be included right now, as we're still sorting through hours and hours and hours of this stuff. Please note: quality will vary (much of it will be from tape sources).

title: Happy Hour Blues Jam
description: Come out to Torch Club, the most popular Blues Club in Sacramento, for a Happy Hour Blues Jam on Sundays.

title: Tess Sell
description: Enjoy a performance by Tess Sell.

title: Hugo with Special Guest Damato
description: There’s an aura of late night heat and mystery in the music of Hugo. For him, Old Tyme Religion isn’t just another album title--it’s an apt summation of a certain conviction that continuously embeds itself in his story, and in his songs. His real life experiences have taken him from the Mekong River jungle to the booth of a favorite Thai restaurant in the Hell’s Kitchen neighborhood he has made home.

title: Open Mic Night
description: The oldest open mic in the Sacramento area has featured many of Sacramento's best musical artists.

title: Acoustic Open Mic with Sandra Delores and Friends
description: Enjoy an evening of Acoustic Open Mic with Sandra Delores and Friends.

title: Grimey Tuesday with Mimosa
description:
Grimey Tuesday is a dubstep & bass night featuring residents DJ Whores, Crescendo, MC Skurge, MC Bruce Lei, and Jaytwo.

Mimosa has made a distinct mark on the west coast sound in the last couple years and has become one of the top west coast exports. This young producer's energy whilst performing is magnetic; the word has spread fast. Fans know Mimosa as someone who brings a good-time energy that is as fierce as it is friendly, taking them on journeys through urban chaos and ecstasy.

Deathface, aka Johnny Love, is a former member of LA electro duo Guns & Bombs and a Chicago native. Named “Artist To Watch 2011” by Beatportal. Currently touring for his new release on Trouble & Bass, the Fall Of Man EP that's out now. A six-track EP inspired by Midwest hardcore in the '90s, Magic the Gathering, woodland bonfire parties, white trash drug debauchery, Atari Teenage Riot and Aleister Crowley. Wait til you see him rock a live set.

Forward is not just a direction, it's a way of life for Colorado based producer Alex B who is rolling out big tunes under the new guise of Paper Diamond in 2011. His sound has raw energy and the kind of dramatic anticipation only a seasoned producer can incite. Driving beats and bass grab on tight while deep, rich tones rumble under layers of spacey synthesizers, sweet melodies, and catchy vocals. One thing is for sure. The energy is high and you will dance.

Also, supporting guest sets from:
-BOGL (Soundpieces SF)
-T DUB (Rebel Bass Collective SF)

Photos by: Lekkycharms Photos. Visuals by: Takeshi. Drink specials & low lows all night.

title: Alex Nelson
description:
Alex Nelson doesn’t yet know where his music is going or where it’s going to take him. It continually changes. Like most gifted young musicians, Nelson is constantly practicing, learning, recording, and experimenting with his music. As long as his music is changing, Nelson will be doing the same.

Alex Nelson stuns his listeners not so much as if he’s reading their minds but rather knowing their hearts without the usual smack of melodrama that tends to accompany music of this genre. With a stellar sense of humor fatefully paired with a lightning-fast wit, both onstage and off, Alex Nelson gets to the bottom of the human heart with all he says and does. His lyrics strip a person down to the soul to reveal a most universally undeniable factor: we all tend to think too much and hold back when we shouldn’t.

title: Dippin' Sauce
description: Dippin' Sauce is an electrifying blues band that has been captivating audiences in the Sacramento area and beyond. The band has three singers and song writers; Ro Harpo, Matt Rainey, and Dave Channell, who help make the sound of Dippin' Sauce fresh and diverse with many styles and influences.

title: Wires & Wood: An Evening of Americana
description:
Wires & Wood is a forum for artists to share their craft. Each episode features a specific genre with a guest host to represent the musical stylings. Whether you are looking for a great place to go on a date or simply hang out and relax with friends, Marilyn's on K provides live music, pool table, and cocktails. This installment of Wires & Wood Acoustic performance series offers a blend of original folk, country, bluegrass. Come on down and listen to Jay, and enjoy authentic Americana.

The Jay Dirt Band (some of Slewfoot String Band) sound like a tough, hillbillified Arthur Lee-led Love when they play Jay's car paean "429," and they love Cash, the Byrds, Neil Young, and Jimmy Rogers. Dark and fun. Featuring Jay Swanigan on vocals and 6-string, they will have your toes tappin' and your fingers drummin' with a sound that's a little bit country and a little bit rock 'n roll.

title: Pub Quiz: Hosted by Morgan
description: Test your wits at Fox & Goose's weekly Pub Quiz.

title: Capitol Steps
description:
The Capitol Steps began as a group of Senate staffers who set out to satirize the very people and places that employed them.

In the years that followed, many of the Steps ignored the conventional wisdom ("Don't quit your day job!"), and although not all of the current members of the Steps are former Capitol Hill staffers, taken together the performers have worked in a total of eighteen Congressional offices and represent 62 years of collective House and Senate staff experience.

Since they began, the Capitol Steps have recorded over 30 albums, including their latest, Liberal Shop of Horrors and Barackin' Around the Christmas Tree. They've been featured on NBC, CBS, ABC, and PBS, and can be heard four times a year on National Public Radio stations nationwide during their Politics Takes a Holiday radio specials.

title: Karaoke Night
description: Enjoy an evening of Karaoke at Laughs Unlimited.

title: Freak Nasty Erotic Poetry
description: Freak Nasty is an erotic poetry jam featuring poets from all around the area. Also enjoy performances by burlesque dancers and other surprises to make all your senses tingle.

title: Stand Up for Education: Special Screening and Discussion
description: Join for a special film screening followed by a brief discussion about education reform. This program is presented by Stand Up for Education, a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring every child has the opportunity to attend an excellent public school.

title: Copyright for Film and Video
description:
Join California Lawyers for the Arts as Entertainment Attorney Christine Lynn O'Connor discusses Copyright Law as it pertains to film and video. Ms. O'Connor's legal practice concentrates on entertainment law, production legal, contracts, and copyright. She also has a background in film and television development, production, post production, and production finance.

Ms. O'Connor will be focusing on obtaining rights to source material (books, life rights), registering your script, work for hire agreements (talent, crew), production clearances and releases (locations, wardrobe, props, set dressing, video playback materials), music clearances, E & O insurance, and registering your film/video. There will also be networking opportunities and a vendor display. Please join us for this highly informative evening!
venue: Claerbout Solutions at Studio 50 (formerly Peppers TV)

title: Acoustic Open Mic
description: Join the Torch Club mid-week for an acoustic open mic happy hour.

title: Jimmy Pailer
description: Jimmy Pailer is known as one of the most influential and talented blues guitarists in Northern California. He has been perfecting his craft for many years and it truly shows. Jimmy attracts attention wherever he plays because of his unique style and entertaining stage presence. He hails from St. Louis, Missouri, and has been blessed to share the stage with many famous and great Blues greats, such as Walter Trout, Tommy Castro, Leon Russell , Chuck Berry, Bobby Vega, Rare Earth, and Richie Hayward.

title: Steve McLane
description: Enjoy an acoustic performance by blues/folk musician Steve McLane.

title: Happy Thursdays
description:
Join us at the winery for live music, appetizers, and specials on wine by the glass.

Check the site for the musical performers.

title: The Builders and the Butchers
description:
Over the five year history of The Builders and the Butchers--from their beginnings playing on rainy Portland, OR, streets for random passersby, to the early unplugged Mississippi Pizza and Valentines’ shows, to the last three years of endless touring--the band has lived and died for its connection with the audience. Whether playing bar gigs for 50 people or opening arena shows for 3000, the band strives to connect with the audience, and for the audience to connect with one another, every time they take the stage. It’s that beyond anything else that keeps the Builders going.

Also playing:
Damion Suomi
The Minor Prophets

title: Mindy Smith
description: It took eight years for Mindy Smith to become an overnight sensation. The world discovered her suddenly around ‘04, when she started winning awards, appearing on national TV, inspiring critics and artists to sing her praises (and her songs), and riding the momentum of One Moment More, her Vanguard debut. But when she wasn’t accepting Best New Artist honors from the Americana Music Association, she was sharing stages with the likes of Dolly Parton and Emmylou Harris.

title: Harley White Jr. featuring Aaron King
description:
Since 1991, Harley White Jr. has been a prominent figure on the Sacramento music scene in a wide array of roles from pop recording artist with Papa’s Culture, as a creative force with Blackalicious, Original Heads, and Dr. Echo, as an award-winning bassist, and as an impresario presenting the WhiteNoise festival.

Aaron is a guitar virtuoso and already a local legend. Playing with Sacramento luminaries such as the Chrome Addicts, Johnny Heartsman, Omar Sharriff, Little Charlie & the Nightcats, and Harley White Jr., as well as his own band the Imperials, King is renowned as an accomplished guitarist in the style of B.B. King.

title: Acoustic X Trio
description: Northern California premiere groove-funk-bluegrass-jazz-psychedelic-rock band.

title: Sinatra Era Sing Along Piano Bar
description:
Napa Valley is bursting into song with piano maestro Dan Daniels and special guest Nicky DePaola at the Wine Train Depot.

Join your fellow song lovers in a Sinatra Era Sing-Along Piano Bar featuring some of the most beloved songs by Frank Sinatra, Sammy Davis Jr., Dean Martin, and Ella Fitzgerald. Come and sing your lungs out with us or be a star and lead the group at the mic!

Free admission, all ages welcome, and no drink minimum. Beer and other beverages available for purchase, too. And no reservations are needed--just drop in when you're ready for a blast from the past!

title: Rock On Live Band Karaoke
description:
Rock On Live Band Karaoke puts YOU in the spotlight as the vocalist in a Live Rock Band. Choose from an ever-growing song list of popular Rock, Pop, and Country songs. The lyrics are presented on a video monitor and the band is ready to help with background vocals. This is WAY more fun than regular Karaoke...this is Rock On Live Band Karaoke. Rock On LBK brings you over 100 years of collective live performance experience in such well-known groups as Honeyspot, Tattooed Love Dogs, American Karma, Seventy and MindX, just to name a few!

Every Thursday night!

title: The Builders and The Butchers
description:
Over the five year history of The Builders and the Butchers--from their beginnings playing on rainy Portland, OR, streets for random passersby, to the early unplugged Mississippi Pizza and Valentines’ shows, to the last three years of endless touring--the band has lived and died for its connection with the audience. Whether playing bar gigs for 50 people or opening arena shows for 3000, the band strives to connect with the audience, and for the audience to connect with one another, every time they take the stage. It’s that beyond anything else that keeps the Builders going.

Also performing:
Damion Suomi & The Minor Prophets

title: Stephen March
description: Stephen March is an independent singer/songwriter from the Sacramento area. He was somewhat of a latecomer to the musical arena, not picking up the guitar until age 23. His older brother who had played guitar since high school showed him some basic chords and he instantly began singing over them and making melodies. He is most passionate about writing meaningful and thought provoking lyrics.

title: The Golden Cadillacs, Infamous Swanks, Whiskey & Stitches
description: Enjoy country/rockabilly/celtic music performed by The Golden Cadillacs, Infamous Swanks, and Whiskey & Stitches.

title: Kevin Hart: Laugh at My Pain Tour
description: Comedian/actor Kevin Hart returns to the Sacramento Community Center Theater for a night of comedy in his "Laugh at My Pain" tour. Recent film appearances for Hart include Death at a Funeral, Extreme Movie, Scary Movie 4, and Fool's Gold. In January 2009, his one-hour comedy I'm a Grown Little Man premiered on Comedy Central. Comedy stops have included apearrances at Caroline's, Stand-Up NY, The Laugh Factory, and Los Angeles' The Comedy Store.

title: Japan XOXO: Dance for Japan
description: Japan XOXO is a benefit dance party for Japan. All proceeds go to The Red Cross. Join local DJs Shaun Slaughter, Adam J, Sam I Jam, and Taylor Cho as they do what they love to support an amazing cause.

title: Pailer & Fratis
description:
Jimmy Pailer is known as one of the most influential and talented blues guitarists in Northern California. He has been perfecting his craft for many years and it truly shows. Jimmy attracts attention wherever he plays because of his unique style and entertaining stage presence.

Lew Fratis' energetic style on stage provides a show that is sure to electrify any crowd and leave them wanting more.

title: Terry Hanck
description: Terry Hanck is well known for his hard blowing sax, incredible range, and gusty vocals. Born in Chicago, Hanck was heavily influenced by the blues, soul, and jazz music of the '50s and early '60s. After moving to California in 1965, he toured with Elvin Bishop through most of the '70s and '80s and Bishop gave him plenty of opportunities to hone his craft on stage.

title: DJ Missy
description: Enjoy tunes by DJ Missy, accompanied by Longshot Soundsystem.

title: White Minorities, Blownload, Skinhammer
description: Come out to this ghetto metal show featuring White Minorities, Blownload, and Skinhammer.

title: Mike Watt + The Missing Men: North American Hyphenated-Man Tour
description: Mike Watt's third opera Hyphenated-Man was released everywhere March 1, 2011 through his new label Clenchedwrench. Mike Watt's Missing Men consist of Tom Watson on guitar and Raul Morales on drums. Their North American Hypenated-Man Tour is coming to Sacramento for one night only.

title: Scenes From Dreams: Landscapes Inspired by Imagination
description: Scenes From Dreams features installation work and landscapes as inspired by dreams of Phillip Altstatt with featured guest work by Kevin Trivedi. Live music will be featured by Island of Black and White from 4:30pm-8:30pm. Free parking!

title: Acoustic with Johnny Knox
description: Johnny "Guitar" Knox is a real bluesman. He helped define the blues scene in Sacramento. Johnny's a homeless man, a true-blue soul, and one of the finest acoustic blues guitarist living in the world today.

title: Ty Curtis
description: Ty Curtis is consumed by his music. There is no other way to explain how, at such a young age, this 23-year-old, Salem, Oregon based, vocalist/guitarist/song writer has amassed a recording catalog of three critically acclaimed albums, earned 2nd place in the prestigious 2009 International Blues Challenge in Memphis, and is nightly thrilling audiences from the Pacific Northwest to Montreal.

title: The Zoo Human Project
description:
The Zoo Human Project's tunes are a frenetic blend of dueling guitars, funky world percussion, and tight three-part harmonies.

Also performing:
The Isaac Howl

title: Godfrey
description: Godfrey is an American comedian and actor who has appeared on BET, VH1, Comedy Central, and feature films such as Soul Plane, Original Gangstas, Zoolander, and Johnson Family Vacation. He was also a spokesperson for 7 Up during the popular "7up yours" advertising campaign. He was a cast member on the first season of The It Factor, a reality television show. Currently, he is a regular performer at the comedy club Comedy Cellar in New York City and voices Mr. Stubborn and Mr. Tall (Season 2) in The Mr. Men Show.

title: Faizon Love
description:
Faizon Love was born Langston Faizon Santisima in Santiago de Cuba and raised in San Diego, California and Newark, New Jersey because of his father's Navy career. Love got his start as a stand-up comedian and made his acting debut in an Off-Broadway at the age of nineteen. His first film Bebe's Kids had him providing the voice of Robin Harris. Harris died before production began and Love replaced him with an accurate impression. He then had a role in The Meteor Man starring Robert Townsend. Townsend then cast Love in a co-starring role on his sitcom The Parent 'Hood. He followed up this role with a breakout performance as the drug dealer Big Worm in the 1995 film Friday.

Follow-up films have included Elf, Don't Be a Menace to South Central While Drinking Your Juice in the Hood, Money Talks, Wonderland, The Fighting Temptations, and Idlewild. Love also guests on Ludacris' "Freaky Thangs" from the album Word of Mouf. Love co-starred in the 2009 film Couples Retreat, a comedy chronicling four couples who partake in therapy sessions at a tropical island resort.

Many gamers may know Love on the role of Sean "Sweet" Johnson, simply known as Sweet, in the Rockstar North game Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Frank Lucero
description:
Enjoy live stand-up comedy from Frank Lucero of the Latin Kings of Comedy. Frank is from a small town north of Sacramento called Colusa. After many a jobs in a small town, Frank decided to go to college at San Jose State Univ. and majored in Theatre Arts. Always entertaining his family at Christmas parties and at other family functions, Frank was inspired to make complete strangers laugh as well. Upon graduating, Frank moved to L.A. to pursue his acting and comedy career.

Frank is quickly becoming one of the top comedians to see. He’s energetic, fun, and all about family. Frank will riff about our everyday routines we call “work” and to breaking that routine by having “fun”, to being with family and playing our guitars.

description:
Serani is a new Reggae artist that has took Jamaica by a storm and is continuing to do so across the world. Serani, born in the mean streets of Kingston Jamaica, decided at a young age that, with his two other best friends who also shared the same intrest in music, would put together the informus DASECA productions in 2001.

title: Portugal the Man
description: An experimental indie rock four-piece centered on frontman John Baldwin Gourley’s abstract musical approach and corresponding upbringing. He was raised in a sort of technological isolation: his log cabin home in the winter wasteland of the fringes of Wasilla, Alaska was powered by a generator and had no telephone. Both of his parents helped completely immerse him in the unique lifestyle that comes with with their jobs as dog sled mushers.

title: House of Floyd: A Tribute to Pink Floyd
description: House of Floyd, a reverent tribute to Pink Floyd, captures the intoxicating sights and sounds of the original for even the most discriminating fan. House of Floyd pays the highest tribute to the original by accurately recreating all of the nuanced musical complexity and powerful visual imagery of Pink Floyd. The result of this obsessive attention to detail is a total Floyd production...music, lights, lasers, and video.

title: The Lipstick Weekender

title: Charley's Aunt
description: This hilarious British farce has been entertaining audiences for over a hundred years. Watch what happens when Lord Fancourt Babberly impersonates Charley’s aunt Donna Lucia in order to chaperone Charley and Jack on their first date with two new young lady friends. Chaos ensues.

title: Write Your Screenplay: An Eight Week Intensive
description:
Award-winning screenwriter Gary Weinberg will guide students as they learn the craft and the business of screenwriting, with an emphasis on how these manifest in the current Los Angeles film and television industry.

The workshop will focus on screenplay and teleplay formatting, building and structuring a story, how to write compelling, believable dialogue, and develop strong characters. Weinberg will also present different options that students have for getting their work seen and produced, and he'll discuss the “unwritten” rules that can help, or hinder, their screenwriting efforts.

The goal by the end of the eight week program is for each student to have a completed first draft of their screenplay. The class runs four consecutive weeks from Feb 22-Mar 15, and then every other week until May 10. This format affords students time to actually write a finished screenplay or teleplay.

title: Live Music by Rolling Fork Blues Revue
description:
Rolling Fork Blues Revue is a Northern California Band playing pure, classic blues. A four-piece combo including guitar, saxophone, bass, and drums, the Rolling Fork Blues Revue brings to life the classic Chicago blues of Muddy Waters and Howlin' Wolf, the Memphis sounds of B. B. King and Albert King, the Texas style of Freddie King, and the classic women's blues of Bessie Smith and Ida Cox.

Charles Oriel, on guitar and vocals, has been playing guitar and singing for 40 years. Bill Bua, on saxophone, is well versed in the jazz tradition. Together Charles and Bill trade dynamic solos and fills. Julia Simon, on bass guitar and vocals, has gigged in blues bands for 9 years. Bob Robbins, on the drums, creates a steady, in-the-pocket groove.

description: Enjoy an evening of Karaoke at Laughs Unlimited.

title: Agent Ribbons
description: The story of Agent Ribbons has not one--but many--beginnings, and fashioning some semblance of chronology from their cut-and-paste four-year history is an art project in and of itself. title: The Alkali Flats CD Release Party
description:
The Alkali Flats have been kicking around in one form or another for several years, playing everywhere from your front porch to Chateaus in France, from roadside fry shops in Cleveland to the annual Hillbilly Fest in downtown Los Angeles. The Sactopalooza Spring Party has 10 acts on 4 huge stages, featuring DJ Rigatony and DJ Peeti-V spinning mad dance beats plus eight nationally recruited top-notch tribute bands performing the music and full stage performance of: Sublime, Dave Matthews Band, No Doubt, Journey, INXS, Van Halen, Beastie Boys, and U2. title: Oaxaca: Textiles & Alebrijes
description:
In Oaxaca: Textiles & Alebriges, you have a great opportunity to enjoy two “artesano” art forms: Textiles & Alebrijes from Oaxaca, México. Alebrijes are fantastical wooden and paper maché sculptures. The first “alebrijes” originated from unsettling dreams/hallucinations by Oaxacan Pedro Linares in the 1930s (very Kafka-ish, right?). During these dreams Linares encountered these animals that kept repeating one word/mantra: alebrijes, alebrijes, alebrijes, alebrijes…To learn more about the history of alebrijes visit the gallery to get a personalized tour.

title: Open Reel: A Juried Short Film Competition
description:
The Center for Contemporary Art, Sacramento (CCAS) proudly announces that it has added Open Reel, a juried, 3 minute short film competition, to the 6th annual Capitol Artists’ Studio Tour (CAST). The juried competition will be the prelude to the Tour weekend, in which nearly 100 artists open their studios to the public for free. CAST has focused largely on more traditional mediums (i.e., painting and ceramics) so Open Reel was added to feature the vibrant, Sacramento independent film community who otherwise do not have an opportunity to showcase their work to the general public.

CCAS Capitol Artists' Studio Tour Committee Chair, Cheryl Holben comments, "I am thrilled to be increasing the scope of the Tour. Open Reel will bring the filmmakers the attention they have long deserved by both the general public and the art’s community.”

Jurors for the competition will be: Jenny E. Stark, Associate Professor of Communication Studies and Film, California State University Sacramento, CCAS Exhibition Committee member and award winning filmmaker and Ed Ortiz, Arts Journalist and Music Critic for the Sacramento Bee, award winning playwright and instructor of screenwriting at California State University, Sacramento.

Participants, both amateur and professional, must submit work that is 3 minutes or less in duration. There are no other restrictions and prizes will be awarded for best amateur film and audience favorite. See the Classified for more information (Submission deadline is July 30, 2011).

title: 2nd Saturday- Midtown Art Walk
description:
On the second Saturday of each month, many local Sacramento galleries feature new shows of individual and collective artists. Many galleries play host to the artists so it's a wonderful way to meet them in person. Some galleries provide beverages, Hors d oeuvres, live music and even dinner with the artist!

Since many galleries are grouped into two main areas in Sacramento, midtown and along Del Paso Blvd (The Uptown Arts District), many people like to take an ARTWALK and wonder from gallery to gallery and make and evening of art and people viewing. More galleries and venues can be found in Old Sacramento, Downtown Sacramento as well as in outlying areas including Folsom & Fair Oaks.

title: Saddle Up & Ride It Out- A Solidarity Dance Party
description: Join us for an evening of country dancing. All proceeds benefit the Sacramento Gay & Lesbian Center, Capital City AIDS Fund, and Capital Crossroads Gay Rodeo Association.

title: '80s Night with DJ Billy Lane
description: Billy Lane of 107.9 The End DJs a weekly '80s dance night every Tuesday. Drink specials include $3 wells and domestics.

title: Mahogany Urban Poetry Series
description: The Mahogany Urban Poetry Series is a weekly poetry open mic with a featured performer. Hosted by Khiry Malik Moore, Ifamodupe, NSAA, and the Poet i.

title: Suspects Dinner Theater
description:
Comedy, suspense, mystery, fun, good food, and audience participation are all rolled into one hilarious evening at Suspects. Since 1989, Suspects Dinner Theater has been performing fast-paced audience participation murder mystery comedies in Old Sacramento. Suspects is not your everyday dinner and a show. During a night at Suspects, the action takes place all around you--an actor may be seated at your table, a guest may become a detective or a suspect, and everyone has the opportunity to solve the crime. The sleuth coming closest receives a prize at the end of the evening.

If you hunger for an exciting evening of murder, mystery, and comedy, Suspects is the place you want to be. But don’t worry: our guests never die, because we know a dead customer is not a repeat customer.
venue: Suspects Dinner Theater - Aboard the Riverboat Delta King

title: History Talks: Art in Reconstructing Societies and Developing Identities
description:
The symposium will discuss different situations where art has been involved in the process of social repair. The objective is to revise models in history where art has been used to recreate features of a community in order to help reestablish its values and identity.

Guest speakers include: Ithaca College professor Jennifer Jolly, University of Essex postgraduate student Esmeralda Salinas, photographer Joaquin Sarmiento from Colombia, and UC Davis professor and artist Xico Gonzales.

This event takes place in the Hinde Auditorium in Sacramento State's University Union.

title: Mastering the Mysteries of Love
description:
Deep love doesn’t actually involve magic, but it does require the ongoing application of communication skills that can be learned. Teach simple skills that have been developed through scientific research to help couples improve ordinary conversations and turn a dysfunctional relationships into a healthy ones.

The MML program teaches couples ten skills that enable them to uncover and communicate their deepest feelings, concerns, and desires and create win-win solutions to even the most difficult problems. Instruction is given in role-play, skills training, and coaching format. These skills can improve any relationship for a lifetime.

title: Legal & Insurance Issues for Volunteer Programs Workshop
description: This is an opportunity to bring yourself up-to-date on legal and insurance issues around utilizing volunteers in nonprofit organizations. Being pro-active can save you a lot of time and money. Join your fellow Volunteer Professionals in this important half-day training seminar.
venue: Shriner's Hospital For Children- Northern California

title: Dementia Support Group
description:
Spouses, family members, and friends who are providing care to seniors with memory loss are encouraged to participate in a dementia support group. Linda Zisko, director of The Club Memory Day Care program, facilitates the group.

The community, managed by Hank Fisher Properties, offers remarkably affordable, high quality independent and assisted living along with The Garden Memory Care and The Club Memory Day Care.

The support group will continue to meet the second Thursday of each month to offer family care providers with encouragement, education, resources, and caregiving guidance.

While caregivers attend the support group, their loved ones can participate in The Club Memory Day Care program at no charge. Space is limited, however, and reservations are required. For reservations, directions, or information about the Chateau at Carmichael Park, call the number below.

title: Building Successful Non-Profit Arts Organizations: A Seminar with Dr. Matthew Hinsley
description:
This seminar is for anyone who values the role of art in his or her community. The seminar will inspire and motivate participants to address the most important issues facing the participant’s nonprofit organization. Dr. Hinsley will give a 90-minute seminar outlining topics in his book including, but not limited to:
1. Board of Director Development
2. Strategic Planning
3. Working with volunteers
4. Raising Money
5. Publicity and the Media
6. Managing Growth
7. YOUR Questions will be answered!

The final 30 minutes will be a no cost reception with food and non-alcoholic beverages. The reception will allow participants to purchase Dr. Hinsley's book (and get a $10 discount) and ask questions to Dr. Hinsley face to face. (Please let us know if you have food allergies. We will accommodate everyone, as we have access to a Registered Dietitian).

For those that want more detailed information from Dr. Hinsley, participants will also be able to sign up for the West Coast Guitar Societies Workshop on Saturday, April 16. The topics apply to all non-profits, not just guitar societies.

Dr. Hinsley was trained formally as an instrumental performer, not as an arts administrator. Over the course of fifteen years building community based arts programming, however, Hinsley learned valuable lessons from volunteers, board members, colleagues, and patrons. The lessons he’s learned, both through successes and missteps, apply to the real-world challenges arts entrepreneurs and their supporters face each an every day.

title: Loose Leash Seminar
description: Tired of your pet walking you? Come to a loose leash seminar workshop to help your pet learn to walk at your command. The Petco trainer will be available in instruct, offer advice and tips, and answer any questions you may have about trainin your pet on and off a leash.

title: West Coast Guitar Societies Roundtable: All Nonprofits Welcome
description:
This seminar is for anyone who values the role of art in his or her community--all Non-profit Arts Organizations are welcome.

Dr. Matthew Hinsley will inspire and motivate participants to address the most important issues facing the participant’s nonprofit organization. Dr. Hinsley, author of the book, Creativity to Community: Arts Nonprofit Success One Coffee at a Time, will dedicate a full day to train participants on topics important to all non-profit arts organizations including, but not limited to:

1. Board of Director Development
2. Strategic Planning
3. Working with volunteers
4. Raising Money
5. Publicity and the Media
6. Managing Growth
7. YOUR Questions will be answered! The Roundtable will provide ample time for discussion between participants and time to ask your specific questions to Dr. Hinsley.

Dr. Hinsley was trained formally as an instrumental performer, not as an arts administrator. Over the course of fifteen years building community based arts programming, however, Hinsley learned valuable lessons from volunteers, board members, colleagues, and patrons. The lessons he’s learned, both through successes and missteps, apply to the real-world challenges arts entrepreneurs and their supporters face each an every day.

title: Chiron 101: Be Your Own Hero
description:
What are the implications of Chiron--its astrology, myth, and cultural context? This presentation is guaranteed to change your perspective on one of the relatively newer additions to sky lore and what it means to you. Often called "the wounded healer," astrological Chiron's mission is to show us how to break through old pain that keeps us stuck, to give back to our community, and find fulfillment.

Joyce Mason has specialized in Chiron throughout her 23-year career as an astrological consultant and writer. She created the Chironic Convergence in 1996, a week-long school near Chiron's mythical homeland in Greece. Her work has appeared in The Mountain Astrologer and astro-publications at home and abroad. Her popular blog, The Radical Virgo, features over 120 of her articles, old and new. Joyce is President of NCGR-Sacramento Area Chapter and is known around the globe for her work on Chiron and her trademark of writing about astrology with both depth and humor.

title: Road Repair Clinic
description: In this 45-minute class you will learn how to fix a flat on both your front and rear tires as well as what to pack in your repair kit. After this class you will never be left calling for a ride the next time you get a flat tire. Bring your bike for hands on learning.

title: The Real Mayan Calendar: An Introduction to the Mayan Underworlds
description:
The Universal Co-Creation Cycle started on March 9 and it is off with a bang! See the Timeline for the Universal Co-Creation Cycle. But what does that even mean? While interest in the Mayan’s grand calendar systems has increased as we approach 2012, the confusion surrounding the implications of this information has hit an all time high. Is the world ending? Is the calendar just re-starting? What will happen after 2012? These are just a few of the common questions surrounding this very misunderstood topic. Join us for a class where Chris will briefly explore the work of Carl Johan Calleman and Ian Lungold in unraveling the mysteries of the Mayan calendar.

In this class you will learn how to distinguish the parts of the calendar that are re-calibrating from the parts that are actually terminating. You’ll learn about evolution through the “Mayan Underworlds” which form the backbone of the Mayan calendar system and which explain the increase in the frequency of change over time. Finally, you’ll learn how the process of creation has been occurring according to a timeline and that it is THIS process that is actually ending.

After the process of creation is complete…what will be the creation? Finally, according to the work of Calleman and Lungold the calendar system representing the process of creation does not actually end on December 21, 2012! Join us and find out when it actually DOES end and what this may mean for humanity as a whole.

Instructor: Christopher Robert Taylor. See a playlist preview of this class.

title: “Live With the Chef” Cooking Class
description:
With the weather heating up, it’s time to “Get Your Grill On” during the next “Live With the Chef” cooking class! Chef Josh will demonstrate cooking techniques and grill secrets to make fast and healthy meals all summer long! This special monthly cooking class is focused on incorporating fresh ingredients designed to maximize the nutrients for a healthy and well balanced diet.

You’re invited to join this ongoing and popular adult cooking series--couples are welcome, too! Space is limited so reserve yours today.

title: Women in Bizness' "Entrepreneuse" Entrepreneurship Symposium
description:
Come board the entrepreneur-ship with Women in Bizness at the "Entrepreneuse" Entrepreneurship Symposium. Featuring the "Woman of Power" Awards Buffet Dinner with a special "Everyday Mother" Mother's Day Tribute.

-Learn how to balance your business and personal life
-Discover the business in your child
-Learn about social media and your business
-Spiritual aspects of business
-How to start your business step by step
-And more!

Make this year, your best year ever--register today!

title: Watercolor Painting with Rice Paper Collage
description:
Watch a demonstration of watercolor painting and collage then experiment using watercolor, rice paper, and your imagination as you compose a symphony of texture, color, and line.

This class is part of the Crocker's new series—called Saturday Singles—of easygoing, half-day and one-day workshops designed for weekend artists to experiment with different art forms. Other classes in the series explore abstract painting, clay hand building, and beginning photography.

About the Instructor: Gayle Rappaport-Weiland is a professional artist, teacher, consultant, juror, and broadcast art expert for KVIE, radio, and internet shows. Rappaport-Weiland creates art from her soul in watercolor, acrylic, and mixed medias. She is known for her teaching ability and for creating a stress–free, positive learning environment. Her mantra is, “You can do anything you put your mind to.”

title: Around the World Cooking Demonstration: Destination: Italy!
description: Ciao Italia! Learn to prepare luscious marinara sauces and bruschetta bursting with freshness at the Around the World Cooking Demonstration: Destination: Italy. With an infusion of Italian flavored aromas to tempt the palate, guests will learn how to prepare signature dishes from Italy but that use today’s heart-healthy ingredients and creative cooking techniques.

title: Teaching Artist Workshop Series: Poetry Off the Page
description:
The Teaching Artist Workshop Series Poetry Off the Page: Crossing boundaries and expanding imaginations with words features performance/praise poet and writer Glenis Redmond, Kennedy Center Presenter. Refreshments are served. Parking is plentiful and free.

Glenis Redmond's love of words has carried her across the country for over thirteen years. Glenis logs over 35,000 miles a year bringing poetry to the masses. This Road Warrior Poet, though steeped in Afro-Carolinian roots, speaks a universal tongue of love, loss, celebration, sorrow, and hope. Her verse uplifts family, culture, and community. Glenis is a gentle pen pusher as she encourages others to find their voice at diverse venues across the country from prisons, universities, festivals, conferences, theaters to schools. Her poems soothe, illicit, and inspire others to pick up their pen and travel their own poetic road.

The Teaching Artist Workshop Series (TAWS) is a series of distinct workshops on a variety of topics of interest to artists who also want to teach and build careers as teaching artists. The series is developed and presented by the Arts Commission’s Education staff with regional and national presenters from the visual and performing arts and education fields.

description:

Successful completion of class includes a Wilderness First Aid certificate. This class is taught by Bobbie Foster of Foster Calm. She has been teaching wilderness first aid across Northern California since 1994.

title: Thistle Dew Playwright Group
description:
The original new play critique forum at Thistle Dew Theatre: Calling all Playwrights and wanna-bees! Do you have a play you'd like critiqued? The workshop members and the owners of The Thistle Dew, Tom and Ellie, are dedicated to supporting original works by local playwrights and offer the opportunity for new works to be performed in Sacramento on the Thistle Dew stage. On Monday nights, jump into the critique fray or listen quietly....until your passions rise and you feel compelled to join the mêlée. (Overheard before a reading: "I came just to listen, honestly, I've never critiqued a play before, but I just had to say something about Act II, Scene Three ...."). Yes. We know. We've all been there. All newcomers are welcome!

Published playwrights since Thistle Dew Playwright's Workshop began three years ago: Laura Sheperd, Annie's Story, Julie Greene, Going Somewhere?, Timothy Cahill, The Seduction of Thomas Sorrell and Going to Tibet, Charles McIntosh, The Divine Court-Martial of Field-Marshal Keitel, Thomas M. Kelly, ...smile, and smile, and be a villain, Ba-Bang! (or the end of an error!), The Timekeeper, Fana!, The Butterfly Within, Extreme Unction, Zen and the Art of Making Par and a collection of childrens plays: You're in Trouble Now, Charlie!, This is Not Our Backyard, Charlie!, Wake Up, Jay! It's Christmas!, and Stop Snoring, Jay! I'm Dreaming of Christmas.

Local playwrights produced at the Thistle Dew Playwright's Theatre: (Full-Length Plays) Timothy Cahill, Julie Greene, Paul Hauck, Thomas M. Kelly, Leo McElroy, Charles McIntosh, Laura Sheperd, Donya Wicken, (Monologues) Gladys Acosta, Timothy Cahill, Charley Cross, Theresa Elliot, Mark Fejta, Bernie Goldberg, Julie Greene, Eugene Griffith, Cindi Bennett, Frank Ingram, Gloria Jones, Thomas M. Kelly, Charles Kelso, Roger Linder, Laura Sheperd, Susan Webster, Donya Wicken and Jeff Webster.

Copies of most of the published plays are available in the lobby of the Thistle Dew Dessert Theatre.

description: This studio time will be available to students who have participated in other ceramics classes and are looking to work independently while getting help as needed. Each week short demonstrations/exercises and various ceramic skills and techniques are given. Instruction will be geared to the participants' interests and needs.
venue: Allied Ceramics Art Institute Studios & Gallery

title: Spring Forest Qigong: Level One Practice Group
description:
Spring Forest QiGong (SFQ) is a simple, efficient, and effective method for helping you heal physical and emotional pain and enhance the quality of your life and the lives of others.

Anyone & everyone--regardless of ability, age, or beliefs--can practice the techniques of Spring Forest Qigong to become healthier and happier.

Join us for a lunchtime Practice Group, no experience necessary. The session is structured in such a way that it allows for some people arriving from their place of work a few minutes after Noon, and leaving a few minutes before 1pm. It is a great way to energize and recharge at mid-week for the last days of the work week!

title: Festival of the Arts
description:
The 2011 Festival of the Arts is put on by Sacramento State's School of the Arts and features performances and exhibitions by various departments. Enjoy music concerts, theatre performances, poetry readings, art exhibitions, and more!

Schedule & highlights include:
Ongoing: The Wiz, The Real Fake: Exploring 3D Art
Wed, Apr 13: Sac State Wind Ensemble
Thurs, Apr 14: Donny McCaslin with Sac State Jazz Group, How Austentious

title: Sacramento Classic Car & Parts Swap Meet
description:
Started in 1965 by Bill Harrah in Reno, the annual swap meet is now located in Sacramento. Many long time vendors, who have been with us over the years and who had quit going up to Nevada, when the room rates and all the City fees got out of control, have now returned and many will be selling exclusively with us at our new location at Power Balance Pavilion. Along with the traditional classic car & parts swap meet there will be a car corral for vehicles for sale.

Event occurs rain or shine.

title: Painters Paradise
description: Patris Studio in partnership with the Oak Park Business Association are proud to host Painters Paradise on 35th Street between Broadway and 4th Avenue. The 2nd Annual Painters Paradise features artists painting live onsite, live music by Lee Bootz's Southside Shuffle, live entertainment, food, kids' zone, vendors, health resource information, flash mob performance, and a car show.

title: 5th Annual Raley Field Brewfest
description: Enjoy a variety of handcrafted microbrews from more than 30 Northern California breweries at the 5th Annual Raley Field Brewfest. Enjoy great beer and live music along the Raley Field concourse, which lends a great view of downtown Sacramento.

title: West Coast Brew Fest
description:
The West Coast Brew Fest 2011 is the 12th Annual celebration of the West Coast heritage of the microbrew revolution. Featuring Tokenless Microbrew Tasting of over 120 different beers from over 60 breweries, along with live music and great food, not to mention awesome people!

WCBF holds a BCJP-sanctioned Commercial Craft Competition two weeks prior to the event and winning Breweries will be displaying their award-winning brews at the festival. A complete list of breweries attending will be available online two weeks prior to the event.

Get your tickets early, they promise to sell out. Proceeds benefit the Make A Difference Project.

title: Raley's Grape Escape
description:
An opportunity to sample from the region’s best wineries and restaurants for one incredible price!

The Sacramento Convention & Visitors Bureau (SCVB) is pleased to announce the return of the 9th annual Grape Escape – A Capital Region Wine and Food Celebration - Presented by Raley's & Bel Air. The event brings the most delicious products from eight counties together at one all-inclusive event to celebrate the region's award winning wine country and highly-touted local cuisine. Featuring more than 100 local wineries and restaurants including wine and food tastings, a chef’s cooking competition, and live music and art displays. 

Named by Restaurant News as the city whose "Restaurants Sizzle," Sacramento has evolved into a vibrant dining Mecca. Time magazine has also named Sacramento the most diverse city in America, which is reflected in the many flavors found in restaurants throughout the region.

To showcase these sizzling restaurants, chefs from the capital region will tempt taste buds and tickle palates as they display their talents with savory spices and a set timer. Take one market basket filled with the freshest ingredients; add a gourmet chef, time for 25 minutes and voila, a recipe for the Chef’s Challenge.

Last year’s competition was fierce as four teams battled it out with spatulas, spoons and whisks! Oh, my! Each team, consisting of a chef and an assistant, was given 25 minutes to produce and serve up a dish featuring fresh produce and a choice cut of meat. Teams competed in two rounds, and winners advanced to the finals to prepare and serve another creative and mouth-watering dish in minutes.

Don't miss this year's flavorful competition!

title: Sacramento Aloha Festival
description: The Sacramento Aloha Steering Committee, under the umbrella of the Hui O' Hawai`i Sacramento Inc., are proud to present the 1st Annual Sacramento Aloha Festival. The Festival strives to perpetuate the culture of Sacramento’s Native Hawaiian and Pacific Island communities through the teaching and sharing of Hawai`i’s hula, language, history, music, and cultural crafts at the inaugural Aloha Festival.

title: Ten22 Spring Patio Opening with NOW 100.5 FM
description:
Relish the beginning of Spring with Ten22, Sacramento’s “Best New Restaurant” (2010, Subscribers' Picks Award, Sacramento Magazine). The restaurant will open its contemporary and spacious patio, celebrating the changing of the seasons with a fresh new Spring Menu, music, and fun!

The festivities will kick off with NOW 100.5 FM’s radio station DJ and promotions team. Patrons will be the first to taste the new Spring Menu featuring local, organic, and seasonal ingredients.

title: Murder Mystery Dinner Theater
description: The Napa Valley Wine Train is pleased to announce a new Murder Mystery play centering on the clandestine world of the gum shoe. Come prepared to mix and mingle, dress the part, or just get down to business and solve the murder.

title: Around the World Cooking Demo: Destination France
description:
Vive la France! As part of a continuing focus on wellness, you won’t want to miss a French-inspired Around the World Cooking Demonstration: Destination France. With a decidedly French flair, guests will learn how to prepare signature dishes made famous in France but that use today’s heart-healthy ingredients and creative cooking techniques.

Open to everyone, advance reservations are suggested as space is limited.

title: Good Finds at Good Eats
description:
This event will feature cooking sauces from locally based Elegant and Easy Gourmet by Betsy Hite, with a demonstration of how to prepare easy dishes using items from the Good Eats Market. In addition, the dishes will be paired with a champagne tasting.

To become a featured purveyor at a future Good Finds event, contact Ruthann Dittrich at (916) 548-9600 or by the email address below.

title: Thursday Night Jazz & Wine
description: Enjoy a relaxing and entertaining spring evening filled with jazz and wine. With wine tastings provided by Chalone Vineyard--the oldest producing vineyard in Monterey County--and live music by Tessa Evans, you’re sure to experience new flavors and meet new friends along the way. This is your chance to enjoy an evening of musical entertainment while appreciating a variety of wines and complimentary light appetizers provided by Arden Hills.

title: The Firehouse's Spring Courtyard Opening Lunch
description:
Voted “Best Outdoor Dining,” Sacramento’s most-celebrated courtyard is set to open for lunch dining.  For more than 50 years, The Firehouse’s brick and ivy-covered courtyard has been the “go-to” place for everything from weddings and anniversaries to business lunches and fundraisers. Combining a New Orleans-style outdoor setting with award-winning cuisine, a world-class wine collection, and impeccable service, The Firehouse’s Courtyard provides the perfect outdoor dining experience for all tastes.

This year, The Firehouse will celebrate the annual opening with the launch of its new Spring Menu, a complimentary champagne toast of Laetitia Brut Cuvée, and a special offer for groups of four or more: 50 percent off their food bill. The opening will also feature live music from Sacramento-native, acoustic guitarist and soul singer Ryan Hernandez, always a community favorite.

title: Moonlight Escape Dinner
description:
Share the magic of the Napa Valley in April as the sun sets at 7:46pm. This moon is named the "Full Pink Moon" because the earliest of the spring flowers are pink. Our Moonlight Escape gourmet dinner takes place upstairs in the Vista Dome rail car with its almost 180-degree view. Guests glide over the evening vineyards touched with the silver light of the rising moon.

This is a five-course dinner, including a glass of sparkling wine, and two glasses of our private label. There is seating for only 24 couples.

title: Dishcrawl Sacramento
description:
No dirty politics, just good food at Sacramento’s first Dishcrawl. Dishcrawl is coming to California’s Capitol city, so don’t miss your chance to taste the various delicacies Downtown Sacramento restaurants have to offer! Experience this city in a different light with fellow foodies, and re-learn everything you thought you knew about the community and its people. Eat good food, make new friends, and remember the night. Participants will hop around to four different restaurants where they will get try a filling taste of the Restaurant's chosen featured dish at each place. Each stop lasts approximately 30 minutes.

Note: The restaurants and dishes are kept a secret until the night of the event. The meeting location will be revealed two days before the event. Cancellations are only taken if done 48 hours in advance.

About Dishcrawl: Have you heard of Dishcrawl? It's a new way to discover your food neighborhood! Get to know friends over an exciting adventure through restaurants you never knew existed. It's delicious and fun! Price of one ticket reservation includes all food for one dishcrawler.

title: Murder Mystery Dinner Theater
description: The Napa Valley Wine Train is pleased to announce a new Murder Mystery play centering on the clandestine world of the gum shoe. Come prepared to mix and mingle, dress the part, or just get down to business and solve the murder.

title: Wine in the Park with the River Cats
description:
Join us for an evening of wine tasting and River Cats baseball! Ticket includes exclusive early entrance to the ball park, wine tasting from four of our favorite boutique/family-owned wineries in the VIP tented patio off the 3rd base line, and a fantastic seat to the game!

Bring your friends, colleagues, or anyone who enjoys tasting new wines, giving to a great cause, and sharing an evening with a great group of people! A portion of the proceeds will be donated to St.John's Shelter Program for Women and Children.

Get your tickets before they sell out!

title: Easter Brunch
description: Easter is made for brunch at the Hyatt Regency Sacramento. Join us for a bountiful holiday buffet featuring omelets made-to-order, pasta, seafood, a carving station, and a dessert extravaganza.

title: 20th Annual Feast for the Streets
description:
This year’s event is dedicated to our beloved Greg Bunker, our Executive Director, who passed away suddenly in December. Greg started the Feast 20 years ago and it has grown and improved every year. Please join us in a toast to honor this incredible man and friend to those most in need of compassion and a helping hand.

This year's Feast features fantastic food from such fine establishments as Mulvaney's B & L , Tuli Bistro, Thai Basil, Espanol, Ella's, and many more exceptional Sacramento eateries. There will also be wine tasting from some wonderful local wineries including Bogle Vineyard, Montevina/Terra del Oro and Heriger Estates. There will be silent and live auctions, where you can bid on everything from creative gift baskets to deluxe vacations and spa retreats. Live music from Jazz Gitan will provide atmosphere for this gala event. If you enjoy good food, good wine, and good company...don't miss this event! Bring your friends.

title: Vintage 2011: A Benefit for Stanford Home for Children
description:
Fine wine and food tasting, silent and live auctions, entertainment, and a program honoring The May Family and Kathy McKim, V.P. External Affairs for AT&T.

Benefiting Stanford Home for Children, this annual fundraiser helps the 1,900 young people and family members that utilize our programs and services annually.

Our signature event has a new name this year--Vintage. However, this event remains the best wine sampling and gourmet fare Northern California has to offer, along with a rousing live auction.

Vintage is an unparalleled vehicle for having a great time and bidding on exceptional wine while funding a good cause. We look forward to sharing a special evening with you at this extraordinary event, and invite you to become a sponsor and support the young people of Sacramento who need your help.

title: Wine, Food, and Music Festival
description: This is one of Land Park's premier social events of the year, benefiting Congregation B'nai Israel. It's a gala fundraiser featuring the region's finest wineries, gourmet foods from Sacramento's top restaurants and caterers, live jazz, and our fantastic silent and live auctions. Once again, our auctioneer is David Sobon of David Sobon Auctions.

title: A Toast to Music!
description:
Taste regional wines, sample local cuisine, and enjoy live music by the Camellia Symphony at this food & wine benefit for the Camellia Symphony Orchestra.

Also enjoy:
-Wine Barrel Auctions: Featuring two barrels of Carvalho Family wine.
-Good Life Silent Auction: Weekend getaways, dining certificates, spa packages, artwork, jewelry, and more.
-Select Your Treasure Raffle

Major sponsor: Carvalho Family Winery.

title: Wine Blending & Tasting Experience: Sonoma
description: Help your mom have a Mother’s Day she won’t forget. More than just wine tasting, this trip will teach you how to mix wines to your own personal liking while enjoying the views of Conn Creek’s estate gardens and the Vaca Mountain Range. This annual Gala event includes a delicious full-course gourmet dinner, followed by a silent and live auction with plenty of wine, spirits, and endless hors d'oeuvres.

In addition, there is free parking, a wide screen TV, and drink specials. Wine tasting is coming soon.

title: Wine Tasting: Sonoma
description: Benziger Family Winery, the premier stop on this tour, has a rich heritage and a unique talent in biodynamic farming. You will not only taste several of their flavorful wines, but you will also have the chance to tour the vineyard and learn about their ground breaking farming practice. You’ll see some of the beauty of Sonoma County’s rolling hills as you travel to wineries such as Imagery Estates and Pelegrini Wineries.

title: City of Trees Food Tasting and Cultural Walking Tour
description:
Join us on a 3 hour guided culinary walking adventure. Learn what continues to make Sacramento a unique and delicious city, one taste at a time. Explore tree-lined side streets, Italianate mansions, historical neighborhood districts, and great restaurants all set within a beautiful Northern Sierras backdrop. The three-hour City of Trees Food Tasting & Cultural Walking Tour will let you see an insiders look at the can't-miss eateries and restaurants that only the locals are lucky enough to know about-until now.

By touring the city on foot, whether a visitor or a resident of Sacramento, uncover the hidden gem restaurants and establishments that you just don't see driving by. Get tidbits of Sacramento's history while tasting the scrumptious foods that make Sacramento's culinary scene a regional treasure. Learn where our state politicians and local foodies dine. You'll taste farm fresh ingredients that inspire local chefs. Explore our beautiful mansions and their architectural history. Our tour will take you on a gastronomic adventure off the beaten path.

Please join Councilman Steve Cohn and the City of Sacramento for a celebration of the most recent Sutter's Landing Park improvements that include a new basketball court, bocce courts, parking lot, and signage improvements, as well as the existing skate park and off-leash dog park.

Located just off Madison/Auburn in a beautifully wooded park. Plenty of places for picnics and family fun.

description: Time for the little ones to tap their feet to some fun musical tunes! That’s right, as part of a continuing monthly offering, kids ages 3 to 6 are invited to participate in a new and exciting “Music Fun With Music Matt” class designed to introduce them to enriching music, instruments, singing, and even some dancing, too. Parents are invited to enjoy the show as well or they can choose to explore all that the wellness resort has to offer (daily resort fees apply).

title: Stuart Little
description: Stuart Little is lively and fun and demonstrates the importance of loyalty, friendship, courage, and the appreciation of the world around us. A show for all ages, the play features colorful characters, creative scenery, and a host of children's favorite characters.

title: Walking Tour: Kids Meet the City: A Tour of California History Especially for Kids
description:
This tour is specially designed to serve as a fun and interactive way to introduce local history to students of all ages. This unique walk through downtown will explore the Gold Rush, the history and route of the famed Pony Express, John Sutter’s place in California history, and the Big Four of the railroad industry as well as offer an introduction to city government with a visit into City Council Chambers.

Make the most out of your tour with DSP's new Kids Meet The City: Activity Book. Download your free guide here!

Tour begins from the steps of City Hall.

title: The Silk Road Ensemble with Yo-Yo Ma
description: Cellist Yo-Yo Ma’s vision for the Silk Road Project first came together in 2000 at the Tanglewood Music Festival. Today, the Silk Road Ensemble is a collective of internationally renowned performers and composers from more than 20 countries, as well as a non-profit organization with a vision of connecting the world’s neighborhoods by bringing together artists and audiences around the globe. Each Ensemble member’s career illustrates a unique response to what is one of the artistic challenges of our times: nourishing global connections while maintaining the integrity of art rooted in an authentic tradition.

title: Hidden Meanings
description:
Discover worlds revealed through Elgar's "most emotional and deeply felt composition", the Cello Concerto in E minor, and Shostakovich's Symphony No. 5 in D minor; profound, expressive and gripping accounts of war, power, and love for country through the lens of the composer.

-Cello Concerto in E Minor - Edward Elgar

title: Lara Downes, Piano with David Sanford, Composer: Long Time Coming
description: Mondavi Center resident pianist Lara Downes introduces Long Time Coming, a new multimedia concert work inspired by Duke Ellington’s iconic 1943 work New World A Comin’. Featuring music from that suite and the world premiere of an original work for piano, live spoken word artist, and jazz ensemble by composer David Sanford, Long Time Coming reflects on the power of hope in troubled times, the impact of music on the collective consciousness, and the interrelationship of American music to the progression of civil rights.

title: Jewish Voices Concert with Rebecca Plack
description:
Local soprano Rebecca Plack will perform songs originally composed or performed by Jewish performers in a solo concert of classical, opera, traditional folk melodies, and Broadway show tunes titled, Jewish Voices: Songs from the Old World, Tunes from the New. Joined by Greg Mason on piano, Plack will highlight Jewish composers ranging from Gustav Mahler to George Gershwin to Stephen Sondheim. She will also showcase the work of Lotte Schöne, the reigning diva of the Berlin State Opera, until she was forced to flee Nazi Germany in 1933.

The first half of the program highlights songs that were composed, performed, and recorded by Jewish musicians before World War II. It begins with songs of Gustav Mahler (1860-1911) and continues with songs of Alexander Zemlinsky (1871-1942), a Viennese Jew whose lyrically beautiful compositions are virtually unknown today. The first half concludes with repertoire of soprano Lotte Schöne (1891-1977).

The concert’s second half features the works of Jewish lyricists and composers who emigrated to America and Israel after the war. These include generations of writers for the American musical theater, such as George Gershwin, Dorothy Fields, and Stephen Sondheim whose Broadway songs are now well-known theatrical standards. The program concludes with Hebrew and Yiddish songs.

With her vibrant voice and her musical knowledge, Plack has performed across the United States, Canada, and Europe. She has given solo recitals for the International Great Romantics Festival in Hamilton, Canada, the ATERForum Festival in Ferrara, Italy, and the Franz Liszt Museum in Budapest. Locally, she has sung at the Mondavi Center for the Performing Arts, the Sacramento Opera, and the Chamber Music Society of Sacramento. Rebecca recently joined the faculty at the San Francisco Conservatory of Music, where she did postgraduate work. She holds degrees in musicology and voice from Princeton University, Manhattan School of Music, and Cornell University. Plack maintains private voice studios in Sacramento and Davis.

The concert will be held at the Center at Twenty-Three Hundred, Sacramento’s newest multi-use venue with state-of-the-art lighting and sound. The concert will help raise funds for the purchase of a new grand piano for the Center at Twenty-Three Hundred and benefit Mosaic Law Congregation’s general fund.

title: China Philharmonic Orchestra
description:
The influential Classical magazine Gramophone pegged the China Philharmonic Orchestra as one of the world’s up-and-coming orchestras in 2010. “In some ways, the China Philharmonic is something of a baby, in others, a wise old sage,” wrote Gramophone. “It was established only in May 2000, but from the ashes of the old China Broadcasting Symphony Orchestra. Its artistic director, Long Yu, is one of the country’s foremost conductors and a very fine technician who arguably brought new standards of orchestral playing to China.” Maestro Yu, who appeared with the Shanghai Symphony Orchestra in the 2009-2010 Mondavi Center Season, leads these talented musicians in a program of treasured favorites and new discoveries.

title: Bryan Adams: Bare Bones Tour
description:
Bryan Adams is a Canadian rock singer-songwriter, guitarist, bassist, producer, and photographer. Adams has won dozens of awards and nominations, including 20 Juno Awards among 56 nominations. He has also had 15 Grammy Award nominations including a win for Best Song Written Specifically for a Motion Picture or Television in 1992. He has also won MTV, ASCAP, and American Music awards. In addition, he has won two Ivor Novello Awards for song composition and has been nominated for several Golden Globe Awards and three times for Academy Awards for his songwriting for films.

The Crest Lounge will be open and selling beer and wine to those 21 and older.

title: Sacramento State Faculty Concert

title: Max Raabe & Palast Orchester
description: Slick, nostalgic, and unmistakably modern, Berlin-based Max Raabe & Palast Orchester bring Weimar-era cabaret to life, channeling the high style and musical glory of the 1920s and 1930s with uncanny precision, drama, and humor. Playing a mix of German and American standards, the elegant, ironic Raabe and his talented 12-piece band provide an unparalleled, unexpected evening’s entertainment.

title: Béla Fleck, Zakir Hussain, and Edgar Meyer
description: Three masterful genre-benders and the leading virtuosos on their instruments, Béla Fleck (banjo), Zakir Hussain (tabla), and Edgar Meyer (bass) move with ease among the worlds of classical, bluegrass, jazz, and world music. Together these limitless creators and composers cross musical boundaries, creating what can only be described as an enthralling musical hybrid.

title: Interpol
description:
Although formed during the late '90s, Interpol rose to international attention in 2002 as part of New York City's post-punk revival. The group took its cues from Joy Division and the Chameleons, fashioning a darkly atmospheric sound helmed by intricate guitars and Paul Banks' somber baritone.

Interpol also had a striking visual presence marked by the members' fondness for suits, which only strengthened their stately, British-influenced appeal. Nevertheless, the band remained rooted in America, where guitarist Daniel Kessler and drummer Greg Drudy first struck up a musical partnership while attending New York University. Carlos Dengler, another NYU student who had previously played guitar, joined as the group's bassist--and by sheer coincidence, Kessler later bumped into Paul Banks, a guitarist/vocalist whom Kessler had spent time with in France.

Having settled on an initial lineup, Interpol became a fully active band in 1998 and began issuing a series of 8-track recordings. After the band's first gigs in early 2000, Drudy vacated his position and was replaced by drummer Sam Fogarino.

Also performing:
School of Seven Bells

description: Sacramento State’s Jazz Ensembles, with guest saxophonist Donny McCaslin, will perform as part of the University’s annual Festival of the Arts.

title: Furlough Friday Concert with Citywater
description: Citywater is a fresh new ensemble on the California music scene. Dedicated to the creation and performance of exciting new works by contemporary composers, its mission is performance without boundaries and education without alienation. Citywater invites audiences to come challenge their expectations of what new music can be.

title: Festival of the Arts: New Millennium Concert Series: Pacific Guitar Ensemble
description: The Pacific Guitar Ensemble will perform. The group has a wide repertoire that includes Sergio Assad and Bach. The concert is part of the University’s New Millennium Music Series and Festival of the Arts.

title: Gohar Vardanyan and Jesse McCann Performances
description:
Gohar Vardanyan and Jesse McCann cap off the West Coast Guitar Society’s Roundtable with solo performances. Armenian guitarist Gohar Vardanyan holds a Master of Music Degree from The Juilliard School where she studied with Sharon Isbin and a Bachelor of Music degree from the Peabody Conservatory of Music where she studied with Manuel Barrueco. She is also an alumna of the Aspen Music Festival and School.

Ms. Vardanyan has performed for the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, DC, New England, and Sierra Nevada Guitar Societies, Guitar Masters Series at the Interlochen Guitar Festival, Juilliard's Wednesday's @1 Series, Peabody's Thursday Noon series, with the Juilliard Opera Center and as a soloist with the Great Lakes Chamber Orchestra. She has been a Guest Artist for Baltimore Classical Guitar Society's Guitar Day and a master class faculty at the Interlochen Guitar Festival and Workshop.

Jesse McCann, from Portland, Oregon, studied with Miroslav Loncar and Natasha Klasinc. Upon receiving his Bachelor of Music, he moved to Portland in 2002. Soon thereafter he enrolled at Portland State University, where he completed his Master of Music under the direction of Bryan Johanson. In addition to being a top prize solo guitarist, he led two award-winning guitar trios and is currently a member of the Oregon Guitar Quartet.

description:

title: Schola Cantorum: Lenten Choral Mysteries
description:
Donald Kendrick will conduct Sacred Heart's Schola Cantorum in a special Palm Sunday Lenten Choral Mysteries performance of Maurice Duruflé's powerful Requiem. Organist Stephen Janzen will accompany Schola, who will be joined by soloists Monica Barnes, mezzo and Daniel Yoder, baritone.

The program in the rich acoustics of Sacred Heart Church will also include works by contemporary English composer/organist David Briggs, Michael McGlynn, Rudi Tas, Mark Jennings, Zdenek Lukas, and Gilbert Martin.

Duruflé, a 20th century French virtuoso organist in Paris, based his 1947 Requiem, known for its subtle rhythms and fluid lines, on Gregorian chant. The work is conceived as a whole with very few moments of repose; there is always a sense of movement, of continuing for eternity. According to conductor Donald Kendrick, "Like the requiems of Brahms and Fauré, Duruflé chose to adhere closely to the central themes of the requiem mass: peace, light, hope, and rest. The purity, peacefulness, and unending nature of the final chords are a masterful summary of this Requiem seeking peace and eternal rest. The unresolved tones eloquently depict the flight of the soul to paradise."

Established in 1992, Schola Cantorum has recorded eight CDs and has appeared in concert throughout the West Coast and in England, Spain, Canada, and Austria. They performed at the Vatican for Pope Benedict during their 2007 concert tour to Italy. Schola plans to celebrate their 20th anniversary in 2012 with a tour to France (Paris and Provence).

A New Song will feature Psalms arranged by Srul Irving Glick, modern and uplifting Kyries, and other soul-stirring cries of the heart from James MacMillan, Craig Hella Johnson, Dolly Parton, and Annie Lennox. Join as HuskyShows brings flamenco guitarist extraordinaire, Jesse Cook and the pulsating sounds of The Rumba Foundation to the newly inaugurated Three Stages at Folsom Lake College.
