The Sacramento Opera has canceled their remaining productions for the 2010-11 season as of December 10, 2010. Single ticket purchasers may obtain a full refund at place of purchase during regular business hours; season subcribers should call the Opera for more information at (916) 737-1000.

For lovers of “film noir,” American composer Stephen Paulus brings to life an old Hollywood classic with his dramatic and lyrical style. Set in California, the story is of a drifter, Frank, who stops at a rural diner for a meal and ends up working there. The diner is operated by the young and beautiful Cora, with whom he has a steamy affair. Cora and Frank scheme to murder her elder husband Nick, in order to start a new life together. The contemporary styled orchestration, strongly influenced by jazz, makes it a rare and fresh experience that can be enjoyed by both the opera newcomer and seasoned patron. Riveting theater at its finest.

Music by Stephen Paulus. Sung in English with English supertitles. Mature content.

title: A Jazzy Moms' Affair featuring vocalist Virginia Ayers-Dawson
description: Mothers Day Jazz Show featuring vocalist Virginia Ayers-Dawson with The Gents of Jazz: Jimmy Malone (piano), Jimmy Robinson (drums), Bob Bell (bass), and Garrett Perkins (saxophone)--Sacramento's legendary jazz players.
venue: JB's Lounge @ the Red Lion Inn

title: Zac Brown Band
description:
Two-time Grammy Award winners Zac Brown Band are back on the road to super serve fans with their southern-flavored rock and decadent five-sense enticing concert experience with stops at amphitheaters and stadiums across the U.S., including a stop at Raley Field.

Following up their 2010 Grammy win for Best New Artist and multiple "Entertainer of the Year" nods in 2010 (ACM & CMA), Zac Brown Band has sold out shows across the country and scored six consecutive No. 1 singles on the radio. Their latest album, You Get What You Give (Atlantic/Southern Ground) debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and features guest appearances by Alan Jackson and Jimmy Buffett.

New on the scene is "Cookie," the band's tractor-trailer sized, custom-built, mobile commercial kitchen that recently debuted under the helm of Executive Chef Rusty Hamlin and will bring a host of southern delicacies at headlining shows. Zac Brown and Chef Rusty will host their pre-show eat-and-greets, where fans get the full Zac Brown Band experience--an opportunity to hang out with the band and sample Southern Ground grub.

title: Four Concerts: Folsom Lake College Music Department
description:
Chaired by Larry Metcalf, these concerts provide capstone performance experiences for musicians and vocalists.

Schedule:
-Wed, 7pm: College Choir: An exciting evening of choral music chosen from the traditional, contemporary, and ethnic repertoires.
-Fri, 7pm: Jazz Choir: An evening of solo and ensemble performances of vocal jazz.
-Fri, 10pm: Jazz After Dark: FLC Afro-Cuban Funk Band
-Sat, Noon: Simulcast: Going Global: ACF launches its first multi-national performance, simulcast in multiple locations around the globe. To accommodate world-wide time-zone considerations, please note start time

title: The Great American Songbook II: Hay Fever!
description: The American River Chorus is producing its second annual performance for this dynamic group. Formed in January 2010, this chorus has grown from 10 members to 93 members in only 14 months. The chorus has already impressed members of the a capella community, taking first place in the recent Far Western District, Northern California Division chorus contest. In addition to the Sacramento area, members travel from as far away as Palo Alto, Merced, Chico, and even Reno to be a part of this exciting new ensemble. Members’ ages range from 16 to 75, many of whom are students at local Sacramento colleges. Come see them perform The Great American Songbook II: Hay Fever!

title: Folsom Symphony: Land That I Love
description:
Founded in 2004 under the direction of Maestro Michael Neumann, the Folsom Symphony remains committed to the exciting and satisfying repertoire that reflects the brilliance—and enjoyability—of the classics.

Their program Land That I Love contains with selections from Bernstein, Grofe, Sousa, Horner, Morricone, and others.

title: Sail Away: Spring Concert
description: Sacramento Children's Chorus presents their spring concert, Sail Away. The concert will feature all five choirs with music from the Paific Rim and guest dancers with the group Sinag-tala.

title: That’s Entertainment: Broadway in Review: Sierra Community Chorus
description: The acclaimed 60-member chorus, under the direction of Lorin Miller, performs an evening of celebrated favorites of the American musical theater.

title: Homegrown Sacramento: Broadway Favorites
description:
The best of Broadway comes to you! Live from Sacramento, Tony award-winning Broadway star Faith Prince debuts with her hometown orchestra, singing favorites from Broadway including Frank Loesser's "Adelaide's Lament" from Guys and Dolls, Stephen Sondheim's "The Ladies Who Lunch" from the musical Company, and the other heartwarming sets of jazz standards. Emerging young Sacramento star and first place winner of the Philharmonic's 2009-2010 Classical Concerto Competition, Ray Anthony Trujillo, also performs with orchestra, playing a romantic-era treasure, Henryk Wieniawski's Violin Concerto No. 2 in D minor.

Selections from Broadway Favorites

Michael Morgan - conductor
Faith Prince - voice (SPO debut)
Ray Anthony Trujillo - Violin

title: Sacramento Guitar Society: Muriel Anderson & Tierra Negra
description:
Muriel Anderson and Germany’s guitar duo Tierra Negra (longtime proponents of Flamenco Nuevo) join forces: the concert begins with separate performances, then after intermission they combine for a fiery finale. A benefit for the Sacramento Guitar Society

“Muriel Anderson… has justifiably gained a reputation as one of the world’s best and, most versatile, guitar instrumentalists.” Chicago Tribune

title: Sacramento Philharmonic Orchestra: Broadway Favorites
description:
Discover our region’s acclaimed professional orchestra, the Sacramento Philharmonic, under the baton of Maestro Michael Morgan in two powerful concerts of masterpieces and favorites. “An extraordinary evening of great music” (Sacramento Gazette)

Their program Broadway Favorites features guest artist Faith Prince.

“The Sacramento Philharmonic dazzled the audience.” SF Examiner

title: Jason Bonham's Led Zeppelin Experience
description: Jason Bonham, who played with the surviving members of Led Zeppelin at the band's London O2 Arena reunion show in 2007, decided to put together his own tribute to his late dad after seeing the show Rain, a Tribute to the Beatles. Bonham has joined forces with Annerin Productions--the critically acclaimed producers of both Rain and The Pink Floyd Experience--to create a visual and auditory spectacle. A high-tech sound system and light show will accompany Bonham's performance, and giant screens will project home movies and photos, as well as art designs to compliment the music.

title: Walk 'N Rock featuring Kiss
description:
Raley Field will host Walk 'N Rock For Kids featuring Kiss. Kiss is regarded as one of the most influential rock and roll bands of all-time. Their career milestones are staggering. Kiss holds honors as one of America's top gold record champions, recording 37 albums over 36 years selling over 100 million albums worldwide.

Over thirty years of record-breaking tours around the globe include high-profile appearances at Super Bowl XXXIII, the 2002 Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City, the 2005 Rockin' The Corps concert dedicated to our troops in Iraq and Afghanistan, and most recently, the 2009 American Idols Finale before thirty million views.

The Kiss legacy continues to grow, generation after generation, transcending age, race, and creed. The unparalleled devotion and loyalty of the Kiss Army to the "Hottest Band in the World" is a striking testament to the band's unbreakable bond with its fans.

title: [re] generation: TAIKOPROJECT
description:
The first American participant in—and winner of—The Tokyo International Taiko Contest, TAIKOPROJECT presents an electrifying evolution of an ancient tradition.

“A celebration of taiko history in America.” (Sacramento Bee)

“This ain’t your mama’s taiko; it may be your hip younger cousin’s” (LA Weekly)

title: Alexander String Quartet
description:
Program:
Beethoven: String Quartet in A Minor, Op. 132
Beethoven: String Quartet in F Major, Op. 135

The acclaimed Alexander String Quartet brings its complete cycle of Beethoven’s string quartets to a close with four shows in the 2010–2011 season. On the cusp of its 30th anniversary, the Quartet has played in the major music capitals of four continents, securing its place among the world’s premier ensembles. Widely admired for its interpretations of Beethoven, Mozart, and Shostakovich, the Quartet has also established itself as an important advocate of new music through more than 25 commissions and numerous premiere performances.

During the matinee, renowned musicologist, author, and composer Robert Greenberg provides commentary throughout the concert.

title: Furlough Friday Concert with Citywater
description: Citywater is a fresh new ensemble on the California music scene. Dedicated to the creation and performance of exciting new works by contemporary composers, its mission is performance without boundaries and education without alienation. Citywater invites audiences to come challenge their expectations of what new music can be.

title: The New Christy Minstrels Benefit Concert
description:
Grammy award winning folk giants, The New Christy Minstrels, under the direction of the charming and humorous Randy Sparks, will be back with us again this year. Enjoy your favorite folk songs performed since 1961 by NCM. Relive old memories or make new ones as you get an education in the history of American Folk Tradition.

The proceeds will be split between the Fair Oaks Theatre Festival building fund and the New Christy Minstrel Foundation, which provides free concerts and sheet music to public schools.

title: Sade with Special Guest John Legend
description:
Sade will perform songs from their collection of timeless hits including songs from their critically acclaimed album, Soldier of Love, which secured the # 1 album spot upon its release in February. Selling over a million copies to-date, Soldier of Love spent three weeks in the number one spot taking its rightful place among the collection of iconic Sade albums.

Sade will perform over 50 concerts in top arenas across North America, in an effort to reach her vast and loyal fan base. Their classic sound set to haunting, unmistakable vocals creates the most intimate of concert experiences in a way that only an unforgettable Sade performance can. Sade performed for more than 1,000,000 fans during her last tour in 2001.

Also performing:
John Legend

title: Sugarland
description:
International super duo Sugarland will continue their highly-successful 2010 The Incredible Machine Tour into 2011 and return to the road this spring with special guest Sara Bareilles.

Sugarland has sold over 9 million records and achieved seven #1 singles since exploding onto the music scene in '04 with Twice The Speed Of Life ("Baby Girl"/"Something More"). Enjoy the Ride ("Want To"/"Settlin'"/"Stay") quickly followed in '06 and their third studio album Love On The Inside ("It Happens"/"Love"/"All I Want To Do"/"Already Gone") in July '08, which skyrocketed them to superstardom, drawing fans from all genres and critics abroad. Sugarland is credited with co-writing all tracks from all three albums and co-producing the last two.

title: Sunday Circus
description: Each and every Sunday M!X Downtown parties like Charlie! No one can beat Sunday Circus' drink specials, $3 you-call-list (up to $10 value), $4 vodka-redbulls, and $4 Jack & Cokes! DJ Gabe Xavier spins hip hop & dance remixes all night. Casual dress code.

title: Bunnies and Bottles
description: April showers brings May flowers--even better--this year, April will host Easter, one of The Park Ultra Lounge's favorite holidays! What's better than a hot bunny stashing away goodies? Join The Park and Nick Willrich as they give away bunny ears, host a $500 best bunny costume contest, and hide easter eggs in hard to find places filled with the ultimate prizes! This event will be crazy!

title: DJ Spider
description:
The Park Ultra Lounge brings back the one and only DJ Spider for an exclusive pre-Easter massive with DJ Peeti V.

About Spider: Whether you’re rocking out to his set at an LA hotspot or listening to one of his mixtapes, the evolution of DJ Spider is apparent. Though his roots stem from a deep love for hip-hop, Spider has cultivated his sound to include an eclectic mix of cuts that transgress nearly every genre of music. He’s been known to take timeless hits such as “Sexual Healing” by Marvin Gaye, mix in the newest club-banger, and blend into an Aretha Franklin classic. It is this variety and originality that makes Spider one of the most coveted DJs across the globe today.

title: Bunny Hop
description: Bunny Hop with M!X Downtown Easter Sunday! Sunday Circus takes no days off when it comes to partying. M!X & DJ Gabe Xavier host the best industry night it town! Enjoy $3 you-call-it drinks (up to a $10 value) and the best vibe in Sacramento!

title: Cinco de Mayo at The Park
description: Ole! Ole! Ole! The Tres Amigos are back!! Rock-N-Rhyme comes roaring in for Cinco de Mayo at The Park. Hosted by the amazing and talent MC Nick Willrich the gang is all together for a chest-pounding, ground-shaking dance party of epic proportion! Tequila and Margarita specials flowing from the bar while the patio heats up with a spicy latin twist! Free guest list hosted by Nick Willrich, Sean Ruiz, and Morgan Ramos.

title: Sacramento Ballet: Icons & Innovators
description:
One of California’s foremost dance companies, the Sacramento Ballet makes its Three Stages debut as part of their 2010-11 season, Coloring Outside the Lines. From creative virtuosity to pure, unadulterated fun — “joyous, life-affirming, graceful and athletic…” (Sacramento Bee)—seeing one performance will inspire you to see all three.

Icons and Innovators features Lila York's Celts, an athletic tour-de-force set to traditional Irish music. Also on the program is Ron Cunningham's Bolero and George Balanchine's The Four Temperaments.

“Nothing stuffy here—Sacramento Ballet opens the windows and gives local dance a breath of fresh air.” -Sacramento News & Review

title: Mystery Spot
description: California Stage premiers Mystery Spot, an award-winning comedy. Dingo, a regular ol' guy from Oroville, gets accepted to UC Santa Cruz where he becomes a Women's Studies major so he can pursue his hobby of chasing around girls. To fund his womanizing, he gets a job at the Santa Cruz Mystery Spot, where nothing is as it seems.

title: Circle Mirror Transformation
description:
In a community-center drama class, four lost souls act out hilarity, sadness, desperation, and hope. But are they really acting?

“An absolute feast! It’s the kind of unheralded gem that sends people into the streets babbling and bright-eyed with the desire to spread the word.” -New York Times.

Sacramento businesses support B Street Theatre. Bring your ticket stub to any restaurant partner for special discounts!

title: The Skin of Our Teeth
description:
The Falcon's Eye Theatre presents The Skin of Our Teeth. A groundbreaking satiric fantasy, Thornton Wilder’s Pulitzer Prize-winning allegory follows the extraordinary Antrobus family through the ages.

This performance takes place in the Falcon's Eye Theatre.

title: Iolanthe
description:
Fairies. Sometimes clumsy, sometimes delicate, but all want to help their fellow half-fairy, Strephon (Chris Baad), get hitched to the woman he loves: Phyllis (Carley Neill). This is complicated by several issues: Strephon's most ardent supporter is his fairy mother, Iolanthe (Sara Haugland), who was banished by the Fairy Queen (Katie Daley) for marrying Strephon's mortal father, the Lord Chancellor (Mike Baad), so she can't readily help his case. Furthermore, the Chancellor is conflicted because Phyllis is a ward of his court and wants to marry her himself. On top of that, the whole house of Peers are in love with beautiful Phyllis. Lord Tolloller (Robert Vann) and Lord Mountararat (Bob Schroeder) convince the Chancellor that it really would be okay if he sought Phyllis's hand in marriage.

To help Strephon's case, the fairies put him into Parliament, and force all the other M.P.'s to pass his bills. A sentry guard (Tim Powers) comments on how dull and unthinking the whole Parliament is. But the whole thing comes to a head when Iolanthe reveals herself to the Chancellorwho had thought her dead, knowing nothing of her banishment. In the end, it seems the best course of action is for all the members of Parliament to marry fairies.

As Lord Mountararat says, "This is what comes of women interfering with politics."

This performance is fully staged, with a live orchestra.

title: Festival of the Arts: Sacramento Dance Sampler
description:
The Sacramento Dance Sampler presents local professional dance companies in two evenings of performances. Presenting Paufve Dance, Dangerous Lorraines Dance Theater, CORE Dance Collective, Linda Bair Dance Company, Sacramento/Black Art of Dance, Red Bucket Dance Company, E:motion Dance Ensemble, and L. Bayne Performance Project.

This performance is part of the Festival of the Arts.

title: Festival of the Arts: Sacramento Dance Sampler
description:
The Sacramento Dance Sampler presents local professional dance companies in two evenings of performances. Presenting Paufve Dance, Dangerous Lorraines Dance Theater, CORE Dance Collective, Linda Bair Dance Company, Sacramento/Black Art of Dance, Red Bucket Dance Company, E:motion Dance Ensemble, and L. Bayne Performance Project.

This performance is part of the Festival of the Arts.

title: Pacific Island Competition Sacramento (PICS)
description:
Na Maka is hosting its 1st Annual Pacific Island Competition Sacramento (PICS), the only Hula and ‘Ori Tahiti competition held in Sacramento. The spirit of the Hawaiian and Tahitian cultures will come alive in our State Capital. There will be a variety of food and vendor booths. Come and join us for a wonderful day in paradise.

Mahalo and Mauruuruu Roa.

title: Sherlock Holmes & The Case of the Jersey Lily
description:
Beautiful actress Lillie Langtry is seeking help from the brilliant detective Sherlock Holmes in a small matter involving blackmail, some missing jewels, and the royal family. Our hero gets some help from his sidekick, Watson, and the famous Oscar Wilde as the evil Professor Moriarty tries yet again to foil the day.

Director: Warren Harrison

title: Festival of the Arts: Die Fledermaus
description:
Sacramento State’s Opera Theatre has set Johann Strauss’ Die Fledermaus in the 1970s.

The performances are part of the University’s annual Festival of the Arts.

title: The Power of Words
description: The Power of Words is a composition of scenes, monologues, and poetry. This show is about the Power of Words and how they affect people's lives, whether it be in a positive or a negative way. This show is meant to get people to be more aware of what you say to people on a day to day basis. It is also focused around the LGBT community and the struggles this community has with harassment. Not only is it an eye opener, it's a benefit. Proceeds to benefit the Lambda Players Theatre and the homeless LGBTQ youth.

title: Inside the Director’s Studio: A Russian Voice: Viktor Kabaniaev
description: Welcome back Viktor Kabaniaev, as he charms us once again with his wry Russian humor filtered though his thoroughly distinctive creativity. Enjoy Viktor’s unique choreographic style as he guides us through the journey of recreating one of his most popular works for a Sacramento Modern Masters premiere.

title: Awake My Soul: 4th Season Closing Performance
description: Awake My Soul is the closing performance of CORE's 4th season. It features "Silent Noise," the first commissioned dance piece by the Crocker Art Museum and inspired by the work of artist Gottfried Helnwein, and "After the Storm," an uplifting new piece set to the innovative music of Mumford & Sons.

title: The Vagina Monologues
description:
The Vagina Monologues is an episodic play written by Eve Ensler and is made up of monologues read by a number of women. Every monologue relates to the vagina, and a recurring theme throughout the piece is the vagina as a tool of female empowerment and the ultimate embodiment of individuality.

Come help support our local community--90% of the event proceeds (including ticket sales, donations, proceeds from the Silent Auction, and advertisements in the printed program) will benefit Sacramento Women Take Back the Night, WEAVE, and My Sister’s House. The remaining 10% will benefit the. 2011 V-Day Spotlight Campaign to support the women and girls of Haiti.

title: Measure for Measure
description: One of Shakespeare’s most original works is an exploration of the extremities of love and lust. Set in a “Vienna Gone Wild,” Duke Vincentio hatches a wild plot to restore order to his city, but not all the players in the game are as they seem. Specifically double cast with 7 players, so that every actor portrays both hero and villain, comedian and tragedian, Measure for Measure is not to be missed.

title: Don't Dress for Dinner
description:
You'll have fun trying to figure out who's sleeping with whom in this hilarious French farce about adultery and gourmet cooking!

In a converted farmhouse, Bernard is hoping to entertain his chic, Parisian mistress for the weekend. He has arranged for a cordon bleu cook to furnish the gourmet delights, is in the process of packing his wife off to her mother, and has even invited along his best friend as a suitable alibi. Seemingly foolproof, what could possibly go wrong...?

title: Othello
description: One of Shakespeare’s four great tragedies, this play explores the fine line between Othello’s passionate love and dangerous jealousy, while tangling with issues of race, gender, sex, marriage, hate, manipulation, and identity.

title: El Dorado Musical Theatre: Anything Goes
description:
The S.S. American, sailing from New York to England, carries an unusual group of passengers. Included amongst them are Public Enemy #13 (Moonface Martin), who is disguised as a minister, his friend and cohort (Bonnie), a wealthy debutante and her mother (Hope and Evangeline Harcourt), a nightclub singer and evangelist (Reno Sweeney), her backup singers and dancers (The Angels), and a wealthy New York businessman and his stowaway assistant (Elisha Witney and Billy Crocker).

It turns out that Hope is Billy's long-lost love. Unfortunately, she is now engaged to a wealthy Englishman, Lord Evelyn Oakleigh. After a series of comedic happenings, Billy manages to win back Hope. Meanwhile, Billy's friend, Reno, manages to win Lord Evelyn. All this happens while Moonface Martin attempts to escape the law and Hope's mother strives to maintain her social status. A series of comical mistaken identities develop as the passengers and crew sing, tap, and dance their way across the Atlantic to some of Cole Porter’s most wonderful songs! It’s big fun and a lot of laughs, with a surprise twist at the end!

Music and Lyrics by Cole Porter. Book by Guy Bolton, P.G. Wodehouse, Howard Lindsay and Russell Crouse. Director/Choreographer: Debbie Wilson. Vocal Director: Jennifer Martin. Costumer: Christine Martorana.

title: Nunsense
description: Nunsense is winner of four Outer Critics Circle Awards including Best Off Broadway Musical in its original New York production. The show is a fundraiser put on by the Little Sisters of Hoboken to raise money to bury sisters accidentally poisoned by the convent cook, Sister Julia (Child of God). Updated with new jokes, additional lyrics, two new arrangements, and a brand new song, this zany musical is a hit wherever it plays.

title: Lucinda Childs: DANCE
description: Lucinda Childs began her career as choreographer and performer in 1963 as an original member of the Judson Dance Theater in New York. After forming her own dance company in 1973, Childs embarked on a number of notable collaborations with major composers, the first of which was DANCE (1979), with music by Philip Glass and film and decor by visual artist Sol LeWitt. DANCE was revived in 2009, and this tour provides a rare chance to experience a true artistic masterwork.

title: Evening of Dance: Mosaic Dance Company
description: From ballet to jazz, hip-hop, contemporary dance, and ethnic forms, Folsom Lake College’s student company is a “mosaic” of dancers and choreographers, launching the next generation of dance artists.

title: Je'Caryous Johnson's Marriage Material
description:
Esteemed lawyer Koren Lyles has been known to slay hearts, but what happens when each of her past romantic casualties end up at a premarital weekend retreat all together? It's a date with disaster!

Koren has it all and unfortunately far more than she bargained for. Life was good, she was up for partner, and her loving boyfriend, Joey Harris, proposes marriage. Then her life changes when her old flame, Cameron, who is also her boss, professes he wants to leave his wife for her. Not knowing how to deal with him, she let Joey persuade her into going to a couples retreat to see if they are ready for marriage. Everything comes tumbling down when her ex fiance, Michael, and her best friend, Jackie, are there too... engaged! The retreat gets heated when she is forced to deal with her past, Cameron coming to claim her, and skeletons that come out of the closet between her and Joey. The weekend turns into a whirlwind as emotions erupt, perceived friendships become fake, secrets are shouted, and old love goes to war with new love!

title: Senior Dance Concert
description: Directed by Lorelei Bayne, this dance concert features original choreography by the students and represents the culminating experiences of graduating dance majors. Seniors choreographers are responsible for every aspect of the production beginning with open auditions, lighting, costumes & publicity.

title: Bellydance Superstars: Bombay Bellywood
description: Bombay Bellywood stars the Bellydance Superstars. There are now few in the world of Bellydance who have not been affected by the advent of the Bellydance Superstars and the first concerted effort to take this ancient art form into the mainstream of international entertainment up there along with ballet and shows like Riverdance. It has been a rocky road in many respects and many disbelievers had to be converted both in the established world of bellydance as well as the mainstream dance arts. By 2009 the BDSS, had performed concerts in 20 countries to well over a million people in over 600 shows including the biggest shows ever in the history of bellydance anywhere. Meanwhile when not touring BDSS stars have taught workshops in the four corners of the globe adding many more countries to the BDSS list.

title: The Moby-Dick Variations
description: Devised and directed by John Zibell, this new work is inspired by Herman Melville’s novel. It is about perspectives and is a poly-cultural, poly-theistic, poly-rhythmic, poly-vocal, non-linear exploration of being in the universe. Set in the here and now it investigates the disappearance of the human animal from the natural landscape.

title: Sacramento Raks! Belly Dance Cabaret Gala Show
description:
Get ready for Sacramento's most spectacular belly dance show yet! Sacramento Raks! Belly Dance Cabaret is a staged show featuring featuring the multi-award winning AHAVA from the Bay Area, Adriane and the Henna and Kohl Dance Company, Badia, Daleela, Deeta, Manasa, Mychelle, Nabeela El Shalimar, Nyla Crystal, Sawako Ama, Selayma Anan, Tasha, Vahana, and more. Top that off with the live acoustic Middle Eastern music of Flowers of the Nile!!

Middle Eastern food will be available for purchase.

title: Corazón de México: Compañía Mazatlán: Bellas Artes
description: Corazón de México is one of California’s most esteemed Mexican folkdance companies. Under the artistic direction of Steven Valencia, 35 exceptional dancers, mariachis, and other musicians present a lively and passionate rendition of Mexican culture, both past and present. For lovers of fine ballet folklórico dance, the “Corazón de México” (“Heart of Mexico”) is colorful and creative, featuring indigenous and folkloric dance costumes and traditions, with accents on their award–winning pieces performed in international competitions.

title: Modern Masters
description: Experience the intrepid exploration of bold new voices in American dance. The brightest rising stars of cutting edge creativity stage provocative works of daring imagination. Now in three great locations…the Company brings the dance to you!

title: Modern Masters
description: Experience the intrepid exploration of bold new voices in American dance. The brightest rising stars of cutting edge creativity stage provocative works of daring imagination. Now in three great locations…the Company brings the dance to you!

title: Sacramento Ballet: Modern Masters
description: Experience the intrepid exploration of bold new voices in American dance. The brightest rising stars of cutting edge creativity stage provocative works of daring imagination. Now in three great locations…the Company brings the dance to you!

title: Jesus Hopped the A Train
description: When he was a child, Angel Cruz believed that Jesus hopped the 'A' train to save his life. Now, he is in 23-hour lockdown on Rikers Island, awaiting trial for killing a religious cult leader who got a grip on his best friend. His fellow inmate, Lucius, is a serial killer on death row who has found Christianity. He tries to convince Angel that God can save him; meanwhile, Angel’s lawyer says she can get him acquitted. What is the real way to salvation, and how is it defined?
venue: Capital Stage - Aboard the Riverboat Delta King

title: Antigone by Jean Anouilh
description:
Based on Sophocles’ classic, Anouilh’s Antigone focuses on the showdown between King Creon and his niece, Antigone, when she defies his order to prohibit the burial of her brother after a brutal civil war. Seen through the prism of our current time, Antigone raises a crucial question--when the towers of society/politics/finance are crumbling around us, do we fight for what works even if that’s wrong or do we fight for what’s right even if that means our end? Integrity versus compromise, individual versus the state, divine law versus human law--Antigone rips into these timeless issues and iconic characters.

Directed by Lisa Thew and starring Kelley Ogden and Patrick Murphy.

title: An Adult Evening of Shel Silverstein
description:
Welcome to the darkly comic world of Shel Silverstein, a world where nothing is as it seems and where the most innocent conversation can turn menacing in an instant.

A bag lady in training? 60 words for boobs? Auctioning of a woman at her own request? A dead pony for a birthday present? The punishment for not reading the fine print?

Eight talented actors in ten imaginative scenes

Directed by Benjamin T. Ismail. Starring: Jouni Kirjola, Ally Krumm, Jeffrey Lloyd Heatherly, Jes Gonzales, Laura White, Heather Judkins, Joelle Wirth, Ben Miller.

title: Hurly Burly
description: Egos run rampant--as a matter of fact so do Ids--in David Rabe’s linguistic rollercoaster ride through 1980s Hollywood. Centering on the lives of four drug crazed, mysoginistic L.A. bachelors and the women they…don’t understand at all; and displaying a virtuoso command of the modern English language, Rabe delivers a remarkable morality tale on the pitfalls of sex, drugs, and showbiz.

title: Dearly Departed
description:
Meet the Bible Belt kin of Bud Turpin. They've got a funeral to plan and--between the feuds, marital flings, and Macaroni and Ham Loaf Surprise--it may escalate into a multiple-coffin memorial service. By the time the Turpins sort through the hangovers, money problems, and headstone engraving options, they've learned that coping with life's losses can turn out to be drop-dead funny.

Director: Dean Shellenberger

title: Passengers
description:
Four actors play seventeen characters in eight short scenes varying from comedic to poignant in this play set in a bus station. Passengers is a character-driving play with challenging transitions ranging from comedic to poignant.

Some strong language.

title: From Orphan to Queen: The Story of Esther, A Musical
description: One Way Productions introduces an original new musical based on the Book of Esther. Travel to Persia and meet King Xerxes and his royal court who insist Queen Vashti must pay for her rebellion. Next, the search then begins for a new Queen of Persia. Who will win the Kings heart? The King now lonely and pre-occupied with his inner troubles relies heavily on his prime minister, Haman. But what happens when Haman suggests the destruction of all Jews? Will the Hebrew nation survive? Who will save this nation from genocide? Come join us and discover the beauty and gift of providence, and the one whose courage is still celebrated today.

title: Annie
description:
Spunky Annie brings joy to her fellow orphanage mates, though they are all kept virtually hostage by the mean and spiteful Miss Hannigan. Annie, meanwhile, meets the millionaire, Daddy Warbucks, bringing joy into his life as well. Miss Hannigan plots evil things but is thwarted. Annie continues to bring joy to everyone, including the mutt, Sandy, and FDR himself.

Directed by Bob Irvin. Great entertainment for the whole family!

title: El Dorado Musical Theatre: Curtains
description:
Curtains is a musical with a book by Rupert Holmes, lyrics by Fred Ebb, and music by John Kander, with additional lyrics by Kander and Holmes.

Based on the original book and concept by Peter Stone, the musical is a send-up of backstage murder mystery plots, set in 1959 Boston, Massachusetts and follows the fallout when the supremely untalented star of Robbin' Hood of the Old West is murdered during her opening night curtain call. It is up to a police detective who moonlights as a musical theater fan to save the show, solve the case, and maybe even find love before the show reopens, without getting killed himself.

title: Local Author Fair
description: Please join us for the 2nd annual Folsom Public Library Author Fair featuring keynote speaker Naida West, popular Sacramento area novelist and publisher. This event also offers book sales and signing by local authors, networking opportunities, and refreshments.

title: Bridal Open House
description: Now that spring has officially arrived, wedding plans are in full bloom, too! Arden Hills Resort Club & Spa invites brides, couples, and event planners to a complimentary “Bridal Open House” where they will enjoy tasty appetizers and refreshments while touring the gorgeous site with three elegant ballrooms, two lush wedding courtyards, the luxurious overnight villas, and award-winning spa and salon. Known as the area’s premiere wedding destination, Arden Hills is the perfect venue for creating events to remember.

title: Author Reading & Discussion: Ishmael Reed
description:
For a writer whose sensibility has always tilted toward the surreal and experimental (Nathanael West was an early and important influence), whose political incorrectness has been so brazen, his public feuds with other writers (pre-eminently feminists) so frequent and bitter, and his critique of white America so relentless, it might seem astonishing that Ishmael Reed has been as lavishly feted by the very establishment and in the very mainstream he typically excoriates.

In his latest book, Juice!, Reed holds his mirror up to the media coverage of trials—and especially its portrayal of black and Latino men—as his protagonist Paul Blessing becomes obsessed with the coverage of the O.J. Simpson trial and spectacularly unravels.

title: Curios & Notions
description: It's a call to all. Artists, patrons, performers...eaters, drinkers, and players...those with a passion for fashion and those with gift for gardening. Curios & Notions is the dot on the grid this weekend. Live music, pop-up fashion, foodie alert.

title: Why Gender Matters
description:
Join us for a conversation about the stalled progress of women in Congress and the State Legislature, and the effect on women's well-being across the country. Guest speakers include a representative of women's health services and a beneficiary of state and federal assistance programs.

Deborah Ortiz, former California State Assembly member, Senator, and current Vice President of Public Affairs for Planned Parenthood Mar Monte, will discuss the current assault on women's reproductive rights. Also, hear how reductions in government aid programs affect families and listen to a single mom explain how these key services help her family succeed.

Questions and open discussion will be encouraged. Admittance includes light appetizers and a no-host beverage service. College students encouraged to attend!

All proceeds go to Sacramento National Women’s Political Caucus, a local caucus dedicated to encouraging, educating, and endorsing women’s and children’s rights and the women representatives who fight for those values.

title: Eva Rutland and Family: Local Author Presentation
description:
Eva Rutland, author of more than 20 novels and winner of the 2000 Golden Pen Award for Lifetime Achievement, will be here with her daughter Ginger Rutland, associate editor for The Sacramento Bee, and granddaughter Eva Fields to give a joint presentation.

Eva's autobiography, When We Were Colored: A Mother's Story, is about an ordinary, yet extraordinary, "colored" family who moved from segregation to integration during the turbulent Civil Rights Era of the 1950s and 1960s. Their story is achingly poignant at times, funny at others, and always down to earth.

title: Sub-American: Poetry & Booksigning with NSAA
description: Poet and Spoken Word Artist NSAA has released a new book, Sub-American, a collection of poems dealing with the concept of being a hyphenated American. In his new book he explores a broad range of topics ranging from President Bush, Hurricane Katrina, and The Civil Rights Movement.

title: Sacramento Living Library: KZAP Radio Retrospective
description:
For the April entry in the 2011 Sacramento Living Library series Time Tested Books and Midtown Monthly are excited to present a look back at a legendary, gone-but-far-from-forgotten Sacramento treasure: 98.5 FM rock'n'roll radio station KZAP! (1968-1992 R.I.P.)

Based on literally every single reaction we've gotten to this news (except one), it's sure to be well-attended...heads up!

The Sacramento Living Library is curated by Time Tested Books' Peter Keat and hosted by Midtown Monthly's Tim Foster. The series continues on in 2011 on the third Sunday of every month at Time Tested Books.

title: Styles of Paradise Charity Fashion Show
description:
The Sacramento State Student Fashion Association (SFA) is having a charity fashion show highlighting student designers and stylists in Sacramento. The benefiting charity is the Autism Center for Excellence at Sacramento State in honor of April National Autism Awareness Month. Enjoy an evening of fashion, music, and fun.

Designers: Julian Gutierrez, Deneen Hayes, Alisa Correa, Christen Brown, Alexis Diaz, Erika Louie, Anakarina Pimental, Tamika Bellamy, Lacey Taylor and Samantha Rachele, Noognuv Thao, and Kira Martinson

Stylists: Abigail Cajucom, Shahirah Ahmed, Morgan Blamey, Fiona Lau, Jonique Fields, Erinn Murphy, Cazzi Coleman, and Bree Neuvirth.

Participating Boutiques: Heart Clothing Boutique, Sugar Shack, Krazy Mary's, and Lucky Lefty's.

Come mingle with designers, stylists, models, and SFA at the Launch Party the Tuesday before the show.

title: Bridal Faire and Show
description: Plan your dream wedding in a single day. Attend the Bridal Faire and Show and get information from wedding professionals about all aspects of your special day including ceremony sites, reception sites, wedding gown boutiques, cake decorators, wedding caterers, wedding planners, photographers, videographers, DJs, entertainers, limos, and more.

title: David Sedaris
description: With sardonic wit and incisive social critiques, David Sedaris has become one of America’s pre-eminent humor writers. A master of satire and one of the most observant writers addressing the human condition today, he deftly slices through cultural euphemisms and political correctness. Sedaris’s pieces appear regularly in The New Yorker and have twice been included in The Best American Essays. His newest book, Fables (with illustrations by Ian Falconer) is due fall 2010.

title: An Evening with Art Spiegelman (CANCELED)
description:
THIS EVENT HAS BEEN CANCELED (AS OF 3/21/11) DUE TO LACK OF TICKET SALES.

California Lectures subscribers have been offered four options to make up for the cancellation: They can receive a tax-deductible letter for the value of their tickets; exchange tickets for additional tickets to the Terry McMillan lecture on March 24 or to the Thomas McGuane lecture April 3; exchange tickets for the May 24 special-event lecture by Roy Blount, Jr.; or exchange tickets for half-price tickets to A Grand Night for Singing at the Cosmopolitan Cabaret, running through May 8. No deadline has been given for ticket exchanges.

Pulitzer Prize-winning author and illustrator Art Spiegelman will give provide a special multi-media presentation entitled "What the %@&*! Happened to Comics?" Pre-signed books will be available for purchase at the event. title: Pony Express E-Waste Day
description:
Pony Express Elementary School PTA is holding a free drive-through drop-off E-Waste Recycling Event. Please bring your E-Waste to Pony Express to help raise funds for our school! Our volunteers will unload your donated items for you...No need to get out of your car! Can't make it that day? Contact us to arrange for pick-up.

We will accept: monitors, televisions, desktop and notebook PCs, VCRs, stereo equipment, speakers, keyboards, mice, PDAs, digital cameras, zip drives, telephones, cell phones, printers, copiers, laser and multifunction scanners, and fax machines.

We will not accept: household appliances (i.e. refrigerators, washers, dryers etc.), furniture, hazardous household waste, including: batteries, paint, pesticides, used oil, cleaning supplies, fluorescent light bulbs, tires etc.

Sponsored by CEAR, INC, California Electronic Asset Recovery, a California state approved electronic waste collector and recycler. For optimal security, CEAR, INC. shreds all computer hard drives.

title: Ladies Day Festival: Spa-Tastique Event
description: Ladies Day Festival Spa-Tastique Event--bring your mom, your sister, your daughter, your aunt, your girlfriend--all the women in your life and enjoy a fabulous day of shopping and fun. Visit our “Spa” for complimentary mini treatments and advice.

title: 12th Annual Public Safety and Community Appreciation Breakfast
description:
The Sacramento County District Attorney is chairing the 12th Annual Public Safety and Community Appreciation Breakfast to pay tribute to law enforcement and the communities they serve. The breakfast will be held at the Doubletree Hotel in Sacramento.

In conjunction with the breakfast, there is a movie screening on April 14 at the IMAX Theatre.

title: Run for the Pink Roses
description:
Run for the Pink Roses is a special event for Wells Fargo that benefits the Susan G Komen Sacramento Valley Affiliate. The event consists of watching this year's Kentucky Derby live, dressing up like we are actually in the South, and just having a great time.

Enjoy big screen viewing of the race, non-gambling wagering on the race and associated activities for prices, hors d'ouevres with a derby flair (such as Hot Browns and dessert), complimentary wine tasting by Placer County Vitners, limited bourbon tasting, cigars for purchase, chapeau parade with prizes, complimentary mint julips in a souvenir take-home glass, goodie bags/silent auction, and photos with a live winning horse & jockey.

Derby attire requested (of course that includes all things pink!). The event takes place in the Historic Saddle Oaks Clubhouse at the Sacramento Horsemen’s Association.

title: Professor Henry Louis Gates Jr.: African American Lives (RESCHEDULED)
description:
Dr. Henry Louis Gates Jr. has rescheduled his appearance on March 7, following the death of his close friend and Harvard University colleague, Reverend Peter J. Gomes. Gates' speech will now occur at 8pm, May 9.

Patrons have several choices: 1) Hold onto existing tickets, which will be honored at the May 9 lecture. 2) Request a refund from the Mondavi Center ticket office at (530) 754-2787 or toll-free at (866) 754-2787 before May 8 (Open Mon-Sat, Noon-6pm). 3) Exchange the ticket for another event.

Literary critic, scholar, writer, and editor Henry Louis Gates Jr. is one of the most celebrated public intellectuals of our day. Gates is the head of the W.E.B. Du Bois Institute for African and African American Studies at Harvard University. In his lecture African American Lives: Genealogy, Genetics, and Black History, Professor Gates will address research and DNA analysis and poignant family stories in a lively discussion on individual lineage and African American history.

This program is presented in affiliation with the Davis Humanities Institute.

Ticket price includes:
-A chance to win diamond jewelry from Hearts on Fire and A. Jaffe, jewelry from Pandora, watches from TAG Heuer, Tissot, Seiko, and Bulova
-Two Race for the Ring T-shirts
-Access to the "After Party" at Raley Field and entertainment from one of Sacramento's hottest party bands

The event is presented by Rogers Jewlery Co. and 100% of the proceeds benefit Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services.

title: Red Hot Sale
times: Daily, times vary depending on participating store hours.

Visit participating Midtown retailers for Red Hot deals and pick up an entry for a chance to win a new Midtown scooter.

Participating businesses include: Artworks 21, Birkenstock Midtown, Crimson & Clover Vintage Boutique, Cuffs Boutique, FreeStyle Clothing Exchange, French Cuff Consignment, J's Beauty Supply, Ladybug Ladybug, Lumens Light + Living, Mixed Bag, Newsbeat, Prevues, Relles Florist, Ritz Camera, Sugar Shack Boutique, Swanbergs on J, The Beat, The Cotton Club, Time Tested Books, Tres Chic Boutique, and United State.

title: Sacramento Bike Swap in the Park
description:
The Sacramento Bike Kitchen, together with the Friends of Fremont Park will be holding their Spring Bicycle Swap Meet in Midtown Sacramento. Last year's event was a big success so if you missed it, or were waiting for next year, this is it.

Here's your chance to get a great deal on used bikes, parts, and clothing from other bike riders and enthusiasts. If you've got some things in your closet that you've been waiting to sell--old, new, vintage, or perhaps wrong size, this might be a great opportunity to finally get it done. If you're looking for stuff, this will be a place to find it.

Proceeds will go to benefit the non-profit organizations Sac Bike Kitchen and the Friends of Fremont Park. There are only so many swapping spots available and are reserved on a first-come, first serve basis.

title: Third Annual Cat's Meow Arts & Crafts Fair
description:
Come and browse many special items including jewelry, beaded purses, quilts, tote bags, aprons, pillows, cat trees, dog clothing, children's books, handmade soap, etched wood jewelry, video montage services for pets and their people, Tupperware, and much more!

Fairgoers can purchase raffle tickets for a chance to win great prizes. Prizes include gorgeous hand-made cat trees, an autographed photo of Tony Shalhoub (star of the hit TV series Monk), feline annual exam and diagnostics from the Sacramento Cat Hospital (a $270 value), and many others. Winners need not be present.

All proceeds from the Fair benefit the Sacramento Cat Hospital Foundation Benevolent Fund, established to provide medical care for injured, sick, and feral cats. Along with specialized care, the Benevolent Fund also provides routine physicals, vaccinations, viral screening, food, water, and shelter to the hospital's foster cats until they find forever homes. For more information about the Benevolent Fund, please visit their website.

title: Roy Blount, Jr. in Conversation with Sands Hall
description:
Roy Blount, Jr. is well known for his regular stint on Wait, Wait Don’t Tell Me! and as a recurring guest on A Prairie Home Companion. He is a humorist, sportswriter, poet, performer, dramatist, and screenplay writer and the author of 22 books. He has written about everything from the first woman president of the United States to what barnyard animals are thinking.

His recent books include Alphabetter Juice: The Joy of Text (May 2011), Hail, Hail Euphoria, and Long Time Leaving: Dispatches From Up South. Blount has been a columnist for Esquire and The New York Times, among others, and his work has appeared extensively in many periodicals and books, including The New Yorker, Gourmet, Playboy, Vanity Fair, Rolling Stone, The Best of Modern Humor, Baseball: A Literary Anthology, and Best American Essays 1997. Blount is a former president of the Authors Guild, a member of PEN and the Fellowship of Southern Authors, a New York Public Library Literary Lion, a Boston Public Library Literary Light, a usage consultant to the American Heritage Dictionary, and an original member of the Rock Bottom Remainders. In 2009 he received the Thomas Wolfe Award from the University of North Carolina.

“If everybody's first English teacher were Roy Blount Jr., we might still be trillions in debt, but we would be so deeply in love with words and their magic that we'd hardly notice.” —The Dallas Morning News

Sands Hall is an author and editor, a director and an actor. Her novel, Catching Heaven, is a Random House Reader’s Circle Selection and a Willa Award Finalist for Best Contemporary Fiction. Her plays include an adaptation of Louisa May Alcott’s Little Women and the comic/drama Fair Use, which explores the controversy surrounding Wallace Stegner’s novel, Angle of Repose. She is a Visiting Professor of Creative Writing at Franklin & Marshall College, Lancaster, PA.

title: Getting Sarai to UC Berkley Fundraiser
description: Sarai - 2 - Berkeley campaign: Please join us for a Carnitas/Fajitas Buffet fundraiser to help support Sarai Rodriguez who was accepted to the prestigious Haas School of Business at UC Berkeley! Sarai has completed Sacramento City College with a 3.96 GPA with no assistance from State or Federal Financial Aid! She needs your support now! Please help her by supporting this fundraiser and/or making your contribution directly! There will be Mariachi music, DJ, raffle prizes, and entertainment.

title: United Way's 3rd Annual Live United Toilet Paper Drive
description:
Residents can spare a square to help local nonprofits save thousands of dollars each year on toilet paper--donate at the United Way California Capital Region’s 3rd annual Live United Toilet Paper Drive. Last year’s drive raised 50,000 rolls of toilet paper, and this year’s goal is 60,000.

The toilet paper will be distributed the following week to many of United Way’s 142 certified partners in Amador, El Dorado, Placer, Sacramento, and Yolo counties.

United Way is the region’s leading provider of innovative solutions on the community’s most pressing issues, including high school graduation rates, household financial stability, and obesity. Working with other nonprofits, businesses, donors, and volunteers, United Way provides positive, measurable results on vital health and human services issues. Through new and traditional fundraising and mobilization programs, community members can give, volunteer, and advocate in support of the causes they care most about, benefiting United Way and hundreds of nonprofits in Amador, El Dorado, Placer, Sacramento, and Yolo counties. United Way is an independent, local affiliate of United Way Worldwide.

title: Boulevard Image Show-n-Shine
description:
Show-n-Shine features Classics, Lowriders, and Muscle Cars. Enjoy tunes from an oldies/old school DJ, great food, raffle prizes, and a 50/50 Raffle. Over 70 trophies awarded.

This is a family event--no alcohol and no attitudes.

title: 2nd Annual Red Shoe Crawl
description:
Join us as we leisurely stroll through beautiful downtown and midtown Sacramento for our 2nd Annual Red Shoe Crawl! Not only will you have an opportunity to enjoy a variety of culinary delights from the best restaurants in the Sacramento region, you will be supporting Ronald McDonald House Charities Northern California!

Each restaurant will have an appetizer sized food item, cocktail, and non-alcoholic beverage designed specifically for this event. A special section has been set aside for you and your fellow crawlers for you to mingle and enjoy the culinary delights.

This event is open to all ages and all proceeds benefit the children and families of the Sacramento Ronald McDonald House and Camp Eagle Lake. All guests are encouraged to wear red shoes in honor of Ronald McDonald's trademark footwear!

Some of the stops on the crawl include: 3 Fires Lounge, Buckhorn Grill, Morgan's Central Valley Bistro, Sapporo Grill & Steakhouse, Zocalo, L Wine Lounge & Urban Kitchen, Mama Kim on the Go, Trey B Cakes, Mini Burger, Lucca, and Rubicon.

Starting point TBD.

title: Summer Sundays
description:
Ahhh, summers in the city! Imagine yourself lounging poolside--guilt-free after a nice workout or exercise class--and enjoying being served frozen grapes, tasty bite-sized appetizers, and listening to a live band. That’s right, it’s “Summer Sundays” at Arden Hills Resort Club & Spa. Open to everyone, a daily resort pass gives you full access to the wellness resort for an indulgent day away from all the hustle and bustle of the week.

Advance reservations are not required, just show up on Sundays with your swimsuit and great attitude and we’ll take care of the rest--we’ll even provide sunscreen and sunglass cleaning!

title: Poetry in Davis at Bistro 33
description: Poetry in Davis presents poetry reading at Bistro 33 in Davis on the 1st Wed of every month. Each event features various artists.

title: Poetry in Davis at John Natsoulas Gallery
description: Poetry in Davis presents poetry readings at John Natsoulas Gallery in Davis the 3rd Thurs of every month. Each event features various artists.

title: Feather Falls Day Hike
description:
This is a spectacular opportunity to see the sixth-highest waterfall in the continental United States. Feather Falls plunges 640 feet over a sheer granite cliff in its rush to meet the middle fork of the Feather River. The hike is eight miles round trip, moderately strenuous and somewhat steep at times, but not technically difficult. Beginners in good shape will enjoy this hike!

Trip includes guides and transportation.

title: Basic Mountain Biking
description:
This ride is geared for beginning or intermediate riders who want to improve their mountain biking skills. We will cover all the riding basics needed to travel down the trail via two wheels. Instruction will cover riding techniques such as successful gearing, brake modulation, and ratcheting, as well as repair, safety, gear, trail etiquette, and much more.

This trip welcomes riders of all abilities. Trip includes guides and transportation. You provide your own bike and helmet. If you don't have a bike, we rent them! Check out the equipment rental page for prices and details.

A pre-trip meeting occurs the Wednesday before the class.

title: Zipline Canopy Tour
description:
If you’ve ever wondered what it feels like to fly, then this is the trip for you. You’ll rocket through the tall redwood trees of Sonoma County across 10 different ziplines reaching speeds up to 25 miles per hour. Over the several hour tour you will see the wonders of the natural world from a whole different perspective, at times gliding 300 feet above a natural ravine, and whizzing around Walter, the oldest tree on the property. First of its kind, the spiral staircase around one of the trees will take your breath away, and the 175 foot sky bridge will make you feel like you’re walking on air.

Trip includes guides, transportation, fees and equipment.

title: Belay 101
description: Looking for a way to reach new heights? This is the ideal course for the novice climber. This course is designed to teach you how to use ropes and other safety equipment to keep your climbing partner secure while climbing. This class will teach you everything that you need to know to pass the belay test, which is required to belay at the WELL climbing wall. During this course you will learn how to tie a figure-8 follow through knot and a double fisherman’s knot, standard climbing commands, and a pre-climb safety check. Additionally, at the conclusion of the course the participant should be able to safely belay a climber up the climbing wall, and then lower the climber back to the ground.

title: Hike of the Month
description: These short local hikes are a great way to get to know what’s in your own backyard. Every third Friday, you’ll have an opportunity to visit a new destination.

title: Women's Intermediate  Day Hike: Mt. Tamalpais State Park
description:
The women’s hiking series goes coastal to Mount Tamalpais, one of Marin Counties towering peaks. This intermediate 4 to 6 mile loop travels through redwood groves, oak woodlands, and grass-covered hills as it circles the upper part of the mountain. On a clear day this hike provides views of the Pacific Ocean, beautiful rolling hills of Marin County, and both the Golden Gate and Richmond bridges. The Dipsea Trail descends into an open view of the ocean and Stinson Beach, which makes for a beautiful and rewarding end to a wonderful hike.

Trip includes guides and transportation. The women's hiking series also includes Women’s Beginning Hike and Women’s Backpacking.

title: Point Reyes Backpacking
description:
Come walk on the "wild" side at Point Reyes National Seashore, one of California’s finest and most well-preserved wildlife areas. You might get a magical glimpse of a fox, badger, or possibly a rare albino deer. As an extra bonus, take a walk down to the beach where you can explore the wonders of tide pool life and possibly catch a glimpse of seals or whales.

If you have always wanted to try backpacking, then this is the trip for you since no experience is necessary! The coastal air will be invigorating and relaxing as you pass through a riparian zone to coastal bluffs.

Trip price includes guides, transportation, gear, dinners, and camping permits. A pre-trip meeting occurs the Tuesday before the trip.

title: Next Level Workshop with Tristina Quattlebum
description:
Take your practice to the next level! Join Tristina for this workshop where you will be guided through step-by-step instructions on how to start incorporating some “advanced” postures into your current yoga practice.

We will cover various topics such as:
-Safe alignment shifting from Chaturanga to Upward Facing Dog
-How to jump back and forward during your vinyasa
-The purpose of bandhas (internal locks) and how to engage them to improve your poses
-Accessing binds and transitioning to poses such as Bird of Paradise
-Accessible preparations for arm balances and inversions

Make the choice to step outside of your comfort zone and discover strength you didn’t know you had!

title: Basic Rock Climbing: Cosumnes River Gorge
description:
If you've always wanted to try this exciting sport, but didn't know how to get started, look no further! Designed for the adventurous beginner, this all-day course provides an introduction to outdoor climbing. We’ll cover the basics: knot tying, belaying, general equipment use, and basic climbing techniques.

While this course is focused on the beginner, the intermediate climbers will still learn valuable techniques to help you climb smarter and safer! Trip includes expert instruction by the Peak Adventures climbing staff, transportation, and all climbing gear.

A pre-trip meeting occurs the Wednesday before the class.

title: Sacramento Ultimate Frisbee
description: Midtown Ultimate plays coed Ultimate Frisbee in Midtown Sacramento, and field teams to Sacramento Ultimate Players Association's (SUPA) local leagues. We teach new players the rules of the game, and get together for eats and drinks after! All players and skill levels welcome. Join the fun!

title: Walk a Mile in Her Shoes
description:
Join the 10th Anniversary celebration of Walk a Mile in Her Shoes and the 1st Walk a Mile in Her Shoes event in Sacramento. The event gets the men in our community to take a stand against sexualized violence. Tens of thousands of men have worn heels to raise hundreds of thousands of dollars to support local rape crisis services and domestic violence shelters. The Sacramento event benefits the Sacramento County Women Escaping a Violent Environment, Inc..

The event will host several fun activities for men to do in heels. The Sacramento State women’s soccer team will challenge participants to score goals on them. Other festivities include live music and live radio coverage by NOW 100.5 FM.

There will be prizes for participants, including the hairiest legs, the most team spirit and the man who raised the most money for WEAVE.

The walk begins in on Capital Avenue, near Zócalo, and returns there for an after party following the walk. At the after party, enjoy food and drinks and a special breakfast cocktail with champagne called “The Bloody Heel.”

title: Thunder Valley Casino IKF Muay Thai Kickboxing Championships
description:
IKF Championship Kickboxing is a Las Vegas style show that features some of the best men and women in full contact knockout Muay Thai/Kickboxing Action! The show is complete with alcohlic beverages, cameras, and beautiful ring girls!

Approximately 15 fights will be presented and five of them are Championship fights with local champions involved. For the sports fan, it's a show you will not want to miss at one of the best casinos in the USA!

title: Fair Oaks Sun Run
description:
Fleet Feet's Fair Oaks Sun Run has been an annual tradition in Fair Oaks for over a quarter century and--believe or not--it hasn't gotten one bit easier! Regarded as one of the most beautiful and challenging courses around, it never fails to attract both the avid runner and those who are out to have a great time at a great event.

Choose either the 5-mile run/walk or a 2.3 mile family walk which both start at Village Park in Old Fair Oaks. The 5-mile route winds through the beautiful Old Fair Oaks residential neighborhood with a keyhole loop to Sailor Bar. The course is half paved roads, half dirt trail, and features the infamous four hills: Grand Daddy Hill, Hernia Hill, The Beast, and Last Gasp. The 2.3 mile event stays on the paved roads through Old Fair Oaks.

title: Haggin Oaks Golf Expo: America's Largest Demo Days
description:
With over 150 different manufacturers and booths scheduled to appear, the Haggin Oaks Golf Expo is truly the show of all shows, hosting golfers from all over California, Oregon, and Nevada to see the latest in golf equipment to the best vacation destinations--and everything in between! More than 21,000 golfers travel to “America’s Largest Demo Day” to test the hottest equipment and accessories from 150+ manufacturers; experience the latest launch monitors & Tour Tech vans; trade in old clubs; and shop in the 15,000 square foot Haggin Oaks Golf Super Shop. Nowhere else in the country will there be a larger collection of golf vendors available to the general public.

The Haggin Oaks Golf Expo is also launching great new initiatives in 2011 including The Game Improvement Stage! A huge stage on wheels will create a mini-amphitheater right on the range where every hour on the hour, free educational opportunities will be presented on topics such as golf ball fitting, putting clinics, golf shaft education, golf fitness instruction, guest instructors, and more.

For the first time ever, the 50+ year old Sacramento Golf Council Putting Championship (formerly won by multi-time PGA Tour winner Bill Glasson) will be held over the weekend. We’ll have three different divisions including Mens, Womens, and Juniors--and each of the overall winners will receive a brand new Limited Edition Never Compromise Gambler Series putter, plus some more goodies.

The Haggin Oaks Golf Expo is also home to Vendor Tour Fitting Vans normally only reserved by PGA Tour events. These mobile fitting vans on wheels come complete with the latest in fitting equipment technology and many build clubs for the consumer right there on the spot. With vendors like Nike, Titleist, Cobra, Cleveland, Mizuno, UST, TaylorMade, Callaway and Ping already committed, this is just one more reason that makes this event unique. description:
This solo show honors the beautiful complexities of the human experience through a collection of oil portraits by local painter Brooke Walker-Knoblich. Come witness the unveiling of three new works at the artist's reception on Preview Thursday!

Among the paintings to be unveiled in their first public viewing is "Winter Bloom" (see crop of original composition). Brooke completed this oil painting in response to the tragedies currently wreaking havoc in Japan. To not only celebrate their strength and courage but to help the Japanese people recover, a percentage of the proceeds of the sale of "Winter Bloom" will be donated to relief efforts.

Please share this reception invitation with your friends or anyone who may be interested in supporting Japan through the arts.

title: Art by Brannon Collins and Music from DJ B-Vega
description:
Brannon Collins is a self taught artist, who has been drawing since the age of five. As an "80's kid" growing up in Hawaii, Brannon watched Japanese cartoon shows like, Space Battleship Yamato and Mazinger Z which sparked his imagination and got him drawing at an early age. He moved with his family to Los Angeles in late 1984 where he was first introduced to graffiti. By 1989, he was tagging his name around his neighborhood, and by the early '90s he was a full-time graffiti writer. While writing graffiti, Brannon further engaged himself in the Hip Hop culture, by picking up the mic and becoming an emcee. He gained quick recognition and partnered up with West Los Angeles hip hop group People Under the Stairs. Through all of this Brannon never stopped painting and drawing. He now lives in Northern California with his wife and daughter and is a freelance illustrator and artist.

DJ B-Vega is from Seattle, WA and has been behind the turntables since '99. Originally a strictly hip-hop/turntabalist background has evolved into a mix of soul, funk, true school, and underground hip-hop. He has played at multiple clubs/venues in Seattle and greater Washington State. Look out for his new line of mixtapes due this summer under his own brand: Chubb Scout Mixtapes.

title: Trifecta
description: Trifecta is a group show dedicated to the glory of spring time! Come to check out fresh paintings, graphic art, and enjoy live music. Featured artists are: Sofia Lacin, Jeff Musser, Brooke Walker-Knoblich, Laurie Hicklin, and Eben Burgoon.

title: New Works: Photography by Cosumnes River Students
description: Come out to the New Works 2nd Saturday Art Show by Cosumnes River Photography Students.

"3" is 3 Artists. 3 Mediums. 3 Days. 3 dimensional work in clay, wood, and steel.

Elliott Roges' painstakingly-detailed clay pieces bring awe and joy in his unpredictable animal creatures. Now a mountain man, we are wondering what cave he is creating out of these days. Rogers left a couple years ago to live off the grid and will be gracing us with his art and presence.

Nathan Cordero is back in these parts after his adventure in New York the last couple of years. With all that eastern culture we are expecting more brilliant concepts cut outta ply and a few ciggies to boot!

Then there is Gale Hart who wants to pack it all in an RV but just can't quite find a place for all that scrap steel--so she threw some more furniture together and even took the time to throw down some graffiti on it.

You all need to come by A Bitchin' Space cause the shows there are few and far between.

title: Busywork: Paper and Process, Sculpture and Installation
description:
Paper: it’s not just for drawing any more! Sac City professor Mitra Fabian curated this show of sculptures and installations made with paper. Fabian (who, working with artist Jen Stract as mfjs, contributes an installation) is a process-based artist in the mold of Tara Donovan--she well understands how the artist can transform the most humble of materials into art. And the materials here are humble, including discarded index cards and shredded business documents.

The five artists in the show (Jill Sylvia, Fanny Retsek, and Penny Young in addition to Fabian and Stract) are all women, and the title is a play on the nature of intensive process work by women “converting fruitless action into impressive and sublime work."
venue: Gregory Kondos Gallery - Sacramento City College

Celebrate Women's History Month during the 1st Saturday Art Walk with an artist's talk from Ms. Marshall's daughter, Kanika Marshall, on Mar 5 from 5pm-6pm.

title: Poetic License: Portraits of Sacramento's Poets
description:
Poetic License: Portraits of Sacramento’s Poets features 45 portraits of Sacramento's poets by local artist Suzanne Johnson.

Johnson was commissioned by the Sacramento Metroropolitan Arts Commission (SMAC) in 2006 through 2008 to create portraits for a deck of cards. The portraits honor poets who were active in Sacramento during the creation and solidification of the poetry scene during the 1960s, ‘70s, and ‘80s. The result was 56 intimate portraits—45 of which are featured in this exhibition—drawn in graphite by Ms. Johnson.

Ms. Johnson studied art at Sacramento City College and U.C. Davis and has been active in the Sacramento poetry community for decades.

The reception includes readings by Julia Connor, Patrick Grizzell, Ann Menebroker, and Kathryn Hohlwein, to name a few.
