title: Migration of Form: New Paintings & Collages by Michaele LeCompte
description:
JAYJAY is proud to present Migration of Form, new paintings and collages from Michaele LeCompte, a one person exhibit from this gifted Sacramento City College painting instructor. LeCompte is often associated with vivid color and abstracted forms, as her work is firmly planted in the 20th century and inspired by those Modern Masters: Matisse and Picasso.

In this body of work, LeCompte is using geometric forms, such as rectangles and squares, but painting them with a thick impasto application of paint, giving them drama and emotion. She is opening up areas of the canvas with larger rectangular shapes that are tilted and leaning, lending movement to the painting. Finally, this new work is predominately limited in palette, pushing the forms in shades of black, grey, white, and cream. The large paintings are complimented by LeCompte’s new collages on paper, composed and assembled from recycled work, but with more negative space--punctuations among these shifting paintings.

title: Flora
description: Despite all the rain, Spring is here! And with the Spring, the Roman goddess Flora begs for our attention as she makes her appearance in all the blooming magnolia, plum, and cherry trees around our city. For the month of April, Tangent Gallery will be celebrating Flora, in all its forms in a show that hopes to offer a contemporary take botanical illustration, or at least artworks inspired by our leafy friends. In typical Tangent style, you can expect to see a wide variety of media utilized in the works displayed, created by a wide ranging group of mostly local artists, including Troy Mighty, Laurie Rindell, and Mary Coldren. Next month--Fauna!

title: Equinox: Kelvin Curry and Stephen Bruce
description:
Equinox: When the length of day and night are closest to being equal; a precise moment in time which is common to all observers on Earth. Experience the earthy, subtle, and elegant patinated copper and brass works of Stephen Bruce and the energetic, vibrant, and passionate pastels of Kelvin Curry.

This is the first time Kelvin Curry and Stephen Bruce will share a profound artistic moment in time. This duet-exhibition brings the viewer to the intersection of two distinctly different mediums--patinated copper and pastels. Equinox will mark a point in time in which the diverse skills and talents of Curry and Bruce will be presented together and featured in one beautifully fashioned masterpiece to be revealed at Evolve the Gallery.

About Stephen Bruce: Though he has only been showing work since June 2006, his acid paintings on copper have already been seen in TV shows (House, Law & Order LA, Big Bang Theory, The New Adventures of Old Christine, to name a few) and movie sets (Smart Car and The Quickening), selected to decorate the 2007 Sunset Magazine Idea House and garnered art festival accolades. Similar in style and philosophy to that of the abstract expressionist painter Mark Rothko, Bruce’s work has quickly gained followers and patrons around the country ranging from prestigious gallery owners to discriminating art lovers.

About Kelvin Curry: Born in Oakland, CA, Kelvin Curry's creative destiny was clear early in life. Initially utilizing black and white graphite as his medium and children as his subjects, Oakland's own black Adoption & Placement Center was among his many venues. His early work caught the attention of jazz musician Wynton Marsalis, who owns a self-portrait by Kelvin. Later, he would expand into mixed media to bring about multi-dimension; as well as a sense of rhythm and grace in abstract figure. Kelvin has exhibited his work in hundreds of juried festivals, exhibits, and galleries throughout the country. To view his work is to experience the association between beauty and love. To bring three energies together in moment--physical, spiritual, and emotional--is his fundamental artistic expression.

title: The Art of Light:  Nature's Spirit
description:
Lumens Light + Living and The Center for Contemporary Art, Sacramento’s Gallery Associates Stacey Wong and Mariana Moscoso are pleased to present Nature’s Spirit, a photography exhibition by Cameron Park-based photographer Sandy Follett. This series exhibition curated by Stacey Wong includes photographs taken in the Yosemite Valley, the High Sierra, Roseville, and Rescue, California.

Follett uses light to capture that special moment in nature, when she believes the light best expresses its spiritual qualities. She spends several days searching for just the right lighting, often returning numerous times to the same spot to check on changes in the light due to weather, cloud cover, time of day, and season of the year, which she says all play a factor in lighting. Her photographs reflect her passion and respect for California’s wilderness areas where she and her family hike and camp. She feels a sense of responsibility to preserve these places and has performed docent and other volunteer services for the Yosemite Conservancy in the Tuolumne Meadows in Yosemite National Park. Follett is a member of the Viewpoint Photographic Art Center.

About The Art of Light series: Lumens Light + Living has invited Gallery Associates Mariana Moscoso and Stacey Wong from The Center for Contemporary Art, Sacramento to collaborate on a series of exhibitions called The Art of Light. In this year-long series, we will explore how artists have taken the concept of light to create a unique visual experience using both traditional and non-traditional media. The visual possibilities of light are infinite and only limited by the artists’ unique experience.

title: En Plein Air
description: En Plein Air features the work of three exceptional painters--Kathy O'Leary, Philippe Gandiol, and Paul Ferney--who have ventured outside the confines of their studios to capture the essence of the Northern California landscape. This challenge has yielded an incredibly authentic body of work, championed by spontaneity and an urgency to capture the natural light of the outdoors.

title: Jeff Felker Solo Exhibition
description:
Exploring themes reformulated from life and his formal background in literature, Jeff Felker creates narrative paintings that blend reality and dreamscape--the human figures within are located in conflicted worlds of emotional isolation. Using oil to juxtapose bright and muted color schemes, Jeff executes his paintings on canvas and board.

On display are 14 art prints, 5 paintings, and a few drawings--a huge quantity of limited edition giclee prints of his paintings. Print prices range from $25-$50 unframed and $50-$75 framed. Stop on by get, get a trim, and check out his work!

title: Depth of Field: 30 Years of Photography & Multimedia
description: Sacramento State photographer Sam Parsons, who retired in January, will share his work in Depth of Field: 30 Years of Photography and Multimedia. Pieces include posters, prints, multi-media projects, and a section on the Sac State gymnastics program.

title: Art Medley
description: Art Medley is an exhibit featuring several of the area's top artists working in a variety of styles and mediums.

title: Work by Fred Martin
description:
Charged with explosive color and brooding abstract imagery, this dramatic series of paintings and prints by the prolific artist, writer, and art historian Fred Martin represents a brilliant new direction for his work. Deeply involved with Bay Area art, Martin was director of the college of the San Francisco Art Institute from 1965 to 1975, and dean of academic affairs from 1983 to 1992. Martin has exhibited widely and is in numerous museum collections, including the Fogg Museum at Harvard University, the Oakland Museum of California, SFMOMA, MOMA, and the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York.

Image: Tarot Series1995 -03-19 “Justice”, Mixed Media, 2005

2nd Saturday activities include a bronze pouring demonstration at 7:30pm.

title: Work by Theophilus Brown
description: This month, works by Theophilus Brown will be on display at b. sakata garo gallery.

title: Curious Incidents Revealed (Almost Lifelike)
description: Curious Incidents Revealed (Almost Lifelike) is an exhibition of artwork by Gary Dinnen & Dutch Falconi. Also on display is Into the Forest, work by Janice Nakashima and Pamela Blotner.

title: Work by Danäe Anderson
description: Skinner Howard Gallery' presents works by Danäe Anderson.

title: 2011 Viewpoint Fine Print Auction and Annual Fundraiser
description:
The April exhibit at Viewpoint displays all the prints that will be available in the 2011 Viewpoint Fine Print Auction and Fundraiser. This year’s featured photographers include Howard Bond, Mark Citret, Charles Cramer, Machiko Kurita, Richard Murai, Ron Reeder, Ryuijie, John Sexton, Jerry Takigawa, Gary Vann, John Wimberley, and Huntington Witherill. Many other Viewpoint members are also represented.

Prints may be purchased throughout the month by Silent Auction and/or at the Live Auction. 20% “Buy It Now” Discount through Fri, April 22. 10% “Buy It Now” Discount through Fri, April 29. Silent Auction closes on Fri, May 6 at 3pm.

See the auction catalog and view the online auction.

title: The Landscape by Gregory Kondos
description: Gregory Kondos is one of the West’s foremost landscape artists. For over 40 years he has traveled the world painting landscapes as inspiring as Yosemite Valley, the French countryside, and the islands of Greece.

title: In the Studio: Public Artists in Their Private Spaces
description:
In the Studio: Public Artists in Their Private Spaces features the studio artwork of some of the area’s most well-known public artists, including Suzanne Adan, Gerald Heffernon, Kurt Steger, Willem de Groot, Jack Nielsen, Michael Stevens, and Richard Feese. The exhibition includes sculpture in a variety of media, as well as scratchboard and oil painting.

For these artists the art practice begins in the studio—inspiration and solitude affording them the opportunity to create more personal work. This personal work informs their public work—although, in varying degrees. In the case of artist Gerald Heffernon, his studio work is whimsical, but can afford to also be a bit dark. His materials are less durable than what’s necessary in public art, allowing for a different sort of artistic freedom. This is evident in “Cabbit”, where Heffernon focuses on cloning genetic selection—a mixture of a cat and a rabbit made startingly real by his imagination and skill as a sculptor.

The gap from studio to public artwork is less pronounced in the case of artist Kurt Steger’s work. A product of his studio practice, “Winter Circle,” closely resembles processes evident in his public artwork, such as “Reflection”, a functional environment located in Sacramento City Hall’s front lobby. Both works employ durable, industrial materials, yet are organic and earthy aesthetically. The scale is the indicator here of studio vs. public work and demonstrates that Steger is working out ideas in his studio that often evolve into larger public projects.

The exhibition can be seen in 10 display cases throughout Terminal B (6 of which are restricted to ticketed passengers).

title: Works by Nathan Cordero
description: Art by Nathan Cordero graces the walls of Cuffs for their April show.

title: Gay Outlaw: The Velocity of Ideas
description:
Primarily regarded as a conceptual sculptor with a growing national reputation, Gay Outlaw works as an investigator of physicality, perception, memory, and materials. Her work revolves around combining inherent contradictions: Sculptures that seem to be constructed of voids; Photographs of false surfaces transformed into solid objects; Images of holes, reversed, and cast in bronze and glass.

For her show at CCAS, Outlaw will present a variety of studio works that continue and document these investigations, and will include many pieces shown for the first time. Mirroring her studio environment, the exhibition will include sculptures in a variety of media, including blown glass, cast bronze, cast and constructed paper, felt, and wood. Although disparate in materials, the works are alive with visual connections. The shape of a cast shadow in one piece is transformed into a three-dimensional structure in another, and a wave cast in paper is mirrored in a small bronze, which in turn is perforated by a grid of holes echoing several other pieces. Each piece addresses the flow of the creative process, and the visual associations and internal dialogues reveal that this process of constant development is the actual subject of her work.

Special 2nd Saturday activities:
-April 9, 3pm, Free: Video Presentation: Gay Outlaw: The Velocity of Ideas. A conversation between Gay Outlaw and exhibition curator, Chris Daubert. Premier showing. Run-time, approximately 30 minutes.
-May 14, 3pm, $5 (Free for Students & CCAS Members): Gay Outlaw Lecture. Gay will discuss her work.

title: Painting Where the Wild Things Are Exhibition
description:
Painting Where the Wild Things Are is an open juried art show at the Sacramento Fine Arts Center benefiting the Effie Yeaw Nature Center. Regional artists will submit paintings of the American River Parkway and the wild things that live there. Juror is Pat Mahony.

This art show is a preview of the Gala and Art Auction to be held at the Effie Yeaw Nature Center.

Entries for the exhibit are taken on April 15 & April 16. See the Call for Artists for details.

title: A Day of Art at the Hart
description:
In honor of Hart Senior Center’s 50th Anniversary, come join us for a Day of Art. All types of art will be displayed: paintings, murals, sculptures, photographs, drawings, jewelry, music, and poetry.

There is still space available to show. If you would like to be featured, check out the Classified for more information.

title: Small World, Small Works Exhibit
description:
The Small World, Small Works Exhibition was designed as an opportunity for local artists to show their work with other artists from around the nation and the world. Specifically, we hope to bring artists from all parts of the world together underone roof for our visitors to enjoy. We hope to enlighten our visitors about art made by people from regions of the world that they would not normally have an
opportunity to see. We value the diversity found in all cultures today and believe that this event will bring people closer to one another through art.

title: The Real-Fake: Exploring 3-D Art
description: Radical new art created with 3-D software will be exhibited in The Real-Fake. The exhibit is organized by Art Professor Rachel Clarke and Chicago School of the Art Institute’s Claudia Hart.

title: Never Can Say: Goodbye
description:
Never Can Say: Goodbye is an exhibit of new paintings, photographs, transfers, and digital paintings by Ann Tracy. While Tracy has been involved in both the theatrical and visual arts communities in the Sacramento area for 20 years, this will be her “swan song show” as she is moving back to her roots in New England–specifically Portland, Maine.

The new work featured will be from many of the series that she works on in tandem. There will be some new transfer work from the “Potency of Memory” series which deals with identity and familial memory. There will also be a new piece from the “Power Series” based on her photography in Romania as a judge for a theatre solo show competition. Other new works include digital paintings where she has appropriated classical masterworks and collaged them into iPod photos as a response to the latest thinking in string theory. She will also exhibit some abstract acrylic work on canvas.

Tracy’s fine art has been exhibited from Japan to Maui to New York City. In 2003 her work, “Stop” was included in the catalog of the Violence Against Women exhibition, Group 78 Amnesty International, Tokyo, Japan. Her digital paintings “The Power of Romania Lies in its Artists” and “Message 3” were juried into the 2010 and 2008 edition of American Art Collector. She also presented a creativity workshop to feature writers at the Sacramento Bee, a daily newspaper in 2008.

title: Shape Shifting: Birgitta Franzen McCarthy
description:
During the month of May, Axis Gallery will show work by Birgitta Franzen McCarthy. The title of this exhibition is Shape Shifting. These paintings and photos are the artistic notations of shifting forms and reflections of patterns outdoors.

The artist comments: “In 1997 I started painting changes in forms and patterns on a table in the back yard through the seasons as a natural observation and noting down the times. It was simultaneous with my dad writing a book about time. With the motion of light, forms change so fast I had to make a random selection. I also started filming and have recently used photography. The incredible flexibility of forms in nature can be hard to even fathom.”

As part of her longstanding commitment to Community Art, Birgitta is also showing a large scale painting from a project made by participants in a group in a community recovery program.

Axis Gallery is a cooperative gallery and features cutting edge contemporary art by local and international artists.

title: All That Jazz: A Fine Art Jazz Exhibition
description:
All That Jazz: A Fine Art Jazz Exhibition features art by Frank Blackwell, Gerry "GOS" Simpson, and Lawrence Sullivan

Meet the artists at the 1st Saturday Opening Reception.

title: Non Solo: A Group Exhibition
description:
The Center for Contemporary Art, Sacramento is proud to present Non Solo, a group exhibition of 2-D and 3-D works in various media by Margaret Coleman, Stephen Eakin, Heather Elizabeth Garland, Jason Gaspar, Lacey Prpic Hedtke, William Hempel, Yasamin Keshtkar, Anna Marie Shogren, and Bonnie Kaye Whitfield. The nine young artists whose individual and collaborative artwork is on view are based in New York, Minneapolis, and Philadelphia.

Non Solo is a show the artists have taken on the road, traveling together in a van like a band of gypsies or a carnival troupe. The art travels with them, much of it in progress – in recombination and otherwise morphing – as Non Solo tours among scheduled art venues and interacts with specific spaces and audiences around the U.S.

Be prepared for surprises when Non Solo comes to CCAS, but some things we can expect. The exhibition opens with a public conversation among the artists. We can also expect to see their Merch Table: an installation-as-gallery of cheaply-priced art objects, clothes, handmade books, zines, and other "merchandise" offered to the public much like a band on tour sells paraphernalia like t-shirts and stickers. The Merch Table appears at all Non Solo venues. At once a fundraising tool and an artwork, it is accompanied by an assemblage video work made from clips of the Non Solo artists interacting.

Another collaborative work on view is an interactive still life sculpture project that viewers rearrange during the exhibition. A satellite installation is the van the group tours in, presented as an artwork and exhibition space.

Note: There will be a 3-5 minute improvised noise performance by Jason Gaspar at an unscheduled time during the reception. Also on view will be the Non Solo van that patrons will be encourage to enter and explore.

title: 6th National Juried Art Exhibition
description:
Axis Gallery's 6th Annual National Juried Art Exhibition consists of work by contemporary American aritst. 2D & 3D work in all media is included--paintings, prints, drawings, photography, digital images, etc. All work is original and has been produced within the last two years.

This year's juror is Dena Beard, Curatorial Assistant for the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAM/PFA). For the MATRIX program at BAM/PFA she assists with the production of site-specific projects by national and international emerging artists, including Ahmet Ogut, Omer Fast, Futurefarmers, Brent Green, Paul Chan, Martha Colburn, Mario Garcia Torres, Trevor Paglen, Tomas Saraceno, Allison Smith, and Tris Vonna-Michell, among others.Independently, she curated the Lending Library exhibition series in Oakland and San Francisco, featuring the research materials of Desiree Holman, Trevor Pa-glen, Kevin Killian, Tom Marioni, Colter Jacobsen, Amy Franceschini, Stephanie Syjuco, among other artists.

Dena is currently working on Take Up Room on the Floor, a project about physical and virtual embodiment, and a solo exhibition featuring the artist Lutz Bacher. The juror graduated from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago with an M.A. in Art History, Theory, and Criticism.

If you are interested in contributing your work to this exhibition, entries are accepted through May 28.

title: Lunchtime Art Tours
description: Every Wednesday, Sacramento Art Complex hosts lunchtime art tours, so walk down and have lunch in the sculpture garden and afterwards enjoy a free guided tour of the art and artists' studios.

title: Chant For Global Peace Festival
description:
This is the 1st Annual Chant For Global Peace Festival. It's an all day celebration of spiritual journey of chanting and hearing transcendental sounds vibration which is healing and soothing. The transcendental sounds vibration has a purifying effects to a person, surrounding areas, and atmosphere that continuously moving around the world.

Drum circle, yoga sounds, meditation, demos on raw cooking, healthy lifestyle and vendors space for health and other well being products.

This event takes place on the Village Green.

title: Belay 101
description: Looking for a way to reach new heights? This is the ideal course for the novice climber. This course is designed to teach you how to use ropes and other safety equipment to keep your climbing partner secure while climbing. This class will teach you everything that you need to know to pass the belay test, which is required to belay at the WELL climbing wall. During this course you will learn how to tie a figure-8 follow through knot and a double fisherman’s knot, standard climbing commands, and a pre-climb safety check. Additionally, at the conclusion of the course the participant should be able to safely belay a climber up the climbing wall, and then lower the climber back to the ground.

title: Basic Mountain Biking
description:
This ride is geared for beginning or intermediate riders who want to improve their mountain biking skills. We will cover all the riding basics needed to travel down the trail via two wheels. Instruction will cover riding techniques such as successful gearing, brake modulation, and ratcheting, as well as repair, safety, gear, trail etiquette, and much more.

This trip welcomes riders of all abilities. Trip includes guides and transportation. You provide your own bike and helmet. If you don't have a bike, we rent them! Check out the equipment rental page for prices and details.

Pre-trip meeting occurs the Tuesday before the class.

title: Boot Camp Workout
description:
An hour long boot camp style class without the yelling! Just fun, hard work for all levels and ages.

This class happens every week in the park. We workout following a circuit style which helps keep your heart rate going the whole time. Working out this way promotes fat loss while building lean muscle.

title: Doggy Dash and Bark at the Park Festival
description: This dog-friendly event draws more than 5,000 people and their dogs for a fun walk and festival in beautiful William Land Park. Come for the 2k or 5k walk and stay for the SPCA’s Bark at the Park Festival, where you can enter your canine pal in the Pup Show, high-flying disc contest, or the ever-popular pug races! Watch canine demonstrations, visit with pet-friendly businesses, learn about Sacramento-area animal rescue organizations, or sit back and just enjoy all of the action.

title: 53rd Annual Town & Country Art Fiesta
description:
We invite you to come celebrate at the Town & Country Art Fiesta. This family friendly event attracts thousands of people. It is the main fundraising event for the Sacramento Suburban Kiwanis. The show has been at the Town and Country Village Shopping Center, since its inception 53 years ago.

Enjoy browsing and buying art and meeting the artists. The show features fine handcrafted art--from jewelry and sculpture to paintings and pottery and more. Artists are juried.

Proceeds from this event help children charities in the greater Sacramento region.

title: 10th Annual Juneteenth: A Celebration of Freedom
description:
Since Summer 2001, Sacramento's Juneteenth festival has celebrated and educated the community about one of America's most important acts of legislation: the Emancipation Proclamation. Signed into law in 1863, the Emancipation Proclamation declared that all those enslaved were now free.

Sacramento's Juneteenth: A Celebration of Freedom Weekend is produced by the Sacramento Convention & Visitors Bureau under the direction of Gary Simon, Director of Multicultural Affairs, with the assistance of the Juneteenth Committee, a group of dedicated local residents who volunteer their time and energy to produce a successful and ever-growing event. 

The weekend is a family-friendly celebration and includes two stages of live entertainment, vendors, children's activities, Tribute to the Buffalo Soldiers and Tuskegee Airmen, Fraternity Row, fishing derby, parade, Juneteenth Educational Theater, spoken word/poetry, cultural dance performances, The Juneteenth Talent Show, The Juneteenth Golf Tournament, and more!

title: Launch Design & Music Festival
description:
Launch is a multi-disciplinary audio/visual festival that connects people with art, music, fashion, and design. Launch recognizes and seeks to highlight the cultural overlaps between creative industry and aims to create a cross-discipline experience that allows people to connect with the artists, their work, and the performances.

Don't miss this event showcasing art, music, fashion, and design from Sacramento amd beyond. Enjoy live musical performances and DJ sets throughout the night, a fashion show, and galleries featuring artists and furniture designers. Launch Events is planned by a collaborative of Sacramento designers, musicians, artists, photographers, stylists, and other creative minds. Come see momentum in Sacramento!

Music: 
-Neon Indian is Alan Palomo, the Mexican-born, Texas-raised, 21-year-old synth-wizard who learned his production chops as part of Ghosthustler and honed them as VEGA. Neon Indian’s album Psychic Chasms was designated as the 14th best album of 2009 by Pitchfork and one of the hottest new bands of 2010 by Rolling Stone.

-Civil Twilight The three lifelong friends Steven and Andrew McKellar and Richard Wouters have been playing music together since they were teenagers, emulating the rock music they heard coming out of Europe and America, from Oasis, U2, and Nirvana to The Verve, The Police, Muse, and Radiohead. From Cape Town, South Africa to Nashville, Tennessee, Civil Twilight’s trip has already taken them a long way…and it’s only the beginning.

Complete line-up TBA.

A shuttle will run between Midtown and The Greens Hotel throughout the night.

title: Pop Comedy with Jesse Fernandez
description:
Pop Comedy brings together some of the most talented comedians in the region to discuss pop culture and do comedy! Pop Comedy is hosted by Jesse Fernandez.

Jesse Fernandez is champion of the 2010 National College Funny Film Competition and runner up in 2009. Jesse has performed in the San Francisco SketchFest (an internationally revered festival) in 2008, 2009, and 2010.

title: Bunnies and Bottles
description: April showers brings May flowers--even better--this year, April will host Easter, one of The Park Ultra Lounge's favorite holidays! What's better than a hot bunny stashing away goodies? Join The Park and Nick Willrich as they give away bunny ears, host a $500 best bunny costume contest, and hide Easter eggs in hard to find places filled with the ultimate prizes! This event will be crazy!

title: Humor Times 20/25 Anniversary Variety Show Extravaganza
description:
The Humor Times is celebrating their 20th Anniversary, while Access Sacramento is celebrating their 25th!

Will Durst: America's foremost political comedian and regular columnist for the Humor Times – the man the New York Times calls “Quite possibly the best political satirist working in the country today.”

Sister Swing: A fresh, exciting trio capturing that Andrews Sisters sound, performing a few amusing tunes.

The Anti-Cooperation League: Sacramento’s longest-running improv comedy troupe.

Also appearing: The Sac City Rollers (women's roller derby team), a magician, jugglers, and others to be announced! Even Marilyn Monroe will be there!

title: ¡Bomba!
description:
Do you enjoy hard partying and euphoria? Oh, awesome, because those jerks who threw that one Friday night party that was notoriously chaotic and weird are throwing a party to bring light to an otherwise dark time. Enjoy tunes by Adam J, Shaun Slaughter, and guests.

Expect a lot of getting weird; expect lasers, LEDs, strobes, and smoke (duh); expect a hodge podge of gritty bass, soulful subs, and lovely synths cut with blinding snares and screaming; expect some cute clothes; expect to fall in love with clubbing again; expect clean bathrooms & glassware. And, as cliche as it sounds, expect the unexpected.

What we like? Feel good, hard party music with some weird spices and tropical juices and the occasional rando edible flowers. Shaun's partial to booty. A fun, Friday night event to break up the break up. Come out, support good things, bring a good attitude and cute clothes.

Guests are encouraged to bring rhythm instruments. $2 pints till 11pm, $2 Pabst all night.

title: Island of Black and White
description:
El Dorado Hills duo Island of Black and White makes music that is a sweet, humble yet raw blend of acoustic rock, funky reggae, and soulful blues. With Chris Haislet on guitar, accordion, flute, and vocals and Jake Brutsche on guitar, harmonica, and vocals, it is a mixture like no other.

The unique sound of Island of Black and White captures the attention of those young and old. It is apparent for anyone watching, that the band shares an immense love for music. Not only does the band enjoy playing, but their incredible performances engage all who listen; and the energy is shared with the entire crowd.

Also playing:
Gerald Please

title: Film Screening: The Economics of Happiness
description:
The Economics of Happiness describes a world moving simultaneously in two opposing directions. On the one hand, an unholy alliance of governments and big business continues to promote globalization and the consolidation of corporate power. At the same time, people all over the world are resisting those policies and are coming together to re-build more human scale, ecological economies based on a new paradigm--an economics of localization.

The film shows how globalization breeds cultural self-rejection, competition, and divisiveness; how it structurally promotes the growth of slums and urban sprawl; how it is decimating democracy. We learn about the obscene waste that results from trade for the sake of trade: apples sent from the UK to South Africa to be washed and waxed, then shipped back to British supermarkets; tuna caught off the coast of America, flown to Japan to be processed, then flown back to the US. We hear about the suicides of Indian farmers; about the demise of land-based cultures in every corner of the world.

The second half of The Economics of Happiness provides practical solutions. Arguing that economic localization is a strategic solution multiplier that can solve our most serious problems, the film spells out the policy changes needed to enable local businesses to survive and prosper. We are introduced to community initiatives that are moving the localization agenda forward.

title: Capitol Steps
description:
The Capitol Steps began as a group of Senate staffers who set out to satirize the very people and places that employed them. Their form of musical political satire is sure to get you laughing. Would you rather see famous public figures or hear the Capitol Steps make fun of them?

In the years that followed their initial creation, many of the Steps ignored the conventional wisdom ("Don't quit your day job!"), and although not all of the current members of the Steps are former Capitol Hill staffers, taken together the performers have worked in a total of eighteen Congressional offices and represent 62 years of collective House and Senate staff experience.

Since they began, the Capitol Steps have recorded over 30 albums, including their latest, Liberal Shop of Horrors and Barackin' Around the Christmas Tree. They've been featured on NBC, CBS, ABC, and PBS, and can be heard four times a year on National Public Radio stations nationwide during their Politics Takes a Holiday radio specials.

title: Open Art: Artists & The Environment
description:
Impressionists became renowned for their plein air paintings of outdoor landscapes. Get ready for the launch of the “Summer of Impressionism” and explore how contemporary artists working in various media incorporate the environment in their work to create a sense of place and history. Artists Enid Baxter Blader and Ned Kahn will participate in a panel discussion moderated by Shelly Willis, Manager of the Sacramento Metropolitan Arts Commission’s Art in Public Places Program.

This program is presented in collaboration with Sacramento Metropolitan Art Commission. Open Art is a part of the program series Thursdays ‘til 9. Sponsored by Bank of America. Free with Museum admission.

title: Brianna Lea Pruett
description:
A singer from her earliest days in the sunny mountains of Nothern California, Brianna Lea Pruett’s childhood musical education came mostly from her parents' vinyl collection--a mix of classical and choir, Jimi Hendrix, Roberta Flack, Janis Joplin, Leo Kottke, Leonard Cohen, John Denver, and Carole King.

She sang jazz as a teen in small clubs and with friends, and recorded and released two records while moving around the country, to New York, Los Angeles, and Portland.

Pruett has studied with The Meredith Monk House Foundation in NYC, is a student of native american flute with 2-time Grammy award winner Mary Youngblood, and has shared stages with Jonah Matranga of Far and Gratitude, Jacob Golden, Sean Hayashi, Mark Kozelek of Sun Kil Moon and Red House Painters, Two Sheds, Ruebi Lynn, Nick Jaina, Coal Beautiere, Karl Blau, Lady Lazarus, and others.

Also playing:
Patrick Walsh

title: Chico Mann
description:
The sounds of Africa have taken multi-instrumentalist Chico Mann—aka Marcos García—all over the world. So it's fitting that after spending years learning to speak Afrobeat, albeit with a Cuban accent, Chico Mann has employed several dialects to make a larger musical statement, creating a hybrid of Afro-Cuban rhythms, Afrobeat, and classic freestyle that has emerged to be one of the new, vibrant musical styles of today. This music is good for your mind and behind. And it's always real. The total package.

Also performing:
World Hood (DJ set)
DJ Whores

title: Cocktail Tasting to Benefit Japan Disaster Relief
description:
Ella Dining Room and Bar will be holding a one-time-only tasting of original Artisanal Cocktails featuring Yamazaki Whisky, with proceeds going to Second Harvest Japan’s disaster relief efforts.

Yamazaki representative Neyah White is also an expert Mixologist and a well-known figure in the food and spirits world. He has served up innovative, hand-crafted cocktails at the Redwood Room and Nopa in San Francisco. Ella’s own Bar Manager and Mixologist Rene Dominguez will also host you, as you taste through some amazingly smooth and balanced Japanese Whisky Cocktails. Tastes of the Yamazaki Whiskies will be offered on their own as well so you can see the subtle differences between them.

On the day of the tasting, Neyah and Rene will be breaking down a 300lb block of ice into manageable pieces that they will then use to do traditional Ice Ball Carving (see video) at the tasting.

Built in 1923 in Osaka, Yamazaki is the oldest distillery in Japan. Their Whiskies are exceptional, and Ella had just begun to carry them when the disaster struck.

This is a very rare opportunity to taste some of Neyah White’s fantastic cocktails and to have him on hand as an expert representative of the Yamazaki brand.

description:
The Celebrity Chef Challenge features six professional chefs in a timed culinary competition with surprise ingredients a la the Iron Chef Television Show. Chefs have 45 minutes to turn five secret ingredients into three power-packed dishes in front of one live audience!

But there’s more…as chefs battle to determine, “whose cuisines reigns supreme,” guests enjoy samples from over 100 restaurants, wineries, and breweries while touring the automotive excellence housed by the California Automobile Museum!

We hope your taste buds are ready, because this is one evening you won’t want to miss!

-From Table 260, Executive Chef Richard Pannell

title: Downlow'd with Samo Sound Boy & Shawn Reynaldo
description:
DJ Whores, Gold Sweat, and District 30 present the the second installment of Downlow'd, a bass forward, alternative house monthly showcasing cutting edge DJs, producers, and sounds around the world that are pushing the proverbial envelope of dance music today.

LA based producer, Samo Sound Boy is part of the next generation of young and emerging new artists coming out of the US producing a fresh and lively club sound. Samo’s first release was out on Palms Out Sounds last year and has since taken the world by storm. Samo is sharpening his craft creating a genre of club music mixing the sounds of old Chicago house, hip hop, R'n'B, and club rave.

Shawn Reynaldo has spent most of his professional career in various facets of the music industry, most notably in radio. Shawn also books and throws two of the most forward thinking dance nights in San Francisco: the staple: Tormenta Tropical and the new kid on the block: Icee Hott. Between both nights he has showcased the cream of the crop of DJ and producer talent from around the world. If you have been to either night in the last couple years you already know what to expect from him and his taste in music.

Also enjoy opening sets from Downlow'd residents: DJ Whores, Loco, and Citystate.

title: Palestine Film Festival
description:
Come join for a Palestinian film festival sponsored by the American Association for Palestinian Equal Rights (AAPER) featuring five critically acclaimed films: Salt of this Sea, "One Family in Gaza," With God on Our Side, Something to Prove, and Private.

The Palestine Film Festival is an event to showcase films which help educate Americans across the United States about the situation in Palestine and the need for an equitable U.S. policy toward Palestine that advances freedom and equality for the Palestinian people.

The Film Festival schedule is as follows:
Saturday, April 30:
-3:30pm, Salt of This Sea: A romantic drama about a working-class woman and her experiences traveling back home.
-6pm, "One Family in Gaza": Through one family’s story, the larger tragedy of Gaza is exposed, and the courage and resilience of its people shines through.
-6:45pm, With God on Our Side: A look at what Christian Zionism teaches and more importantly, the real implications it has on the people of the Middle East.

Sunday, May 1:
-1pm, Something to Prove: A documentary following fifteen 15-year old boys from Gaza as they visit the United States for the first time.
-2pm, Private: A Palestinian family is trapped inside a house commandeered by Israeli soldiers.
-3:45pm, "One Family in Gaza"
-5:15pm, With God on Our Side
-7pm, Salt of This Sea

title: Crazy Ballhead & Be Brave Bold Robot
description:
Crazy Ballhead is not your average Hip-Hop artist. 20 years after reciting his first rap, the Sacramento-based emcee still extracts inspiration from all that life has to offer. The good, the bad, and the ugly of the world have helped to sculpt one of the sharpest minds in music today. Crazy Ballhead’s lyrics are an entertaining mix of self-introspection and a reflection of American society past and present.

Be Brave Bold Robot is Soul Coughing meets the Mountain Goats meets Bob Dylan meets Tom Waits meets the Counting Crows meets Calexico meets a good friend for a beer and a Bob Wilson lecture. Singer-songwriter songs about love and grandmothers and justice and life-affirming attitudes. Lots of sweat and passion, several different key meditations, and just enough tempo changes to keep things at least mildly interesting. Be Brave Bold Robot is a joyous celebration of sinful innocense, of deliberate absentmindedness, of Social Obligation that tries not to think too much of itself.

title: Neil Hamburger
description:
Neil Hamburger has appeared on Jimmy Kimmel Live, Tom Green Live, and Tim and Eric Awesome Show Great Job. Gregg Turkington is best known for creating anti-comedian Neil Hamburger. Hamburger’s pacing is off, constantly clears his throat, and most of his jokes fail. Neil’s unique brand of comedy has thrilled, perplexed, and repulsed audiences worldwide. Since 1998, he has released a number of records on Drag City.

Neil will be performing with The Kenny “K-Strass” Strasser Yo-Y0 Extravaganza and Major Entertainer Mike H.

title: Sage Francis
description:
“All great truths begin as blasphemies,” proclaimed the fiery playwright George Bernard Shaw. It’s a sentiment that can be applied exponentially to the works of rapper Sage Francis and his exhilarating new album Li(f)e. Francis has never been afraid to provoke. As a result he is a sometimes polarizing and increasingly important figure in modern music. Adored by many, reviled by a few but never ignored and always essential, Sage Francis has emerged as the reigning agent provocateur of hip hop.

Also playing:
Who Cares

description:
Sac Cycle Chic & Juniper*James present: Vélo & Vintage, a bicycle fashion show that highlights urban cycling as a smart, stylish, and fashionable mode of transport. Vélo and Vintage is a unique fashion show that brings together the thriving, independent communities of cycling and boutiques in Sacramento. Attendees will enjoy a fusion of modern and vintage looks, as each model cycles down the runway. Whether it’s a vintage look with a modern edge or a modern ensemble with a vintage flair, each model displays a high-end yet accessible way to wear the latest trends while still capturing a timeless element.

Vélo & Vintage is held during “May is Bike Mont,” a month-long event that celebrates Sacramento’s Region bicycle culture. The venue, Hot Italian, is the only restaurant in California awarded with the “Bicycle Friendly Business Award” from the League of American Bicyclist.

Darren's contagious charm and vivid imagery paints a picture that is both relatable and one of a kind--no wonder critics nationwide are calling his act "one of a kind" and "a must see."

After appearing in the summer blockbuster Be Cool with John Travolta, Comedy Central's Premium Blend, BET's Comic View, The Tonight Show with Jay Leno, and Comics Unleashed, Darren is quickly becoming a household name. Darren can also be seen on Chelsea Lately on E! and Comics Without Borders on Showtime.

The BFF brings together many creative communities, including fashion, music, and art as well as various bicycling communities--including fixed gear, BMX, and road cycling--over a shared passion for bike riding.

description:
The Harold improv structure is popular at comedy theatres in New York, Chicago, and Los Angeles. Harold is a long form improv structure developed by Del Close. Two Harold teams perform every Wednesday night! These hilarious and smart shows start with a single suggestion which inspires improv scenes that weave together at the end of the show.

Sacramento Comedy Spot students who have completed our Improv 3 Class are eligible to audition for our Harold Teams. Current Harold Teams: Uncomfortably Numb, Yummy Bunsen Burner, and Ambidextrous Octopus.

title: Lydia Loveless
description:
Lydia Loveless, the 19-year old songstress, is worth the chance. One quick listen to Lydia’s hauntingly beautiful voice and you are instantly intrigued. Her craft is put together like a bride on her wedding (albeit a shotgun-type) day; something old, something new, borrowed and blue. Her voice calls on the spirits of past legends like Patsy Cline, Kitty Wells, and Tammy Wynette, even Hank Williams – and living legend, Loretta Lynn.

Her songs are written from her perspective, raw and honest, without watered down concerns of pleasing the masses. The juxtaposition of Lydia’s timeless, sagacious voice singing out the concerns and perspective of a young turk is quite the introduction.

description:
Gene Pompa, comedian and writer, was born in East Los Angeles, California. He has been a Mexican-American most of his life, except for a few years during the 1970s, when he was a practicing Chicano. Gene became a product of his multi-ethnic upbringing in the suburbs of Los Angeles and it was this diverse background which ultimately inspired Gene to incorporate universal themes into his stand-up comedy and writing.

Gene's television credits include several appearances on NBC's Late Night with Conan O'Brien and CBS's Late Late Show with Craig Kilborn. Pompa has also starred in his own half hour Comedy Central special as well as a 30 minute comedy showcase on SiTV. His acting has been featured on FOX's In Living Color, CBS's Style & Substance, and The Brothers Garcia on Nickelodean. You may have also seen Gene on Showtime, HBO, MTV, MUN2, Galavision, or the Game Show Network, as well as the feature film Just Go With It.

description:
Join Clemón for Happy Hour at 3 Fires Lounge inside the Marriot Residence Inn every Tuesday. Relax with a glass of wine and listen to his worldly influence of his hometown, Barbados. Clemón infuses a West Indian sound with American alternative rock and jazz.

His voice is a deep, sultry style with a raspy touch in the alternative rock and folk genre as he performs his original songs. Each cover song is tailored to a folk and jazz sound that range in the 1960s-1990s to reach many audiences.

Live performances by Clemón are perfect for private functions and intimate settings. An experience of a deep sultry voice creates a sexy setting for private parties, weddings, and lounges.

title: An Evening with David Sedaris
description:
David Sedaris, NPR humorist and best-selling author, comes to the Crest Theatre in Sacramento! With sardonic wit and incisive social critiques, David Sedaris has become one of America ’s pre-eminent humor writers. The great skill with which he slices through cultural euphemisms and political correctness proves that Sedaris is a master of satire and one of the most observant writers addressing the human condition today.

David Sedaris is the author of the bestsellers Barrel Fever and Holidays on Ice, as well as collections of personal essays, Naked, Me Talk Pretty One Day, and Dress Your Family in Corduroy and Denim, each of which became immediate bestsellers. He is the editor of an anthology of stories, Children Playing Before a Statue of Hercules: An Anthology of Outstanding Stories. His essays appear regularly in Esquire and The New Yorker.

Sedaris and his sister, Amy Sedaris, have collaborated under the name “The Talent Family” and have written several plays which have been produced at La Mama, Lincoln Center, and The Drama Department in New York City. These plays include Stump the Host, Stitches, One Woman Shoe, which received an Obie Award, Incident at Cobbler’s Knob, and The Book of Liz, which was published in book form by Dramatist’s Play Service. His collection of essays, titled When You Are Engulfed in Flames, was published in June 2008.

description:
Together, California Auto Museum and MaverickPhotography.us bring you CAM Photo. With nearly 20 incredible talented photographers MaverickPhotography.us is the official designated photography team that makes up the museums photo department.

Couple a wonderful education center and auditorium for classrooms, a floor of vintage and exquisite automobiles, and a team qualified and eager to mentor and teach photographers, you have a great recipe for informative, educational, and fun photography workshops.

Taking you from basic to advanced throughout the year, anyone with a desire to learn photography will find themselves growing and developing their photography skills right away.

The team of Maverick Photographers are easy going and look forward to taking their time, at your pace to help you learn this ever expanding and changing art.

Join us the 4th Tuesday of each month and watch yourself grow into an accomplished photographer.

title: Lecture Series: Color Transformations in Impressionism – In the Eye
description:
The first of this three-part lecture series, examines the science of color as it was understood during the age of Impressionism and the challenges to this understanding when confronted with the color transformations found in the aging or ailing eye. Dr. John S. Werner, Distinguished Professor at the University of California, Davis Eye Center, will discuss how Impressionist painters, from Giverny to the Monterey Peninsula, attempted to capture the fleeting effects of light and color present in the retinal image.

On Tuesday, May 17, the topic will be “On the Canvas,” and the topic on Tuesday, June 14, will be “Across the Life Span."

Event is free with Museum admission.

title: 1906 Earthquake Living History Program
description:
Step back in time and witness volunteers and staff of the Capitol Museum costumed in the attire of the period re-enacting scenes in response to one of America’s greatest disasters--the 1906 San Francisco Earthquake and Fire.

Meet Governor George Pardee as he receives a telegram from President Theodore Roosevelt offering $1 million for disaster relief. Attorney General Ulysses S. Webb, Secretary of State Charles Curry, and Treasurer Truman Reeves will be on hand to help the refugees, some of whom camped out on the Capitol grounds and at Sutter’s Fort. Meet the women of Sacramento who assisted the San Francisco families to obtain meal tickets, clothing, and blankets.

This glimpse into turn-of-the-20th-century California history is free for everyone.

The two hour workshop will include a lecture, a hands-on examination of typical varieties, and a short walk through the garden looking at some of the garden's nearly 500 old and historic roses.

title: We Won The Vote: 100 Years of Equal Suffrage in California
description:
After a long and innovative campaign, California women won the right to vote in a special election on October 10, 1911. The 1911 California victory for woman suffrage was the culmination of a long, hard-fought battle to win political freedom and basic civil rights. California was the sixth western state to win the vote for women, inspiring suffragists nationwide and increasing national attention on what had long been a controversial political and moral debate. With the 1911 triumph of equal enfranchisement, six-hundred thousand California women doubled the number of women who could vote in the United States.

The campaigns in the West, and California's in particular, set new standards for bold actions, new ideas, and successful techniques for efforts in other states across the nation. It helped to build up electoral power and political support in the nation's capital to finally ensure passage of the 19th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution, granting American women the right to vote in 1920.

This exhibition will feature historical photographs, period campaign materials, objects, and oral histories designed to guide the visitor through the history of the successful 1911 campaign for woman's suffrage in California. Highlighted are specific issues and activities of the California campaign, and how the state's experience related to and dramatically affected the way the national campaign played out over the next decade. Visitors will actively engage in the debate over women's right to vote through the incorporation of historical questions, objective presentations of both sides of the issue, and interactive displays.

A preliminary panel exhibition opened on March 3, 2011. The full expanded exhibit, featuring artifacts from the Center for Sacramento History, is scheduled to open June 10, 2011 and run through September 15, 2011. It will then move to the State Capitol Museum from October 1, 2011 through October 1, 2012.

title: California Automobile Museum’s Annual Fundraising Dinner
description: Spend an evening raising funds for the California Automobile Museum. Dennis Gage of "My Classic Car" will be the guest speaker. Enjoy dinner, silent and live auctions, and a night of entertainment to support the Museum.

title: Gold, Greed, & Speculation: The Beginnings of Sacramento City
description:
The Historic Old Sacramento Foundation and the Sacramento History Museum are proud to present Gold, Greed & Speculation: The Beginnings of Sacramento City in the museum’s lobby gallery. Visitors have the unique opportunity to explore the city’s first fifty years. The exhibit storyline goes beyond Sacramento’s origins as a gold rush boomtown, as the story is more complex than just miners seeking their fortunes in gold. Sacramento's early days are marked by surprises and contrasts, riches and scarcity, generosity and greed, and violence and beauty.

Visitors can explore this history and discover the colorful characters from a variety of cultures; vast wealth gained, lost, and gained again. They can meet the individuals that forged the city, better understand its development and how its citizens withstood catastrophic floods, fires, and epidemics in the first years of its existence. Sacramento’s citizens persevered and rebuilt the city again and again playing an instrumental role in establishing it as the capital city of the State of California.

title: The Community Gallery
description:
As a community, Sacramento has changed greatly over the city's relatively young history and the Community Gallery richly details its growth in chronological order. Visitors learn about the first people, the Nisenan & Maidu Indian Nations, through a collection of baskets, jewelry, and weapons.

As you leave the Native American exhibit, you say goodbye to that way of life. In 1826, tempted by the abundance of fur-bearing animals, trapper Jedehiah Smith, among hundreds of men and fur companies settled this land. Of course, this huge migration had a disastrous effect on the land and native people. Animals were massacred and the Indians became infected with malaria and small pox. Thousands died.

Through carefully preserved correspondence, photographs, historic fashions, and heirlooms, guests wind through the exhibit and see a city grow from a dusty miner town of the 1850s to an early 20th century where new forms of transportation and communication were introduced. The exhibits then tell the stories of Sacramento and America in a World War, Japanese-Americans being interned, and how the famous Dunlap family turned their home into a successful neighborhood restaurant.

title: The Agricultural Gallery
description: Sacramento is located in the heart of the Central Valley—one of the richest agricultural areas in the world. Agricultural pioneers are renowned for devising ingenious methods to make farm work more efficient and profitable. In this gallery, visitors see the original McCormick Reaper that revolutionized grain farming. In addition, the beautiful cannery label collection is a testament to the industry that dominated Sacramento in the early part of the 20th century.

title: Going Green: It's Cool For the Planet
description: On Earth Day 2009, the Museum opened Going Green: It’s Cool for the Planet, an exhibit displaying and telling the story of clean fuel alternatives. The exhibit includes a 1913 Rauch & Lang Electric car; one of only twelve 1997 General Motors EV1s still in existence; a 2000 Daimler-Benz NeCar 4a Fuel Cell Vehicle; a 1972 Datsun electric car; a CHP Custom Electric Chopper; a 2007 BMW Hydrogen 7 and our newest additions: two Nissan Electric Vehicles--a Hypermini and an Altra.

description:
Local seniors are invited to join residents of River’s Edge Retirement Community for a luncheon program where Barbara Kennedy will talk about her exploits as a World War II pilot with the Women Airforce Service Pilots.

title: Hula Workshop
description:
Interested in learning hula and Hawaiian culture? Halau 'O Keikiali'i - Sacramento is open to all ages; men, women, and children. Whether you are a beginner or experienced, please come and join us for an educational workshop.

Hâlau o Keikiali`i - Sacramento, Hula Me Ke Aloha is a Sacramento, California - based hula hâlau. Established in 2001 with the blessings of Kumu Hula Uncle John Keli`iokahekili Manuia, Hula Me Ke Aloha has built a strong foundation on tradition, hula and `ohana. After the passing of Uncle John, the Hâlau now formally falls under the lineage of Kumu Hula Kawika Keikiali`i Alfiche of Hâlau o Keikiali’i in South San Francisco. The hâlau will continue our traditional education and journey under his guidance.

We are an authentic Hula Hâlau that is dedicated to follow the protocol and customs of our lineage. It is a hula lineage that reaches back to the late 1700's, one we are proud of and dedicated to preserving.

We hope to see you there! Mahalo!

title: 2011 Amgen Tour of California
description:
World-Class Professional Cycling Race on the Streets of Sacramento for Stage 2 of the race!

One of the longest stages of the race, Stage 2 has “sprinter” written all over the race route. Starting at the site of the 1960 Winter Olympics and one of the largest ski resorts in the U.S., Squaw Valley, the riders will head north to the town of Truckee and then west past the infamous and rugged Donner’s Pass. At 7,100’, this will be the only KOM of Stage 2. From here it will be a more than 7’000’ of descending to the State’s Capitol (elev. 25’). The route will pass through Nevada City, California (last year’s official Start City) and after working its way west for several miles, the peloton will turn south and head through one of the country’s premier military installations, Beale Air Force Base. From there it will be a fast ride through the suburbs of Sacramento. Entering the circuit just past the finish line in Sacramento, the riders will begin the first of two circuit laps with a finish at the State Capitol building. You can expect the crowds in Sacramento to be some of the largest for the entire race.

Click here for a detailed route map.

There will be a Free Lifestyle Festival  sponsored by MBT footwear at the Capitol in conjunction with the finish.

title: Benefit Country Concert with Julie Roberts
description:
Nashville recording artist Julie Roberts will be performing for a small, intimate gathering. This benefit concert raises funds for the Accelerated Reader (AR) program at Breen Elementary School. California schools have been hard hit by recent budget cuts and library funds are one of the first items on the chopping block. 100% of the net proceeds benefit Breen's AR program. This family friendly acoustic concert includes a fabulous BBQ dinner and is sponsored by Coca Cola. Ticket sales are limited.

Perhaps best known for her smash hit "Break Down Here" from her self-titled debut album, Roberts recently revealed on her blog that she is also putting the finishing touches on her third album. Roberts has released two albums on the Mercury Nashville label, one being certified gold. She has had music videos on both CMT and GAC Television. This will be the first new music from her in five years. She will be performing some of her new music during Breen Elementary's fundraiser.

The Midtown Bazaar honors Sacramento’s long history of invention, commitment to the arts, and entrepreneurial spirit. Much as Sacramento’s original Public Market at the corner of 13 & J Streets, the Midtown Bazaar enlivens the centralized Midtown Sacramento corner. Embracing Midtown’s avant-garde personality, the market promotes community while providing artisans, musicians, local and organic farmers, small businesses, and eateries an opportunity to engage with customers. title: Ruth Eckland's- At the Edge of the World
description:
At the Edge of the World is a multi-channel video installation by Ruth Eckland with music by Matt DiFonzo. Ruth Eckland’s At the Edge of the World is a meditation on the fragility, ambiguity, and uncertainty of what we think of as reality. Halcyon beach scenes are layered and juxtaposed with television news images of the sudden, catastrophic destruction of the Japanese tsunami. Unidentifiable figures pass through obliviously, or motionlessly bear witness. Borealis-like flashes of light signify another dimension beyond the quotidian, the cataclysmic, in which transcendence and illumination beckon.

As in much of the artist’s recent work, the video is altered to resemble experimental film or painting, creating metaphoric visions as if in a dream. Interpretation, including associative narrative, becomes a collaboration with the viewer. To aid in this process, sound is integral, much as in music videos or film scores. L.A. composer and producer Matt DiFonzo has written the music for the piece, adding layers of subtext to the visual images and creating a more evocative, immersive experience.

Eckland has exhibited throughout the U.S. and internationally and finds it particularly gratifying to discover the connection that viewers in countries as diverse as Costa Rica, Kazakhstan, Germany, Singapore, and China have made with the work. Some universal language seems to be communicated, some global core touched. Or, as Kenneth Baker has said in one of his many insightful reviews of Eckland’s work over the past few years in The San Francisco Chronicle, “Eckland handles video like the medium of collective dreams that we share without knowing it. Apparently she wants us to know it.”

Wicked tells the story of their remarkable odyssey, how these two unlikely friends grow to become the Wicked Witch of the West and Glinda the Good.

Compassion!, The Vagina Monologues) and features musical staging by Tony Award winner Wayne Cilento (Aida, The Who’s Tommy, How To Succeed…). title: The Real Mayan Calendar: An Introduction to the Mayan Underworlds
description:
The Universal Co-Creation Cycle started on March 9 and it is off with a bang! See the Timeline for the Universal Co-Creation Cycle. But what does that even mean? While interest in the Mayan’s grand calendar systems has increased as we approach 2012, the confusion surrounding the implications of this information has hit an all time high. Is the world ending? Is the calendar just re-starting? What will happen after 2012? These are just a few of the common questions surrounding this very misunderstood topic.

Join us for a class where Chris will briefly explore the work of Carl Johan Calleman and Ian Lungold in unraveling the mysteries of the Mayan calendar.

In this class you will learn how to distinguish the parts of the calendar that are re-calibrating from the parts that are actually terminating. You’ll learn about evolution through the “Mayan Underworlds” which form the backbone of the Mayan calendar system and which explain the increase in the frequency of change over time. Finally, you’ll learn how the process of creation has been occurring according to a timeline and that it is THIS process that is actually ending.

After the process of creation is complete…what will be the creation? Finally, according to the work of Calleman and Lungold the calendar system representing the process of creation does not actually end on December 21, 2012! Join us and find out when it actually DOES end and what this may mean for humanity as a whole.

Instructor: Christopher Robert Taylor. See a playlist preview of this class.

title: Citizens Academy
description:
Meet your public safety leaders, officials, officers and experts. Learn about racial profiling, gang and hate crimes, in-car cameras, internal affairs, “three strikes” and more. Lunch with judges, tour the county jail and communication center and see a taser demonstration.

The Sacramento County District Attorney’s Office, the Sacramento Police Department, and the Sacramento Sheriff’s Department are proud to announce its 11th Citizens Academy course. In an effort to improve communication, relationships, and provide a better understanding between ethnic and cultural communities and the criminal justice system, District Attorney Jan Scully formed the Citizens Academy.

Since the start of the academy in 2002, there have been ten graduating classes with more than 500 participants. In partnership with the Sacramento Police Department and Sacramento Sheriff’s Department, Jan Scully has brought this program to the community to provide an overview of the criminal justice system (law enforcement roles, responsibilities, and challenges) and to engage citizens from all backgrounds in communication, participation and mutual learning about issues within the criminal justice system. The course continues to make a great impact on multicultural and multi-ethnic sensitivity within the criminal justice community.

Representatives from the DA’s office, the judiciary, public defense, law enforcement, and community organizations answer community questions, address their concerns and demonstrate a commitment to building, bridges between the criminal justice system and the various ethnic, racial and faith-based communities. Citizens Academy is hosted by the District Attorney’s Office in partnership with the Sacramento Police Department, and Sacramento Sheriff’s Department.

title: Work by Danäe Anderson
description:
Skinner Howard Gallery' presents works by Danäe Anderson. Movement and music vitally inflect the improvised choreography of the paintings. The relationship with the "canvas" is intense and instinctive, accessing and allowing marks that arise through the uncensored conscious. Chance associations arise from the immediacy/physicality of intuition and observation. The residue of these actions reveal a visual narrative that documents and honors human experience. A deep overlay of play, language, events, dreams, objects, the self, the ordinary, sense/nonsense, the seen/unseen, the ancestors and progeny, memory and daily experience is recorded.

In indigenous cultures, things done (the making of objects: art), and things happening (music and dance) are one.
Action / process become the principal mode of thought. The artist is called to respond to things happening and so documents the imperatives of life.

With a selection of both new and classic kiddie rides, riders of all ages can experience the thrills of the carnival.

title: Book Cover Drawing Class
description: Design an alternate book cover for a much loved--or much loathed--book of your choice. Winners will be selected by library staff and their work will be displayed in the library for the summer.

title: Musical Charis, Blvd Park Welcome Back Show
description: null

title: Sacramento State Vocal Jazz Ensembles
description: Sacramento State’s Vocal Jazz Ensembles, winner of numerous Downbeat jazz awards, perform.
