description: Choral music will ring out when Sacramento State’s three choirs perform.

title: Vocal Art Ensemble: Cloudburst--Sounds of Nature
description:
Davis-based mixed a capella choral group Vocal Art Ensemble presents its Spring concert series, Cloudburst--Sounds of Nature, painting a picture of the natural world with playful madrigals, stunning modern works, and evocative pieces that span the world’s cultures. Glimpse birdsong at breaking dawn, whimsical frog and firefly, shimmering ocean, thundering rainstorm, and quiet, earthly rest.

Featuring delicate instrumentals and contemplative poetry, Cloudburst explores the wonders across our beautiful Earth. The finale will be Eric Whitacre’s Cloudburst, evoking the sounds of a thunderstorm through voices, sound effects, and the assistance of the Juuliebells handbell choir from the Unitarian Universalist Church of Davis. The concerts also feature instrumentals by group members and poetry and translations presented by Gerry Hair.

The twenty-one experienced singers of the Vocal Art Ensemble (VAE) rehearse several times weekly in the director’s Davis home. Since its inception in February 2008 VAE has presented seven concert sets and, in September 2010, traveled to Ireland for a ten-day performance tour. The group has created two CDs of past performances, available for sale at concerts. Performing throughout Yolo, Sacramento, and Solano Counties, VAE relies on concert donations to defray costs.

title: String Project Concert
description: The String Project of Sacramento State is a flagship program in which groups of children in the third grade on up are taught violin and cello by University undergraduate and graduate teachers. Come see them in concert!

title: Jammin' in the Park 2- Starring Malo
description:
Celebrate the 40th anniversary of legendary Latino rockers Malo with their encore performance at "Jammin' in the Park 2." La Raza Galería Posada, Sacramento's not-for-profit midtown gallery and cultural center, will bring back their highly successful family day of Latino celebration with music, poetry, food, arts & crafts.

This year, La Raza Galería honors Fathers of the Chicano Arts Movement on this Father's Day weekend event. The 12-piece Latin Rock legend Malo, starring guitarist Jorge Santana and lead singer Arcelio Garcia thrilled the capacity crowd last year. Additional performers will be announced soon.

title: Flame: Live in Concert at the 2011 Youth Summit
description:
St. Paul Oak Park Community Outreach in association with E.W.B. Entertainment, Inc. presents Grammy, Stellar, and Dove Award Nominee & Clear Sight Music recording artist Flame with guest performances by V Rose, SPEC, and F.A.R.

Flame's new album (released 12/2010) debuted: #1 on Billboard Gospel, #5 on Billboard Christian, #11 on Billboard Independant, #17 on Billboard Rap Chart.

This is the Opening Concert for the 2011 Annual Youth Summit, which also includes Keynote Speaker Stephen Stafford.

title: Earth Day Special
description: Join M!X Downtown for an Earth Day Special! Come out for twice the DJ--DJ Mike Moss & DJ Elliot Estes take control of the decks. Enjoy Club Classics, '80s remixes, and essential pop/top 40! Be kind to your Earth <3

title: Royal Honeymoon
description: The Park Ultra Lounge puts on their proper pants for The Royal Honeymoon: a black and white ball in honor of William & Kate. Everyone loves a wedding reception, so let's show Great Britain how The Park gets down and celebrates. All those in a black or white dress will get in free before 11pm.

title: Japan XOXO: Dance for Japan
description: Japan XOXO is a benefit dance party for Japan. All proceeds from the door go to The Red Cross. Join local DJs Shaun Slaughter, Adam J, Sam I Jam, and Taylor Cho as they do what they love to support an amazing cause.

title: Democratic Convention Afterparty
description: Join The Park Ultra Lounge & DJ Peeti-V for the 2011 California Democratic Convention Afterparty. Whether you're red or blue, come out and party (like a jack-ass)! Enjoy the huge outdoor patio and our brand new crazy sound system.

title: Laugh Out Loud: Comedy/Music Show
description: Laugh Out Loud is a comedy & music show featuring comedians Bob Fernandez, Rick Pulido, and Del Van Dyke (Voted Best Comic in Sac) with live band Not for Profit. All proceeds to the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society.

title: O'Drinko de Mayo
description:
Every year de Vere's celebrate the San Patricio's, a band of Irish men that bravely fought along side Mexican Soldiers during the Mexican American War. These men were later caught and tried for deserting the American army, for which they paid the ultimate sacrifice and were publicly hanged. In honor of this sacrifice de Vere's host a party every Cinco de Mayo for the St. Patrick's Battalion.

Join until the beer is gone for $2 Coronas, $2 Tacos, $3 Milagro tequila shots, and $4 Margaritas!

title: Lights Down Low with Sinden & Light Year
description:
Sinden may be best known for his work with Herve as the Count & Sinden ("Beeper" and "Mystery Jets" on After Dark), or possibly for his remixes of Basement Jaxx, Miike Snow, Bjork, Mark Ronson, and Ardman Van Helden. Sinden is a world class producer and DJ whose label Grizzly is churning out top notch tracks every month.

Straddling a bass heavy club sound that also encompasses left-field rock music and global beats, Sinden is renowned for his genre-blending DJ sets, cracklin’ hot radio show, and banging remixes.

Light Year a.k.a. Flight Facilities are one of the most exciting new artists coming out on Australia's Bang Gang Imprint. With remixes of Tiga, Classixx, Bag Raiders, and Surking under their belt, plus a slew of amazing originals, they are quickly becoming an "it" name in dance.

Plus, resident DJs Shaun Slaughter (Rough House/D.A.M.B./Lipstick), Adam J (Rough House), and Alx-T (Visao Media) spinning house music and other dance floor gems.

Enjoy awesome drinks and the amazing outdoor patio!

title: Planet Rock inside The Station
description: Are you old school? Coming to Roseville straight out of Frisco is DJ Chill and Midnite Cru bringing old school in the mixx every Friday at Planet Rock inside The Station. Get off your sofa and come get your dance on! This is for the mature party people.

title: That Championship Season
description: That Championship Season is a play that won the 1972 Pulitzer Prize and the original Broadway production won the 1973 New York Drama Critics' Circle, Drama Desk, and Tony awards for best play. The setting is 1972 at the Coach's home in Scranton, Pennsylvania. On the twentieth anniversary of their victory in the Pennsylvania state championship game, four members of the starting lineup of a Catholic high school basketball team have gathered to celebrate. The coach is terminally ill, and this reunion may be their last chance to reminisce with him.

title: Linda Bair Dance Company: Burst
description: The Linda Bair Dance Company is celebrating the culmination of a jam-packed dance season with Burst, an exciting, eclectic evening of contemporary dance featuring three premieres and two of the company’s signature dance pieces. Bair’s five dances explore themes as diverse as the isolation of being in a foreign place to the light-hearted water dances of Esther Williams with music equally varied.

title: True Life Stories 2
description:
The second True Life Stories project is a change of pace from the first production. It has its own power and intensity at times, but it is an exploration of the heart and of love, and is a bit more lyrical. The project is a laboratory of sorts, experimenting with playwriting (which has to come fast) and directing, of course. It is essentially an exploratory journey into the heart of acting, an invigorating theatrical process in the creation of a unique new play.

Five actors include their experiences in a theatrical mosaic about love–the highs and the lows.
venue: Cosumnes River College Performing Arts Center (formerly River Stage Theatre)

title: Corazón de México: Compañía Mazatlán: Bellas Artes
description: Compania Mazatlan Bellas Artes is one of California’s most esteemed Mexican folkdance companies. Under the artistic direction of Steven Valencia, 35 exceptional dancers, mariachis, and other musicians present a lively and passionate rendition of Mexican culture, both past and present. For lovers of fine ballet folklórico dance, the “Corazón de México” (“Heart of Mexico”) is colorful and creative, featuring indigenous and folkloric dance costumes and traditions, with accents on their award–winning pieces performed in international competitions.

title: Jesus Hopped the A Train
description: When he was a child, Angel Cruz believed that Jesus hopped the "A" train to save his life. Now, he is in 23-hour lockdown on Rikers Island, awaiting trial for killing a religious cult leader who got a grip on his best friend. His fellow inmate, Lucius, is a serial killer on death row who has found Christianity. He tries to convince Angel that God can save him; meanwhile, Angel’s lawyer says she can get him acquitted. What is the real way to salvation, and how is it defined?
venue: Capital Stage - Aboard the Riverboat Delta King

title: "The Importance of Being Earnest" and "Victoria at 18"
description:
Victoria at 18 (a one-act production by Tim Kelly) is a historical drama about the clash of wills between Victoria and her mother, the strong-willed Duchess of Kent, who has always refused to let her daughter grow up. Vicky must sleep in a cot by her mother’s bed, let her mother make every decision—in effect, speak for her. But now she’s 18, and the very next morning, without asking permission, she moves into a bedroom of her own! The next day a dramatic encounter follows as the young girl learns that she is now queen.

The Importance of Being Earnest (by Oscar Wilde. One Act Adaptation by IE Clark) is a farcical comedy in which the protagonists maintain fictitious personas in order to escape burdensome obligations. Working within the social conventions of late Victorian London, the play’s major themes are the triviality with which it treats institutions as serious as marriage, and the resulting satire of Victorian ways.

Opening Night includes a “Better than Champagne” and Cake reception with the cast after the show (May 5, make your reservations early!). For Mother’s Day (May 8), Mothers get in free! (with the purchase of one general admission or student ticket or two child tickets—must be purchased in advance, not available at the door).
venue: Victory Life Church (Facility used by Generous Donation)

title: Poetry Reading: Gillian Wegner & Gerald Fleming
description:
The Poetry Night Reading Series is proud to welcome poets Gillian Wegener and Gerald Fleming.

Gillian Wegener is one of the shining lights of Modesto poetry. Her poems have been published in In the Grove, RUNES, The Ledge, The Mad Poets' Review, Central Valley Poetry Journal, and Zambomba, among others. She received her BA from Humboldt State University and an MA in Writing from the University of San Francisco. Born in New York, but now living in Modesto, California, Gillian Wegener teaches English at Oakdale Junior High School.

Gerald Fleming’s poetry and prose poems have appeared widely over the past thirty years. He has won numerous awards and fellowships, and between 1995 and 2000 he edited and published the literary magazine Barnabe Mountain Review, whose archives can be found at U.C. Berkeley's Bancroft Library. His book of poems Swimmer Climbing Onto Shore was published by Sixteen Rivers Press in 2005. He taught in the San Francisco public schools for thirty-seven years, and has published three books for teachers, the most recent of which is Rain, Steam, and Speed. He lives in Lagunitas, California.

title: Peace. Love. Swap: 1st Annual Swap-a-Palooza
description: If you like freecyle, you'll love this! Celebrate Earth Day, do your spring cleaning, and bring down all your gently used (clean!) items that you don't use anymore and swap them out for items that you need. You can bring anything (that you can carry): women's, men's, kid's clothing & accessories, books, movies, music, electronics, kitchenware, tools, office supplies, garden items, small furniture, and accessories. It's the ultimate recycling event.

title: Styles of Paradise Charity Fashion Show
description:
Enjoy an evening of fashion, music, and fun at the Sacramento State Student Fashion Association (SFA)'s charity fashion show highlighting student designers and stylists in Sacramento. The benefiting charity is the Autism Center for Excellence at Sacramento State in honor of April National Autism Awareness Month.

Designers: Julian Gutierrez, Deneen Hayes, Alisa Correa, Christen Brown, Alexis Diaz, Erika Louie, Anakarina Pimental, Tamika Bellamy, Lacey Taylor and Samantha Rachele, Noognuv Thao, and Kira Martinson

Come mingle with designers, stylists, models, and SFA at the Launch Party the Tuesday before the show.

title: Justice/Brilliance: Mark Gonzales & Remi Kanazi
description:
Justice/Brilliance is two poets affirming life, demanding justice, and celebrating struggles: Mark Gonzales, HBO Def Poet and brilliant wordsmith celebrating cultural intersections across all borders and Remi Kanazi, currently on his Poetic Injustice book tour.

This event takes place in Del Norte, Room 1004 on the Sacramento State Campus.

title: Remaking California: Breaking Political Gridlock
description:
The Center for Sacramento History, in association with the Sacramento History Foundation, will host a panel discussion with the authors of the recent book, Remaking California: Reclaiming the Public Good. The panel will delve into the causes of California’s governmental gridlock, the effects on its citizens and environment, and prospects for restoring a healthy democracy.

The panel includes: Dr. Jeffrey Lustig, emeritus professor of government, California State University, Sacramento; Dan Walters, political columnist for the Sacramento Bee; Lenny Goldberg, executive director of the California Tax Reform Association; and Osha Meserve, a Sacramento attorney specializing in environmental matters.

The speakers will examine the problems of how California is governed – from the constraints of the state’s current constitution and the implications of Proposition 13, to the ails of the Delta and the challenge of meeting the needs of a diverse population. The evening will shed light on why reforming California state governance is important; how it should be done, and why Sacramentans should care about these issues.

The authors will sign copies of the book, Remaking California, at the conclusion of the presentation. The book will be available for purchase that evening; cost is $15, cash or check only please.

This project was made possible by financial support from the Sacramento History Foundation and the Sacramento Convention Center.

title: Jane's Walk: Midtown
description:
William Burg, historian, Sacramento Old City Association Board Member, and author of Sacramento’s Streetcars, will guide this tour of Midtown’s mixed-use business corridors and adjacent residential neighborhoods, from the days of Sutter through the streetcar era to the present day. The tour will focus on walkability, transit, mixed-use neighborhoods, and Midtown’s legacy as a regional epicenter of creativity and art.

Jane’s Walk USA is a series of free neighborhood walking tours, inspired by the books of legendary neighborhood advocate Jane Jacobs (author of The Death and Life of Great American Cities) that helps put people in touch with their environment and with each other, by bridging social and geographic gaps and creating a space for cities to discover themselves.

Sacramento’s Jane’s Walk series incorporates elements of urban planning, neighborhood advocacy, urban history, and architectural history, to demonstrate how a neighborhood’s physical form promotes its walkability, sustainability, and economic and social vitality.

title: Ride for Earth 2011
description:
Everyone is welcome to Ride for Earth. What better way to celebrate Earth Day than to spend some quality time with Mother Nature and good people on bikes! The ride will begin at Practical Cycle in Old Sacramento. Riders are encouraged to bring their own bikes, but free rentals will be available by reservation only. The ride will traverse leisurely for about a mile along the Sacramento River to its confluence with the American River in Discovery Park and back to Practical Cycle. Afterward, enjoy Rainforest Alliance certified decaf from Chocolate Fish Coffee, followed by some easy post-ride stretches with Michelle from It's All Yoga.

Sponsored by: Practical Cycle, It's All Yoga, Chocolate Fish Coffee, Velocab, and Sac Cycle Chic.

title: de Vere's Irish Pub Derby Day
description: You don't have to be in Kentucky to get lucky! Join for de Vere's Derby Day and enjoy $5 Mint Juleps & $5 Pimm's Cup specials, plus a Big Hat party for the ladies. de Vere's Chefs will be making some good old southern favorites for you to share with your friends while enjoying this age old American tradition. Come watch the race with friends and family at de Vere's Irish Pub.

title: Hike of the Month
description: These short local hikes are a great way to get to know what’s in your own backyard. Every third Friday, you’ll have an opportunity to visit a new destination.

title: Paria Canyon Backpacking
description:
Escape the everyday as you explore one of Backpacker Magazine’s December 2001 “Best Hikes.” While traveling through Paria Canyon’s Wire Pass you will squeeze through slot canyons so thin that you just might have to take your pack off. You will travel through Buckskin Gulch, the world’s longest slot canyon. And that’s only the first day!

As the canyon widens the walls reach up to 2000 feet high. With a short side hike up Wrather Canyon you will have the chance to see the 246 foot Wrather Arch, the 4th largest natural arch in the world and the longest of any outside of Utah. Explore old abandoned homesteads and try to decipher the ancient petroglyphs.

After the five day 44 mile hike kick your boots off in the cool grasses of Lonely Dell Ranch watered by the original natural irrigation system designed in 1883. If the desert heat is too much, end your expedition with a dip in the chilly Colorado River. This trip includes transportation, guides, group gear, camping fees, and all meals.

title: Midtown Urban Art Bike Tour
description:
Enjoy a guided 90 minute tour with a perspective on the amazing and diverse murals that shape the urban art landscape of Midtown. Your thoughts are encouraged and welcomed in an open forum of discovery. See art, give your opinion, and have fun riding a bike! Bring a friend and have lunch afterward in Midtown.

Cost includes bike, guide, water bottle, and snack. Tours start and end on 23rd Street in the block between K Street and L Street.

title: Yosemite Backpacking
description:
With a view that will rival the splendor of Half Dome, Smith Peak is a chance to see some of the best that Yosemite has to offer. This secret gem of the park allows you to enjoy everything Yosemite without the crowds. At its more than 7000 foot summit, Smith Peak allows you a birds eye view of the Hetch Hetchy reservoir, as well as several of the waterfalls that make the area a favorite among backpackers.

The 360 degree view will take your breath away on this challenging and rewarding trip. Beginner backpackers welcome. Trip includes transportation, knowledgeable guides, equipment, dinners, and entrance/permit fees. A pre-trip meeting occurs the Monday before the trip.

title: Grant Napear's "Fairway To The Future"
description:
"Fairway to the Future" benefits The FUTURE Foundation of Sacramento. As a board member and volunteer mentor with the FUTURE Foundation of Sacramento, Grant Napear (TV voice of the Kings and sports radio talk show host on Sportsline 1140) hosts this annual golf tournament to raise funds to help disadvantaged youth make college an obtainable goal. The tournament benefits the FUTURE Foundation of Sacramento, Inc.--a non-profit 501(c)(3) corporation that provides both volunteer mentoring and funding to students in support of their college education.

Golfer package includes: Round of golf at Catta Verdera Country Club, lunch, massage on practice tee, hole-in-one prizes, photo of foursome, tee prizes, awards dinner & live auction, meet celebrity guests.

title: Critical Mass
description:
Sacramento’s Critical Mass ride has been going since April 2007. Rides start up and then die again, but we’re trying to keep this one alive. Any and all cyclists are encouraged to join us for a lawful, respectable, and fun group ride that meanders through the streets of the grid. We have no leaders and no set routes. We just want to ride!

Critical Mass is an event typically held on the last Friday of every month in cities around the world where bicyclists and, less frequently, skateboarders, roller bladers, roller skaters and other self-propelled commuters take to the streets en masse. Critical Mass events have no leader, and have no officially-stated message, though it is largely understood to promote alternative (non-motorized) modes of transport and to raise awareness of safety issues facing commuters using non-motorized forms of transport alongside motor vehicles.

Participants meet at a set location and time and enjoy the security and companionship of traveling as a group through city streets.

title: Big Wave of Comedy

title: Midweek Night Owl Gig with the MRQ Band
description:
MRQ BAND, 10pm: Mike Regina and Joe Prassa met back in '71 at LA's Loyola University, and started playing music together almost immediately. Regina was a smart street kid from Brooklyn and Prassa was a cowboy from Arizona, born in Chicago. After gigging hard as a duo, they joined the LA band Pork Pie Hat, named after a tune by Charles Mingus.

Enter Pete Kmeto, 2010 (of Sacramento's former jazz/funk bands Missing Pieces and Downstroke). Kmeto, a bassist and accordion player, found himself impressed with Regina's original tunes while jamming with the boys at Fox & Goose. Kmeto introduced Steve Namle (former House Drummer at the famous Palomino in North Hollywood) in to the mix and next thing you know, this foursome had a legit band and a bunch of catchy, original tunes by Regina.

LA's Alina Eden, a recent transplant to Sacramento, came in to the picture to sing back up for Regina. Eden had previously found herself uninspired by the rigid technicality of studying classical voice at both California's Idyllwild Arts Academy and The Boston Conservatory, and was looking for a singing opportunity with more "soul". Regina and Eden started sharing the lead on the new tunes- And now, what BEGAN as the "Mike Regina Quintet", became simply, "MRQ."

Mostly originals and some cover favorites, if you like Tom Waits or Dan Hicks you'll love "MRQ!"

Blaze and Kelly (Idaho) open, 8:30pm.

title: Warped Pupu Party: Pepper & Iration
description:
The Warped Puppy Party features performances by Pepper and Iration.

Pepper is a rock band that plays music often classified as a combination of reggae, dub, and rock. The band consists of vocalist/guitarist Kaleo Wassman, vocalist/bassist Bret Bollinger, and drummer Yesod Williams. Since the band's formation, they have released five studio albums as well as one live album.

Kick off the Bicycle Film Festival and the Amgen Tour of California. The Crocker’s courtyards will come alive with bike art, a bicycle fix-it workshop, and a no-host BBQ. Bicycle valet service will be provided.

title: Truth or Dare: Burlesque Behind the Scenes
description:
Join the women of the Sizzling Sirens Burlesque Experience for Truth or Dare, an intimate behind the curtain party set to show the troupe’s fans just how much they are appreciated!

In addition to sensational teaser performances from the Capitol City’s original leading ladies of burlesque, Truth or Dare, is set to deliver never before seen, exclusive, stripped-down sets from celebrated local musicians Hans Eberbach from the Nibblers and Mondo Deco, sexy grindhouse tunes provided by DJ Agent 19, an interactive Siren Burlesque Boutique fashion show, vintage photo booth with Marie Young Photography, Siren style drinking games (that’s right…), and much more!

The Sizzling Sirens are a fresh, innovative dance theater company that has been reimagining Sacramento's alternative arts & culture landscape since June 2008. The Sirens infuse modern elements of song, dance, music, mask work, and allure into the classic burlesque structure, creating a truly unprecedented performance experience.

description: John Caparulo is an American stand-up comedian perhaps best known for his appearances on the late night E! talk show, Chelsea Lately.

title: Monsters on Tour: Combichrist
description:
Combichrist is an Aggrotech band formed in 2003 by Norwegian Andy LaPlegua (founder of the band Icon of Coil).

Also performing:
iVardenshpere
Star Killer
Blownload

title: The Epilogues
description: The Epilogues are a rock/experimental/indie band from Denver.

title: MidMo Movie Night: Chris & Don
description:
This month Midtown Monthly & Verge Center for the Arts present a screening Chris and Don, the love story between British writer, Christopher Isherwood (whose book The Berlin Stories inspired the musical and film Cabaret) and Don Bachardy, American portrait artist.

Refreshments for sale, popcorn free. Donations requested at the door for Verge.

title: The BluSoul Band
description:
Melding musical influences each member brings to the band, the distinctive BluSoul sound has made them a favorite at venues throughout the Sacramento and the Foothill area. Art Luna, owner of Luna's Café says of The BluSoul Band "...awesome...full of soul...and brings it at another level...professional and musically mature."

Performances are dynamic and high energy and keep people moving, dancing, and coming back for more. Spontaneity and excitement have always been The BluSoul Band hallmarks since the group's inception and their set list reflects the band's diverse collective of musical experiences, from contemporary pop, blues, and jazz to R&B and soul.

title: Texas Hold'Em Charity Poker Tournament
description:
Poker enthusiasts from the greater Sacramento area will compete for the coveted “Championship Belt” at DDSO’s 6th annual Texas Hold’Em Charity Poker Tournament. Play for a chance to host a great event for your friends: fly-fishing trips, a weekend in Tahoe, yacht rides, box seats at Raley Field, and more. Professional dealers ensure that this game is a top-notch experience for everyone. Come early to enjoy a great meal and drinks with friends.

All proceeds benefit DDSO programs. DDSO is an organization committed to enhancing quality of life for persons with developmental disabilities.

title: Sexy Soul Xplosion: Jon B & Vivian Green
description: Sacramento...don't miss the Sexy Soul Xplosion featuring Jon B & Vivian Green, performing live with full band.

title: A Skylit Drive
description:
A Skylit Drive is a six-piece post-hardcore band from Lodi, California. The band has released a DVD, one EP album, and three studio length albums: Wires...and the Concept of Breathing in 2008, Adelphia on in 2009, and most recently Identity On Fire in February 2011.

Also performing:
Trances
Above The City
A Holy Ghost Revival
Trial By Fire
Pledge The Silence
Look Alive

title: Graduation Weekend with DJ Billy Lane & DJ Peeti-V
description: It's finally here! School is coming to an end and summer is heating up! Join for a fabulous, unforgettable, buck wild graduation weekend! DJ Billy Lane & DJ Peeti-V provide the beats. Don't wait in line on your special day, call Sam at the number below for a VIP bottle service section.

title: Gabriel Iglesias
description:
As of April 19, the following performances are sold out: Fri 7:30pm; Sat 7:30pm & 10:30pm.

Gabriel "Picachu" Iglesias' style of comedy is a mixture of story telling with characters and sound effects that bring all his personal issues to life. His amazing ability to cross over with a clean animated style of comedy has put him in big demand throughout the stand-up comedy circuit. Ask anyone who has seen him in concert and you will probably hear the same thing: "He was so funny!"

title: My Sister's House 10th Anniversary Gala: One Night Only
description:
In the style of Broadway, an array of stars will gather in Sacramento for One Night Only. Oh what a night, when performing on stage will be the tunes of: the Tokens, Beyoncé, Frank Sinatra, Elvis, Peter Paul & Mary, Little Eva, Sam Cook, Three Dog Night, and many more. Trust us: you'll be entertained all night long!

Please join for a pre-show reception at the Social Club (5:30pm) followed by the show at the Crest Theatre (7pm) in Downtown Sacramento as we honor these Knightly Heroes in our community who have made a real difference for women in crisis: Congresswoman Doris Matsui and The California Endowment

Proceeds will benefit My Sister's, the only organization in the Central Valley that provides shelter and supportive programs to Asian Pacific Islander women and their children who are victims of domestic violence. The profits from this event will help provide 5001 nights of safety for one year. For 10 years, My Sister's House has provided over 12,000 nights of shelter at its 6-bed safe haven. In addition to culturally sensitive shelter and job skills training, they also provide a 24/7 multi-lingual help line, a legal advice clinic, and innumerable referrals to health and mental health services.

title: Sean Na'auao
description:
Sean Na`auao is a talented singer, musician, composer, and producer who continues to work "outside the envelope" in the multi-faceted musical world. As a singer and musician, he has firmly established a successful island music solo career in Hawai`i.

Also performing:
Ka Nalu

title: Chicano Comedy Allstars
description: Enjoy your laughs with the Chicano Comedy Allstars.

title: Fitz and the Tantrums
description:
Fitz & the Tantrums are a soul group from Los Angeles. They were founded by Michael Fitzpatrick, who had begun writing soul music for a solo project on an old church organ he had purchased. He added friend James King to the group as an arranger and soon after expanded the band to a seven-piece, including several horns. Fitzpatrick shares the vocal duties with Noelle Scaggs. Other members include Joseph Karnes, Jeremy Ruzumna, and John Wicks.

Also performing:
Ximena Sarinana
The New Humans

title: Elizabeth Cook
description:
Country singer/songwriter Elizabeth Cook made her Grand Ole Opry debut on March 17, 2000, appearing repeatedly thereafter—a remarkable achievement considering that, at the time, she was an indie artist with no radio airplay. But such was the excitement generated by her clear, beautiful voice, strong songwriting ability, and live performances, all of which have drawn comparisons to Dolly Parton.

Also performing:
Attwater

title: SacShows Presents: Soundcheck 7
description: Soundcheck, presented by Sac Shows Presents & Ace of Spades, is a showcase of local bands. This month includes performances by Stepchild, Prylosis, Princess Die, For All I've Done, Tear Down The Sky, and Represa.

title: B Side Players and Sol Peligro
description: The B-Side Players are a 10 piece power house of bilingual reggae, funk, and cumbia. With fierce political lyrics and an overwhelming positive vibration of love, culture, and unity, their live shows have raised them to legendary status. The Players have been igniting and uplifting dance floors for 15 years and have been blessed to share the stage with, The Wailers, Toots and the Maytals, Ben Harper, War, James Brown, and many more.

title: Searching for Eden
description:
Searching for Eden by James Still, partially adapted from short stories by Mark Twain comprise act one combined with an original and contemporary twist in act two which imaginatively recreates the world’s first love story of Adam and Eve. In Searching for Eden, the play opens at the dawn of time in the Garden of Eden where the battle of the sexes begins, language is deliciously invented, and loneliness and heartbreak are poignantly discovered. The play juxtaposes their new love with a leap forward to present day and a middle aged Adam and Eve returning to Eden, now an upscale resort called “E,” for their anniversary in an attempt to recapture the primal passions of their youth. This witty and original play is a must see modern look at marriage exampled by the “first couple.”

Searching for Eden is the seventh and final play of B Street’s 2010-2011 Mainstage Season. Starring Jason Kuykendall and Lyndsy Kail. Buck Busfield directs.

Sacramento businesses support B Street Theatre. Bring your ticket stub to any restaurant partner for special discounts!

title: Gene Pompa with Special Guest Cristela Alonzo
description:
Gene Pompa, comedian and writer, was born in East Los Angeles, California. He has been a Mexican-American most of his life, except for a few years during the 1970s, when he was a practicing Chicano. Gene became a product of his multi-ethnic upbringing in the suburbs of Los Angeles and it was this diverse background which ultimately inspired Gene to incorporate universal themes into his stand-up comedy and writing.

Gene's television credits include several appearances on NBC's Late Night with Conan O'Brien and CBS's Late Late Show with Craig Kilborn. Pompa has also starred in his own half hour Comedy Central special as well as a 30 minute comedy showcase on SiTV. His acting has been featured on FOX's In Living Color, CBS's Style & Substance, and The Brothers Garcia on Nickelodean. You may have also seen Gene on Showtime, HBO, MTV, MUN2, Galavision, or the Game Show Network, as well as the feature film Just Go With It.

title: Sacramento Comedy Showcase
description: Get your laughs at the Sacramento Comedy Showcase.

title: Groove Thang Band
description: Groove Thang performs a variety of high energy dance music from the '70s to present. The Groove Thang band is definitely THE best "get off your seat and dance" variety entertainment party cover band in Northern California. The Groove Thang Band plays a diverse mix of non-stop dance cover music including R&B, Funk, Motown, Disco, Smooth Jazz, Rock ,and yes, even some Country from the '70s, '80s, and '90s. Something for everyone!

title: Blaqk Audio
description:
Blaqk Audio is an electronic music band formed by current AFI members Davey Havok and Jade Puget.

Also performing:
Boggan
Hamm FM

title: Tom Drinnon & Dueces Wild
description: Tom Drinnon was born in a small northern town in California called Lakeport and raised in Manteca, CA. Like his mother and father before him he took great interest in music at an early age and has pursued the dream of becoming a professional recording artist. At the young age of 23, Tom moved to Nashville, TN where he met his manager only two weeks after arriving. Tom signed with a major management company that also managed Kenney Chesney, Confederate Railroad, Lorie Morgan, Alabama, and Johnny Paycheck. From there he went out on the road performing across the nation. Best known for his authentic country sound and versatile range, Tom Drinnon is sure to impress any crowd.

title: 2nd Saturday Rock n' Roll Style
description: 2nd Saturday Rock n' Roll Style includes performances by Arden Park Roots, Lonely Kings, Early States, Not Your Style, Dogfood, and Element of Soul.

title: Jack's Mannequin
description:
Jack's Mannequin is an alternative-rock band formed in 2004, originally hailing from Orange County, California. The band began as a side project of Andrew McMahon, the frontman for Something Corporate, and is composed of guitarist Bobby Anderson, bassist Mikey "The Kid" Wagner, and drummer Jay McMillan.

Also performing:
Steel Train
Lady Danville

title: The Airborne Toxic Event
description:
The Airborne Toxic Event is an indie rock band from Los Feliz, Los Angeles, California. It consists of Mikel Jollett (vocals, guitar, keyboards), Steven Chen (guitar, keyboards), Noah Harmon (electric bass, upright bass, backing vocals), Daren Taylor (drums), and Anna Bulbrook (viola, keyboards, tambourine, backing vocals). The band released its debut self-titled album in 2008 and released its follow-up album, All at Once, in April 2011.

Named after a section of the book White Noise, by Don DeLillo, the group is known for its blend of rock music and orchestral arrangements, having performed frequently with the Calder Quartet, a string quartet based in Los Angeles. The group has also played concerts with the Louisville Orchestra and the Colorado Symphony Orchestra.

title: Mickey Avalon
description:
Remember the boy next door that played records all day, and at night kept you up with songs of his own? He left home one day and was never heard from again. He moved to the big city, living in cheap motels, eating dollar hamburgers, working the boulevard with ex-models, thorazine freaks, transvestites, mothers, fathers, drunks, junkies, and punk rockers alike.

He struggled during many long lonely desperate nights under the dizzying city lights but made a vow that he would never forget the magic in this world the things he loved the most: his first fix, his first girl, and most importantly the first time he rocked a mic. Mickey Avalon has done whatever it took to get him to and off Hollywood Blvd. to invite you into his world.

Mickey Avalon is an American rapper from Hollywood, California. His debut self-titled solo album was released in 2006 on Interscope/Shoot to Kill Records in association with MySpace Records. Frequent topics of Avalon's songs are his experiences with substance abuse and prostitution.

title: Mojo Child: A Tribute to The Doors
description:
Mojo Child is a Tribute to Jim Morrison & The Doors. They recreate the music, magic, and madness of a live Doors show. Come and experience note-for-note stylings of all The Doors hits. Truly a Jim Morrison celebration!

"Is everybody in? The Ceremony is about to begin." -J. Morrison

title: Face to Face
description:
Face to Face is a pop punk band from Victorville, California formed in 1991 by frontman Trever Keith. Originally known as "Zero Tolerance," Keith has been the only constant member of the band during their years of touring and recording albums.

Also performing:
Strung Out
Blitzkid
The Darlings

title: Tech N9ne
description:
Aaron Dontez Yates, better known by his stage name Tech N9ne, is a rapper from Kansas City, Missouri. In 1999, Yates and Travis O'Guin founded the record label Strange Music. Throughout his career, Tech N9ne has sold over one million albums and has had his music featured in film, television, and video games. In 2009, he won the Left Field Woodie award at the mtvU Woodie Awards.

His stage name originated from the TEC-9 semi-automatic handgun, given to him by rapper Black Walt due to his fast rhyming style. Yates later applied a deeper meaning to the name, claiming that it stands for the complete technique of rhyme, with "tech" meaning technique and "nine" representing the number of completion.

Also performing:
Krizz Kaliko
Kutt Calhoun
Big Scoob
Jay Rock
!Mayday!
Steve Stone
Quette Daddie

title: Ladies Night Out II with Kevin Sandbloom, E. Clark, and others
description:
Ladies Night Out II is a night of poetry, fashions, and music. Featuring: Demesha Kennedy (Signs of Praise), comedian E. Clark, singer Bajan, neo-soul singer Kevin Sandbloom from Los Angeles, dancer Sonic Boom, singer Yvette Gauf, singer Tony R., poet Terry Moore, Khiry Malik Moore, The Poet i, and poet group E-Legal Tag Team.

The last event sold-out so don't wait to get your tickets. Free massages during the event! Men are welcome to attend and support the event.

title: Cold Shot
description: Cold Shot gets into the groove and gets the party started. The band is all about vibe and spirit, a lively show masterfully done. Cold Shot's mix of retro and contemporary chart hits is irresistible to those who love partying to recognizable music. And, Cold Shot's goal is simple: to not only get your party started at clubs, festivals, corporate, and private events, but take it to the next level with irresistible, high-energy dance music!

title: Led Zepagain
description:
Led Zepagain is Southern California's Led Zeppelin Tribute Band. Catch them in Sacramento!

Also performing:
Big Boss Graffiti
Rue The Night

title: Mother Mayhem
description: Mother Mayhem has quickly become the premiere dance party band in Northern California. Key to their meteoric rise in the NorCal music scene is their unbelievable song selection along with their outrageous stage show. From rock anthems such as "You Give Love a Bad Name," to the most current dance, hip-hop, and rock hits on the radio by B.o.B., Lady Gaga, Eminem, and more, Mother Mayhem's explosive renditions of the greatest music of all time sets attendance records at clubs and is guaranteed to keep the dance floor packed.

title: Moonlight Escape Dinner
description: Share the magic of the Napa Valley in July as the sun sets at 8:32pm. This moon is named the "Full Thunder Moon" because thunderstorms occur most frequently at this time of year. Our Moonlight Escape gourmet dinner takes place upstairs in the Vista Dome rail car with its almost 180-degree view. Guests glide over the evening vineyards touched with the silver light of the rising moon. This is a five-course dinner, including a glass of sparkling wine. There is seating for only 24 couples.

title: Launch Design & Music Festival
description:
Launch is a multi-disciplinary audio/visual festival that connects people with art, music, fashion, and design. Launch recognizes and seeks to highlight the cultural overlaps between creative industry and aims to create a cross-discipline experience that allows people to connect with the artists, their work, and the performances.

Don't miss this event showcasing art, music, fashion, and design from Sacramento amd beyond. Enjoy live musical performances and DJ sets throughout the night, a fashion show, and galleries featuring artists and furniture designers. Launch Events is planned by a collaborative of Sacramento designers, musicians, artists, photographers, stylists, and other creative minds. Come see momentum in Sacramento!

Music: 
-Neon Indian is Alan Palomo, the Mexican-born, Texas-raised, 21-year-old synth-wizard who learned his production chops as part of Ghosthustler and honed them as VEGA. Neon Indian’s album Psychic Chasms was designated as the 14th best album of 2009 by Pitchfork and one of the hottest new bands of 2010 by Rolling Stone.

-Civil Twilight The three lifelong friends Steven and Andrew McKellar and Richard Wouters have been playing music together since they were teenagers, emulating the rock music they heard coming out of Europe and America, from Oasis, U2, and Nirvana to The Verve, The Police, Muse, and Radiohead. From Cape Town, South Africa to Nashville, Tennessee, Civil Twilight’s trip has already taken them a long way…and it’s only the beginning.

Art by: Aaron Kraten, Brady Tuazon, Carmen Winant, Chelsea Greene Lewyta, Jeff Dojillo, Jeff Felker, Joel Lee, John Horton, Keith Telfeyan, Kristina Collantes, Micah Crandall-Bear, Nicholas Wilson, Raoul Ortega.

Complete line-up TBA.

A shuttle will run between Midtown and The Greens Hotel throughout the night.

title: Moonlight Escape Dinner
description: Share the magic of the Napa Valley in June as the sun sets at 8:07pm. This moon is named the "Full Red Moon" because as the moon rises it can appear reddish through a hot, sultry haze. Our Moonlight Escape gourmet dinner takes place upstairs in the Vista Dome rail car with its almost 180-degree view. Guests glide over the evening vineyards touched with the silver light of the rising moon. This is a five-course dinner, including a glass of sparkling wine, and two glasses of our private label. There is seating for only 24 couples.

title: Off to the Races
description: Gear up for Race for the Arts with this fundraising food and wine tasting event. This premier event will return to the beautiful garden setting of Pavilions. Guests will be treated to live entertainment, wines from around the region, and an assortment of scrumptious hors d'oeuvres prepared by some of the area's top restaurants. Unwind and capture the essence of the Arts.

title: FLCCA presents The Water Coolers
description:
Partners of Three Stages, Folsom Lake Community Concert Association presents The Water Coolers

Do you ever feel like you've got all your eggs in one basket, six balls in the air, and 7,000 emails to return? Well, gather 'round The Water Coolers for a high energy, laugh-out-loud evening of award-winning song and sketch comedy. For anyone who's ever been held captive by a help line ("And hold please"), stalked by a sales parent ("Who will buy this crap for my kid's school?"), or found themselves judged by how many words a minute they can type with their thumbs ("Blackberry"), The Water Coolers take a hilarious look at what we go through just making every week happen. Simply put: it's your life, but killer funny.

A unique combination of NY comedy writers, directors, and business people from around the country work together to create a funny, smart, authentic take on work and life. Based in New York City, The Water Coolers has become a working home for some of the finest and most exciting comics and singers in professional show business.

This performance is part of the FLCCA 2011-2012 Season.

title: 2nd Saturday: Midtown Art Walk
description:
On the second Saturday of each month, many local Sacramento galleries feature new shows of individual and collective artists. Many galleries play host to the artists so it's a wonderful way to meet them in person. Some galleries provide beverages, hors d oeuvres, live music, and even dinner with the artist!

Since many galleries are grouped into two main areas in Sacramento, Midtown and along Del Paso Blvd (The Uptown Arts District), many people like to take an Art Walk and wander from gallery to gallery, making and evening of art and people viewing. More galleries and venues can be found in Old Sacramento and Downtown Sacramento, as well as in outlying areas including Folsom & Fair Oaks.

title: Saddle Up & Ride It Out- A Solidarity Dance Party
Trivia Night Wednesdays
description: Are you smarter than other people? Let's see how smart you are without Google Search! Every Wednesday come out toTrivia Night at the Blue Cue. Top 3 teams win prizes. Enjoy some amazing eats and drinks while you destroy the competition.

title: Homeschool Day
description:
Homeschool and individual family groups are invited to visit the Museum for thematic, gallery adventures designed to intrigue children ages six and older.

Reservations are required.

title: Art Appetizer
description:
On 2nd Saturday, start your evening at the Crocker with a tour of the Museum’s most recent exhibitions. Never the same tour twice, Art Appetizer is a 50-minute experience designed to fulfill your art cravings.

Free with Museum admission.

title: The Pixar Collection
description: The California State Railroad Museum will host a special event with Stage Nine Gallery, presenting Disney’s Fine Art – The Pixar Collection, a fine art collection inspired by the films of Pixar Animation Studios. Twelve artists portray the stories of Pixar’s eleven modern animation classics through fine art. View the art collection and meet the artists in person.

title: Canine Warriors: The History of America's Military Working Dogs
description: Learn more about the history of America's military working dog.

title: Whale of a Weekend!
description:
The Discovery Museum Science & Space Center celebrates their 60th Anniversary with a year-long retrospective of science milestones of the last six decades. In May, they celebrate great science of the 1970s.

One momentous scientific occasion was the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972. Kids celebrate by making a paper whale pillow and viewing real whale bones. Other ocean specimens are on display for this weekend only.

Planetarium shows at 1pm and 3pm are included with admission (ages 4 and above only); live animal shows at Noon and 2pm are for all ages.

title: Drop, Yak, Splat: A Museum Adventure for Families
description:
Different artworks will provide inspiration for a stimulating gallery experience for families and children of all ages.

Free with Museum admission.

title: Baby Loves Art: Over the Rainbow
description:
Baby Loves Art is an entertaining and interactive way for children ages three and under and their caregivers to experience the educational stimulation that the visual arts can provide.

Free with Museum admission. Advance registration required. This program is funded by the First 5 Sacramento Commission.

title: Lunch & Learn
description: Join us for an in-depth 30-minute talk about one or two works of art on view. This discussion will focus on Jamini Roy's "Baby Krishna." Participants are encouraged to enjoy lunch at the Crocker Cafe before or after the talk. Free with Museum admission.

title: Playlist: Tom Rigney & Flambeau
description:
Playlist moves outside to the E. Kendell Davis Courtyard for the summer. Tom Rigney and Flambeau offer up fiery Cajun and zydeco two-steps, low-down blues, and funky New Orleans grooves.

Playlist is part of the program series Thursdays ‘til 9. Sponsored by Bank of America.

title: Model T Basics Workshop
description: Have you ever wondered why the Ford Motor Company manufactured over fifteen million Model Ts from 1908 until 1927 and why it had such an impact on our nation’s society and economy? Enroll in this workshop at the California Automobile Museum to find out why. Current driver’s license required. Discover the wonder of Model T construction, nomenclature, operation, and basic maintenance. Also, each adult student will have the opportunity to learn how to drive a Model T--an experience that won’t be forgotten!

title: May the Force Be With You
description:
The Discovery Museum Science & Space Center celebrates their 60th Anniversary with a year-long retrospective of science milestones of the last six decades. In May, they celebrate great science of the 1970s.

Celebrate one of the most classic science fiction movies of all time--Star Wars! Take kids back to the '70s by viewing fan memorabilia. Children craft a Star Wars-themed project while viewing the original movie in the classroom. This weekend only, any person wearing a Star Wars costume receives $1 off admission.

Planetarium shows at 1pm and 3pm are included with admission (ages 4 and above only); live animal shows at Noon and 2pm are for all ages.

title: Classical Concert: Sacramento Saturday Club Presents
description: Works by American Impressionist composer Charles Griffes will be performed by flautist Maquette Kuper, vocalists Rona Commins, James Gentry, and Rufina Jones, and pianist John Cozza. The Zephyr Wind Quintet will also perform.

title: CAM Photo Workshop: Lighting 101
description:
Together, California Auto Museum and MaverickPhotography.us bring you CAM Photo. With nearly 20 incredible talented photographers MaverickPhotography.us is the official designated photography team that makes up the museums photo department.

Couple a wonderful education center and auditorium for classrooms, a floor of vintage and exquisite automobiles, and a team qualified and eager to mentor and teach photographers, you have a great recipe for informative, educational, and fun photography workshops.

Taking you from basic to advanced throughout the year, anyone with a desire to learn photography will find themselves growing and developing their photography skills right away.

The team of Maverick Photographers are easy going and look forward to taking their time, at your pace to help you learn this ever expanding and changing art.

Join us the 4th Tuesday of each month and watch yourself grow into an accomplished photographer.

title: Wee Wednesday
description:
Bring your little one and yourself to this gallery-based play date for children ages 3 to 5. Encourage your early learner’s development through multi-sensory activities inspired by art and storytelling.

Free with Museum admission. This is a family program and space is limited. Signup begins at 10am on the day of the event at the Museum Admission Desk. This program is funded by the First 5 Sacramento Commission.

title: Big Names, Small Art
description: Music, artist demonstrations, a good time, and a great cause. Join us for a silent auction party featuring the work of “Big Name” regional artists. Each “Small Art” work measures in at 12 inches or less. Bidding starts at the small price of $25.

title: Art Q&A
description:
Discover the essence of the art on view in tours that emphasize looking, conversation, and group interaction.

Free with Museum admission.

title: Endangered Species Weekend
description:
The Discovery Museum Science & Space Center celebrates their 60th Anniversary with a year-long retrospective of science milestones of the last six decades. In May, they celebrate great science of the 1970s.

Once an animal or plant is extinct, it is gone forever. The implementation of the Endangered Species Act in 1973 was voted almost unanimously by Congress to prevent this from happening. Bring youngsters to the Museum this weekend to share how important this Act is and what types of animals it protects. A variety of specimens are available, highlighting endangered species. There is a focus on turtles and tortoises, including live threatened species to meet and learn about. A turtle craft is available for children 12 and under.

Planetarium shows at 1pm and 3pm are included with admission (ages 4 and above only); live animal shows at Noon and 2pm are for all ages.

title: Holiday Monday: Memorial Day
description:
The Crocker continues its Holiday Monday series with a day of special programs. From the multi-media presentation “Jazz in Animation” to an open art workshop inspired by the American flag, as seen in artworks by Childe Hassam, Faith Ringgold, and Jasper Johns, there is something for all ages and interests.

Thanks to the generous support of Target, Museum admission is free.

title: Jazz in Animation
description:
Using clips from classics like “Betty Boop” to contemporary features like “The Princess and the Frog,” animation expert Jerry Beck and jazz authority Joe Gilman will take a melodic journey through cinematic history. Presented in conjunction with the annual Jazz Festival and Jubilee.

Thanks to the generous support of Target, Museum admission is free.

title: Essayons: 100 Years of the California Cadet Corps
description: Essayons (Let Us Try!) is the motto of the California Cadet Corps. Formed on April 5, 1911 by the California National Guard this organization, originally known as the California High School Cadets, predates the Junior ROTC program by five years.

title: Muscle Car Tune Up Workshop
description: This class teaches tune up for ‘60s and ‘70s era muscle cars at the California Automobile Museum. Reviews include the cranking systems, engine condition, ignition and advance, base timing, fuel system performance tests, and service tips. Also included, information on parts resources and methods for increasing power on your muscle car. Adult students are encouraged to bring their muscle car to class so they can perform the tune-up tests and adjustments directly on their vehicle.

title: Father's Day Special
description: In honor of Father’s Day, dads who come into the California Automobile Museum with their families will be admitted for the day free of charge. Come in and enjoy the day viewing the American Muscle Car Exhibit and the Automobilia! Exhibit with your dad.

title: Beyond the Locomotive: Award Winning Photographs
description:
As part of a special display, the California State Railroad Museum is proud to showcase award-winning photographs recently given prestigious honors as part of an annual Creative Photography Awards Program competition organized by the Center for Railroad Photography & Art. With a compelling "Beyond the Locomotive” theme, a record-setting 700 photographs were submitted as entries this year by more than 200 photographers around the world.

A first time entrant, Brandon Robert Smith of Norman, Oklahoma, received the Center's 2010 top prize for Creative Photography. A California-based photographer named Steve Crise was also honored in the annual competition, which has international appeal.
Judged by Kimberly Parker, Director of the O. Winston Link Museum in Roanoke, Virginia, the competition this year was extremely competitive due to the sheer number of entries.

This special photography exhibit will remain on display at the California State Railroad Museum through June 2011, joining the Museum’s regular lineup of permanent and changing exhibitions, along with special events. In addition to being showcased in the special exhibit at the Railroad Museum, the award-winning photographs will be featured in an upcoming issue of Railfan & Railroad magazine.

More information about the competition and the Center for Railroad Photography & Art can be found at online.

title: Meaning and Medium
description:
This exhibition explores the diversity of media in art, including photography, painting, sculpture, and mixed media. Pieces on display include work from various Sacramento-area high schools.

This exhibit is part of the Student & Community Exhibition Galleries.

Meet the artists who have explored portraiture through fresh eyes at the Opening Reception: Sun, May 15, 1pm-3pm.

title: Third Annual CAM Car Cruise
description: Get ready for Sacramento to come alive with the sights and sounds of hundreds of unique cars from all eras and manufacturers as they celebrate an American summertime tradition of cruising with community-wide particpation. The 3rd Annaul CAM Car Cruise, hosted by the California Automobile Museum (CAM), will be a fun-filled day for the whole family as it cruises through the streets of Sacramento, along Fulton avenue where the event concludes with a huge car show at Fulton & Marconi. Attendees are encouraged to enjoy the local fares of fulton vendors.

title: Above Ground Walking Tours
description:
In addition to the popular Old Sacramento Underground tour program already underway for the season, the Historic Old Sacramento Foundation is adding to the fun with intriguing "above ground" walking tours as well. On weekends beginning in May and continuing through August, two informative walking tours will be offered that include the following: Sacramento City: California's Gold Rush Legacy Tour and From Canvas to Brick: Old Sacramento Architectural Tour.

For the Gold Rush Legacy Tours, docents in historically appropriate attire take guests on a journey back to the 1850s using original and reconstructed Gold Rush-era buildings as a compelling backdrop to describe what the town was like during that fascinating period in California's history.

For the Old Sacramento Architectural Tours, guests are guided through Old Sacramento to see how the architecture of the buildings silently but assuredly reflects the compelling history of how Sacramento was transformed from a water-logged tent city--with floods, fires and the Gold Rush along the way--to a firmly established city and the state's capital.

All Old Sacramento walking tours last approximately one hour in length and guests are encouraged to wear comfortable shoes and be prepared to walk on uneven surfaces. Walking tours begin and end at the Sacramento History Museum.

The above ground and underground tour programs are coordinated by the Historic Old Sacramento Foundation (HOSF) and in partnership with the City of Sacramento, California State Parks, Old Sacramento Business Association, and participating merchants and businesses.

title: The Politician and the Pop Princess
description: The California Automobile Museum presents The Politician and the Pop Princess featuring the famous powder blue 1974 Plymouth Satellite (owned by California Governor Edmund G. “Jerry” Brown during his first two terms in office, 1975-1983) and a 1982 Porsche 911SC Targa which was originally owned by Brown's one-time girlfriend, rock legend Linda Ronstadt. These vehicles, and additional artifacts, pay affectionate tribute to Governor Brown and Ms. Ronstadt and will take Museum visitors back to the 1970s. The cars and artifacts tell a uniquely "California" story of romance, the media, and the intersection of politics and fame.

title: Sirens of Chrome
description: The California Automobile Museum presents Sirens of Chrome which is an artful expression of elegance by intertwining the natural beauty of human figures and automobile masterpieces within the photography world. The collection of visual goddesses which are portrayed as human hood ornaments started in the early 1900s and is now a traveling exhibit. Get lost within the wondrous world of the gorgeous models of both women and vehicles during this featured exhibit in the rotating gallery.

title: California Automobile Museum’s Annual Fundraising Dinner featuring Dennis Gage
description: Spend an evening with special guest Dennis Gage of My Classic Car and emcee Nick Toma, (Good Day Sacramento) raising funds for the California Automobile Museum. The event will feature a live and silent auction, catered dinner, cash bar, and entertainment.

title: Hands on History: Candle Light Tours
description: Darkness lends mystery to the Fort, a romantic aura that disguises the harsh reality of pioneer life. Candlelit tours offer glimpses into the private lives of those who uprooted their families for a better life in early California. A behind the scenes look at the real faces of those who saw opportunity or possible devastation in their new homes, husbands debating with wives, mothers reassuring their children, tradesmen negotiating business, all surrounded by the night which allows us to truly travel back in time.

title: Dementia Support Group Meeting
description:
Spouses, family members, and friends who are caring for seniors who have memory loss are encouraged to participate in a dementia support group. Elizabeth Rawson, MSW and a family consultant with Del Oro Caregiver Resource Center in Sacramento, will facilitate the meeting.

In the group, family caregivers are encouraged to share their experiences and challenges so they can learn from one another. Professional resources and caregiving guidance is also offered. The support group is on-going and meets the 2nd Tuesday of each month.

The Chateau at Carmichael Park is managed by Hank Fisher Properties and offers remarkably affordable, high-quality independent and assisted living along with The Garden Memory Care and The Club Memory Day Care.

There is no charge for the group, but space is limited and reservations are required. Those attending may bring their loved ones to The Club Memory Day Care at no charge while the meeting is in progress. For reservations, directions or information about the Chateau at Carmichael Park, call the numbers below.

title: Sacramento Kings: #HereWeRally
description:
The Kings are still Sacramento's team and we aim to keep it that way! Before the hard work starts we celebrate how far we've come. You owe it to yourself to attend.

This Tuesday is the #HereWeBuild rally you've been waiting so patiently for: #HereWeRally. Expect to see Kings' legends Scot Pollard and Doug Christie, Coach Paul Westphal, and other special guests. Stay for the fireworks and a live performance by Sacramento's own, TESLA! If you're a Kings fan then this is the place to be. You will not want to miss this, so mark your calendar or start camping out now if you need, but make sure you are there.

Bring your Kings gear, cameras, cowbells, signs, and get yourself downtown. This is sure to be a special moment in Sacramento history. Tell your family and friends that May 10 is the day we celebrate our city and our team. Be there, and #BeHeard.

Celebrate our victory and get galvanized for the fight ahead!

title: Advance Directives Seminar
description:
Local seniors and their family members are encouraged to join the residents of River’s Edge retirement community for a much-needed conversation about ensuring that individual wishes about medical treatment are met, even in medical emergencies. Heather Chubb, a life transitions attorney, will lead the seminar.

Ms. Chubb will discuss advance directives and other legal documents needed to express one’s wishes about medical treatment. She will also explain what POLST is and how it fits in the health care picture, the importance of HIPPA, and making it easy for family to access healthcare information.

River’s Edge is a Hank Fisher Properties senior living community that offers elegant independent living.

The seminar is free but space is limited. To reserve your place, contact the community at the number below.

title: Blues in the Schools Benefit
description:
You don't want to miss this opportunity to support and listen to some young blues players in the Sacramento area. Students from the Blues in the Schools after school programs will be performing along with their teachers (local favorite blues musicians: Jimmy Pailer, Lew Fratis, Joe Lev, and Rick Taylor).

Headlining the program is the award winning, showstopping Laurie Morvan Band. Laurie and her band bring sizzling hot modern American blues to The Station. Along with searing guitar playing Laurie is an excellent songwriter. Her orginal tunes are personal, funny, and profound. Bring the whole family for a fun, exciting night with dinner and a rocking hot blues show.

title: Senator Steinberg's 10th Annual Passport to Summer Youth Fair
description: The Passport to Summer Youth Fair is a wonderful event for parents, young adults, and children, as it highlights a wide-range of opportunities for healthy summer and after school activities. Programs offered by the local parks and recreation departments, as well as opportunities provided by a number of other community organizations, including the Boys and Girls Clubs, Sacramento Youth Symphony, Crocker Art Museum, Sacramento State Campus, and YMCA will be featured. More than 400 organizations have been invited to participate. Learn about the many great summer enrichment programs for children and youth. There will be free medical screenings for children and youth. Enjoy live entertainment, children activities, snacks, and a raffle.

title: Bicycle Film Festival (BFF)
description:
The Bicycle Film Festival (BFF), a celebration of bicycles through film, art, and music, returns to Sacramento for a second year in its 11-year history, in honor of May is Bike Month. Originating in New York City, the festival added California’s Capital City last year to its roster of 40 global cities, including Amsterdam, London, Milano, and Tokyo. For 2011, BFF Sacramento is expanded to include an additional night of films and activities. The BFF brings together many creative communities, including fashion, music, and art as well as various bicycling communities--including fixed gear, BMX, and road cycling--over a shared passion for bike riding.

Thursday, May 12 at Crocker Art Museum
