title: Why We Sing: Singing About Peace, Love, and Women's Lives
description:
Why We Sing: Singing About Peace, Love, and Women's Lives is a benefit for WEAVE presented by the Sacramento Women’s Chorus, a musical group of women who love music, care about each other, and support the greater Sacramento community.

Special Guest artist Eva Cranstoun--vocal performer, Waldorf educator, and therapist--has acquired had a wide perspective and deep soul understanding of the human voice.

The Sacramento Women's Chorus is a non-profit group of diverse women who are building friendships and community through their love of music, dedication to musical excellence, and commitment to performing music which reflects the lives women. They perform on behalf of all women, the environment, peace, social justice, tolerance, LGBT equality, and the celebration of diversity.

The event takes place in Stegmann Hall on the Rudolph Steiner College campus.

title: Guided Nature Walk: Things That Slither
description: What has no arms or legs and smells with its tongue? Learn about the life cycles, predators and prey, habitats, locomotion, and defenses of reptiles and amphibians. Then “slither” up to meet our resident animals up close.

title: 2011 Sacramento Arthritis Walk
description: It is time to celebrate the wonders of Spring. Bring your family, friends, and canine companions and walk for a cure at the 2011 Greater Sacramento Valley Arthritis Walk. May is National Arthritis Awareness Month and the 2011 Walk is not only a means to spread the word of the benefits of physical activity to ease the pain of arthritis; but as a way to come together to help raise money to find a cure. Following the Walk, the Health and Fitness Expo will feature refreshments, a Kids’ Zone, and a special Pets Zone for our four-legged walkers.

title: Cirque Du Soleil: Quidam
description: A young girl fumes; she has already seen everything there is to see, and her world has lost all meaning. Her anger shatters her little world, and she finds herself in the universe of Quidam. She is joined by a joyful companion as well as another character, more mysterious, who will attempt to seduce her with the marvelous, the unsettling, and the terrifying.

title: Kidical Mass
description:
Spring has sprung and it's time to gear up for another family bicycle extravaganza. Kidical Mass is a legal, safe and FUN bike ride for kids, kids at heart, and their families. All types of bikes, trailers, trail-a-bikes, longtails, Long Johns, tandems, folders, trikes, and whatever rolls are welcome.

Ride with your kids. Parents are required to accompany their children. The ride will go slowly enough that kids of all ages can keep up. A few “sweepers” will be trailing the group to help anyone needing assistance and to make sure no one is left. Riders are required to wear helmets.

The 2nd Kidical Mass takes place for May is Bike Month. The ride begins from 51st Street, between M & L Streets, near East Portal Park.

title: Remembering the Nakba: Celebrating Palestine
description:
An event of Reflection on the Past - Hope for the Future that features displays, speakers, music, food, children’s activities. From 1947-49, over 750,000 Palestinians were driven from their homes by colonial militias and then the Israeli army. The new state of Israel destroyed or occupied 531 Palestinian villages and took over 78% of historic Palestine.

On May 15, Palestinians commemorate these events as Al-Nakba, which means “The Catastrophe” in Arabic. Palestinians, who had lived in historic Palestine for generations, continue to celebrate their culture while they struggle for freedom, justice, equality, and the right to return to their homes and lands.

title: 2011 Amgen Tour of California: Stage 2 Finish & Festival
description:
Sacramento is hosting the Amgen Tour for the fifth year in a row--world-class professional cycling on the streets of Sacramento for Stage 2 of the race (Miles: 133.2; KM: 214.4). One of the longest stages of the race, Stage 2 has “sprinter” written all over the race route. Starting at the site of the 1960 Winter Olympics and one of the largest ski resorts in the U.S., Squaw Valley, the riders will head north to the town of Truckee and then west past the infamous and rugged Donner’s Pass. At 7,100’, this will be the only KOM of Stage 2.

From here it will be a more than 7’000’ of descending to the State’s Capitol (elev. 25’). The route will pass through Nevada City, California (last year’s official Start City) and after working its way west for several miles, the peloton will turn south and head through one of the country’s premier military installations, Beale Air Force Base. From there it will be a fast ride through the suburbs of Sacramento. Entering the circuit just past the finish line in Sacramento, the riders will begin the first of two circuit laps with a finish at the State Capitol building. You can expect the crowds in Sacramento to be some of the largest for the entire race.

See a map of the route to Sacramento & see a map of the race in Sacramento.

There will be a free health & cycling Lifestyle Festival  (10th Street between L and N) sponsored by MBT footwear in conjunction with the event. There is no better place to experience the spectacle of race day than at the Lifestyle Festival. The festival features a health & fitness expo, cancer awareness education, cycling gear, family activities, bike safety, food, entertainment, and more. There will be plenty to see and do for everyone in your family.

Other Amgen events: Sutter Health Community Ride, Breakaway from Cancer Walk. See a complete schedule & map.

Public Parking is available around the event. Garages available: Tower Bridge, Surface Parking Lot X, Old Sacramento, Memorial, Downtown Plaza: Central, East and West. See a map of parking restrictions.

title: 2011 Amgen Tour of California: Breakaway from Cancer Walk
description:
Sacramento will be hosting the Amgen Tour of California for the fifth year in a row. The Breakaway from Cancer Walk will take place in conjunction with the race. Amgen's Breakaway Mile is a walk to honor the millions of cancer survivors worldwide during the Amgen Tour of California. Those touched by cancer--patients, survivors, caregivers, and advocates--are invited to join this one-mile (approximate) walk across the Amgen Tour of California finish line, prior to the professional riders rolling across the finish.

Breakaway Mile participants will be invited to view the race action from a reserved viewing area near the finish line. The riders in the 2011 Amgen Tour of California will enter the downtown circuit and race around the State Capitol around 3:30pm and finish by the north steps of the State Capitol.

Public Parking is available around the event. Garages available: Tower Bridge, Surface Parking Lot X, Old Sacramento, Memorial, Downtown Plaza: Central, East and West. See a map of parking restrictions.

title: 2011 Amgen Tour of California: Sutter Health Community Ride
description:
At the Sutter Health Community Ride cyclists of all ages will be able to ride around the downtown circuit with Mayor Kevin Johnson. This event is in conjunction with the 2011 Amgen Tour of California. The event lines up at 13th & L Streets.

Public Parking is available around the event. Garages available: Tower Bridge, Surface Parking Lot X, Old Sacramento, Memorial, Downtown Plaza: Central, East and West. See a map of parking restrictions.

title: Movie Matinee
description: It’s the end of the school year--kick back and relax at Franklin’s Movie Matinee. This time we’ll be watching the despicable story of a despicable evil scientist who discovers there just might be more to life than being despicable.

title: Fancies: Found Love, Fleeting Love
description:
The Women's Choral Studio, a Sacramento-based chamber vocal ensemble under the direction of Catherine Fagiolo, celebrates three years of chamber vocal music-making with a program of part songs from the centuries-old tradition of participatory singing.

Fancies: Found Love, Fleeting Love features a selection of part songs ranging from the earliest part song known--a 13th-century canon, Sumer is icumen in--to three-part, light entertainment canzonette (little songs) from Claudio Monteverdi’s collection of 1584, and hallmark pieces from Schumann, Beethoven, and Britten. The Rose Trilogy of Eleanor Daley and songs of Stephen Foster round out the program.

The Choral Studio also welcomes the Voices NOW young singers and pianist Tavifa Mordovtseva to the concert in the lovely ambience of the 150-year-old Trinity Episcopal Church in historic Folsom.

Families are invited to this concert of lovely and accessible vocal music.

title: Scooter's Clean Air Pet Fest and First Birthday
description:
Please join us in bringing awareness this Spare The Air season with our mascot, Scooter, and all his friends. Scooter will be hosting Scooter’s Clean Air Pet Fest and celebrating his first birthday! Everyone is invited for the free festivities, even the family pet. The celebration will take place by the dog park area where you can enjoy food and music and check out pet oriented services and products to pamper your furry friends.

For more information on Spare The Air, please visit the website.

title: Capitol Ballet Company: A Classical Ensemble
description:
Capitol Ballet Company proudly presents A Classical Ensemble, featuring excerpts from Swan Lake, Le Corsaire, and the premiere of Grofe Variations. Stuart Carroll and Sharon Newton, Artistic Directors.

Capitol Ballet Company brings the beauty and artistry of ballet to a diverse audience of art lovers. The strength and vitality of their pre-professional dancers generates excitement and appreciation for the arts at venues throughout the Central Valley Region of California.
venue: Sheldon High School Performing Arts Center

title: Chhankata 2011
description:
Chhankata is the biggest outdoor International Bhangra Competition & family mela in California.

The event takes place in The Cove and X Lot.

title: Russian-Ukrainian-American Yarmarka Festival
description:
The 13th annual International Russian-Ukrainian-American Yarmarka Festival is sponsored by Afisha Russian Media. This festival is the most popular event of the year for our Russian speaking community. Each Yarmarka Festival takes the entire year between them to plan the next, and this proves to be more effective every year in creating public awareness and curiosity about European culture.

A traditional Slavic fair originated in the 19th century from a simple market place event, it evolved into elaborate Festivals with musicians, dancers, and artists performing in the town square surrounded by local merchants. We hope to bring back some of this festive spirit with concerts and display local businesses. This is a wonderful opportunity for Russian and Ukrainian people to celebrate their culture--and for Americans to enjoy learning about other traditions.

Communal celebrations involving carefully planned programs, outpourings of respect, rejoicing, or high revelry, are established by custom or sponsored by various cultural groups or organizations.

Yarmarka is a very memorable event for the whole Slavic community. The all-day-event features a number of bands and solo performers on a concert stage, entertainment and games for the children, picnics, food booths, arts & crafts booths, souvenirs, and products from local merchants, sports events, and much more. Native Russians who now live in the area and even out of state came together with the coordinators of the festival to create an exciting experience.

Afisha Radio, Russian Newspapers and TV will do remote broadcasts.

title: 43rd Annual Hangtown Motocross Classic
description:
No race is like it in Northern California, boasting more than 25,000 spectators annually, the 43rd Annual Hangtown Motocross Classic is coming to Prairie City State Recreation Park. It‘s not just any motocross race, but the oldest and one of the most coveted trophies on the 12 race Lucas Oil AMA Pro Motocross Championship Series. As host to professional motocross since 1968, the Dirt Diggers North Motorcycle Club (DDNMC) has established the Hangtown Classic as the crown jewel of the series, hosting the largest attendance of the season, year end and year out.

Since it was such a popular event, this year on Friday, the riders will be at Prairie City SVRA park for autograph signing for free with paid Saturday ticket, come join the fun! Outdoor series will start on Saturday. Practice and time qualifications will be in the morning; opening ceremony in the afternoon, and two motos each for the women, 250 and 450 classes. A full action packed day from sunup to sundown.

With expanded seating and hospitality section for spectators, the modified course will not only provide new vantage points to watch all of the action, but will bring the race closer to the huge spectator base that popularized Hangtown.

title: 19th Annual Pacific Rim Street Festival
description:
Taking place in Old Sacramento and the Westfield Downtown Plaza, for years the festival has displayed the richness and diversity of many Pacific Rim cultures through cultural programs, entertainment, art, and food. The event also enhances the community's knowledge of Asian/Pacific Island cultures in a fun and positive environment.

The street fest is planned and staged by volunteers from more than 15 Asian Pacific community groups. Their goals are to broaden the awareness and understanding of the Asian Pacific heritage, to showcase the many positive contributions to the community at large, and to lend support to cultural endeavors in the form of grants and scholarships. 

Each year an aspect of Asian culture is featured as the theme of the festival. For the year 2011, the theme is "Spice."

"We live in a multicultural world. The Asian Pacific Rim is just a small part of such diversity, that we live today. Like the spices and herbs that we put on our food each country takes on a flavor of its own. Many groups of explorers of all ethnicity fought many centuries ago and discovered and traded many spices. Many lives were lost because of the spice wars and trade that they tried to get all for their own. Anywhere from Africa to Arabian traders, each one had their ultimate origin in Southeast Asia." -Randall Ishida

The program for this event can be downloaded from the website. Please visit the website for more info and a full listing of sponsors.

title: Have Fun with Dad Day Basketball Tournament
description:
Father & Child Have Fun with Dad Day includes activities/games, Dad & Son Game, Dad & Daughter Game, and The Dads' Game.

Brought to you by The Center for Fathers and Families.

title: Carson and Barnes Circus
description:
For four generations the Carson & Barnes Circus has toured North America with their traditional Big Top Circuses. They strive to bring first-class family entertainment to all parts of America--small towns, big cities, urban America and native America, border to border, and coast to coast. Each year, Carson & Barnes searches for the best acts from around the globe and weave them together with their world-famous animal acts and traditional circus music to produce the finest Big Top show in America.

Carson & Barnes Circus takes place in Parking Lot A.

title: Cinderella
description:
Bob and Ro Productions brings children’s theatre to Citrus Heights with their production of Cinderella!

Two rotten stepsisters, a crabby stepmother, and an inexperienced Fairy Godmother--what is a girl to do?

title: River Cats Bike Night
description: As part of May is Bike Month, the first 100 people who ride to the game or are wearing a Bike Month I Ride t-shirt will receive a prize. Come out to the game and see the Sacramento River Cats take on the New Orleans Zephyrs.

title: '50s, '60s, and '70s Sing-Along Piano Bar
description:
Napa Valley is bursting into song with piano maestro Dan Daniels at the Wine Train Depot. Join your fellow song lovers in a '50s, '60s, and '70s Sing-Along Piano Bar. Featuring beloved hits such as "That'll Be The Day," "Great Pretender," "Rockin' Robin," "Downtown," "Pretty Woman," "Under the Boardwalk," "Maggie May," "One Less Bell to Answer," and "How Can You Mend a Broken Heart." Come and sing your lungs out with us or be a star and lead the group at the mic!

Free admission, all ages welcome, and no drink minimum. Buy a bottle from our Wine Shop to enjoy in the station with no corkage fee. Beer and other beverages available for purchase too. And no reservations are needed--just drop in when you're ready for a blast from the past!

title: 7th Annual International Kids Festival
description:
Bring your family and friends to the 7th Annual International Kids Festival for a great Memorial Day get-away (at no cost!). You will be sure to enjoy the stage entertainment program, professional magician show, face painting, jump houses, and lots of fun and prizes, including activities for the little ones.

For the seventh year, the International Kids Festival allows children from Russian-speaking, Asian, Latin, African American, Indian, and local communities to share their talent and cultural heritage on a professional stage.

title: Guided Nature Walk: Native Plant Walk
description: Join a naturalist led walk and learn to identify some of the common native plants of our area. Explore ways people have used plants for food, medicine, clothing, and shelter.

title: Sacramento County Fair
description: The 2011 Sacramento County Fair will celebrate 75 years of fair memories and magic at Cal Expo! Carnival, food, barn animals, music, shopping, and the popular demolition derby will entertain you, your friends, and your family for hours.

title: Sacramento Pride 2011
description: Join for Sacramento Pride 2011--the 26-year-old annual celebration of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender equality. Check the website for updates.

title: Art Happens...
description:
2nd annual Art Happens...shows the art of wine, beer, coffee, visuals, music, and more. This is a benefit to raise money for grants and scholarships to be distributed to selected artists and musicians throughout the Sacramento Region. 2011 News and Review Jammies winners will be performing as well as other local musical talent. This year, Sutter Middle School and Nevada Union High School will be selling student artwork to save their art programs. Adults and children will be able to experience art at various boothes such as clay, painting, beading, and more.

Please support over 30 local artists, 2 schools, 10 bands, businesses, wineries, and breweries. Let's build our SAC, Inc. community together.

title: Public Art Tour: Spring Beyond the City Center: North Natomas
description:
A guided tour of three artworks at the North Natomas Library including works by Ray Gonzales and James Piskoti. Artist James Piskoti will be present to talk about his work at the library.

Tour meets at the entrance to the library.

title: Three Little Kittens
description: "What...lost your mittens? You naughty kittens! So you shall have no pie!" Where are those mittens?

title: 53rd Annual Town & Country Art Fiesta
description:
We invite you to come celebrate at the Town & Country Art Fiesta. This family friendly event attracts thousands of people. It is the main fundraising event for the Sacramento Suburban Kiwanis. The show has been at the Town and Country Village Shopping Center since its inception 53 years ago.

Enjoy browsing and buying art and meeting the artists. The show features fine handcrafted art--from jewelry and sculpture to paintings and pottery and more. Artists are juried.

Proceeds from this event help children charities in the greater Sacramento region.

title: Extraordinary Things: Through the Eyes of Anne Frank
description:
A young girl’s view of the world cannot be shaken…even by its cruelest acts. A drama of life, love and courage for children ages 7 and older. This unique and profound coming-of-age story offers an intimate perspective of the extreme conditions millions of Jews faced in Nazi occupied Europe during World War II. The audience joins Anne Frank in hiding, guided by her diary entries, from an attic in Amsterdam alongside her family and four others. We watch as she deals with the everyday complexities of a girl becoming a woman, the unusual setting in which this change is taking place including a lack of space and privacy and several larger-than-life roommates, all set against the enormity of war.

Extraordinary Things: Through the Eye of Anne Frank is written by Dana Friedman and will feature Stephanie Altholz as Anne Frank. This is the fourth and final show of B Street’s 2010-11 Family Series.

Sacramento businesses support B Street Theatre. Bring your ticket stub to any restaurant partner for special discounts!

title: Carmichael Park Community Band Festival
description:
The Sacramento Valley Symphonic Band Association & Sacramento Symphonic Winds present the annual Carmichael Park Community Band Festival at the Carmichael Park Amphitheater. There will be a community band, one every hour, both days. Included in this year’s line-up is the 59th Army National Guard Band "The Governor’s Own." Bring the entire family, a picnic, lawn chairs, and enjoy a lovely afternoon of music under the shade trees!

title: Dorothy Meets Alice or The Wizard of Wonderland
description: Two of literature's most unforgettable young ladies get mixed up together in a magical meeting that produces hilarious results as the audience becomes reacquainted with a cast of familiar characters and sees them in a new light: the cowardly Lion, the White Rabbit, the Tin Man, the Mad Hatter, the Queen, and the Witch from those enduring classics The Wizard of Oz and Alice in Wonderland. This fun-filled romp follows Alice, Dorothy, and their friends as they try to unscramble their stories with the help of a contemporary young lad who started the whole thing to begin with when he put off a book report until the very last minute.

title: The Mastermind Hunt: Sacramento
description:
Assemble your teams, mark your calendars, and prepare to exercise your brains! We'll supply the map and clues, you bring your wits, a good pair of shoes, and your sense of adventure.

A unique event centered on the history and culture of Downtown and Midtown Sacramento. Fun and challenging clues will lead the players from Sacramento landmarks, to parks, and even to public art and local businesses. Fast-paced and exciting, the hunt is also an amazing opportunity for family and friends to learn about the city and their fellow hunters.

Partial proceeds will go to Hands on Sacramento, the regions full-service volunteer action center.

Clues can involve wordplay, puzzles, trivia, simple code-breaking, or other challenges, and are usually more difficult for one person to solve on their own. Teams that make use of the combined knowledge and skills of each member will have the greatest advantage. The hunt will last 2-4 hours, and is open to groups of friends and family ages 10 and up.

The Mastermind Hunt is presented by Mastermind Treasure Hunts and Downtown Grid. The hunt starts at the Courtyard at 1801L Street and runs on foot in Midtown and Downtown.

title: RoundRock 3on3
description:
RoundRock is more than just an annual 3 on 3 basketball tournament held on the streets of metropolitan areas. The event brings together athletes of varying degrees of ability, family and friends of all ages, and local businesses and charities. title: Screening & Discussion: Consider the Conversation
description:
Partners of Three Stages present Consider the Conversation, a beautiful film about a universal subject. The facts are these: thanks to the wonders of science, many of us live longer and die more incremental deaths. While 80% of us say that when our time comes we prefer to die at home, 75% of us will die in a hospital or nursing home. How can we live our lives to the fullest, right up to the end?

Featuring Dr. Martin Welsh (1954-2010), Consider the Conversation is an eloquent call to plan now, talk now, and prepare for the last part of your life to unfold. “A rich and engaging portrait of why we need to have end-of-life wishes respected,” Ellen Goodman, Pulitizer Prize-Winning Columnist.

Following the documentary screening, there will be a panel discussion. Panelists include the filmmakers Mike Bernhagen, Director of Community Engagement & Care Partner Relations at Rainbow Hospice Care of Jefferson, WI, and Terry Kaldhusdal, an Oconomowoc, WI teacher and filmmaker.

This West Coast premier is sponsored by Marshall Medical Center and Sacramento News & Review. Proceeds to benefit Snowline Hospice & Partners in Care.

6:30pm: Live Music Preshow

Also, review a moving editorial on the end of life by Dr. Martin Welsh in the Los Angeles Times.

description:
The National Train Show is fun for the whole family, from your littlest engineer to the most experienced Model Railroader. The 21st Annual National Train Show is the industry’s most respected model train show and trade exposition, which showcases all aspects of model railroading including the industry’s newest and unique products and services from manufacturers and retailers from the U.S. and around the world. The event will cover 134,000 sq. ft. of space, including 35,700 sq. ft. featuring extraordinary operating model train displays.

Special highlights:
-It’s All Here: All of the latest and greatest model trains, accessories, collectibles, and more from the world’s best-known manufacturers and retailers geared for all model railroaders--from first-timers to old-timers.
-The Incredible LegoMiniLand: It’ll stop you in your tracks! This 2,500 sq ft area is dedicated to the creation of a dynamic, originally-designed display featuring operating model railroads, hundreds of train cars, various landscape settings and waterfalls, scale buildings, retractable bridges, and more…all made entirely out of millions of Lego pieces! Attendees are invited to “meet the modelers” and learn how to build their very own original display.
-Ask The Collectibles Appraiser: Have an old train set hidden away in the closet? Wondering what it’s worth? Bring it to the show and find out from The Collectibles Expert. Free to all attendees.

The National Train Show was established in 1988 by the National Model Railroad Association as a nationally sponsored combined industry trade show and public train show to promote the hobby of model railroading. The 2011 National Train Show is held in conjunction with the National Convention of the NMRA in Sacramento.

.

About Charles Rosen: The breadth of Charles Rosen's endeavors reflects a remarkable synthesis of performing musician, scholar, writer, and lecturer. A widely respected pianist, he brings to bear upon his playing the weight of his fascinating and far-reaching intellect, which has given rise to several books, including Sonata Forms, which was nominated for a Pulitzer; the celebrated The Classical Style: Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven; and The Romantic Generation. He then spent six years studying with the legendary Moriz Rosenthal, who had been a pupil of Franz Liszt. Even with these roots deep in the great traditions of piano playing, he has not hesitated to blaze new trails, recording the complete piano music of Pierre Boulez, Igor Stravinsky’s Movements for Piano and Orchestra with the composer conducting and numerous solo piano works of Elliott Carter.

title: Ruth Eckland: At the Edge of the World
description:
At the Edge of the World is a multi-channel video installation by Ruth Eckland with music by Matt DiFonzo. Ruth Eckland’s At the Edge of the World is a meditation on the fragility, ambiguity, and uncertainty of what we think of as reality. Halcyon beach scenes are layered and juxtaposed with television news images of the sudden, catastrophic destruction of the Japanese tsunami. Unidentifiable figures pass through obliviously, or motionlessly bear witness. Borealis-like flashes of light signify another dimension beyond the quotidian, the cataclysmic, in which transcendence and illumination beckon.

As in much of the artist’s recent work, the video is altered to resemble experimental film or painting, creating metaphoric visions as if in a dream. Interpretation, including associative narrative, becomes a collaboration with the viewer. To aid in this process, sound is integral, much as in music videos or film scores. L.A. composer and producer Matt DiFonzo has written the music for the piece, adding layers of subtext to the visual images and creating a more evocative, immersive experience.

Eckland has exhibited throughout the U.S. and internationally and finds it particularly gratifying to discover the connection that viewers in countries as diverse as Costa Rica, Kazakhstan, Germany, Singapore, and China have made with the work. Some universal language seems to be communicated, some global core touched. Or, as Kenneth Baker has said in one of his many insightful reviews of Eckland’s work over the past few years in The San Francisco Chronicle, “Eckland handles video like the medium of collective dreams that we share without knowing it. Apparently she wants us to know it.”

Josh delighted his fans during last year’s Before We Begin shows, in which he solicited feedback from the audience on which songs should be included in the set-list. As a result, for the Straight To You shows, Groban will continue to interact with audiences and perform favorites from his best-selling albums, including his self-titled debut, Closer, and Awake, as well as songs from Illuminations.

title: Keith Urban: Get Closer World Tour
description: Keith Urban and his band, along with a very special guest, Jake Owen, go on tour in support of his sixth studio CD Get Closer.

title: Michael Jackson: The Immortal World Tour
description: The Estate of Michael Jackson and Cirque du Soleil present Michael Jackson The Immortal World Tour, written and directed by Jamie King, the leading concert director in pop music today. This once-in-a-lifetime electrifying production will combine Michael Jackson music and choreography with Cirque du Soleil creativity to give fans worldwide a unique view into the spirit, passion, and heart of the artistic genius who forever transformed global pop culture.

The Art Service Group will sponsor an antique appraisal session focusing on paintings with Jim and Karen Alkons, and gold, silver, coins, currency, antique photographs, and daguerreotypes with Doug Scougale

title: Chicanoism: American by Birth. Chicano/a by Choice

Chicanoism: American by Birth. Chicano/a by Choice features work by Esteban Villa & Simona Hernandez. Paintings and prints…Power to the people, la gente, el publo, la comunidad, el barrio, la colonia, la union, and la familia.

All ages welcome. Offering refreshments & music in garden. Sponsored by the Los Rios College Federation of Teachers. Chief Curator: George Esquibel. Assitant Curator: Carol Davydova.

title: Truth-Compassion-Tolerance Art Exhibition
description: The Truth-Compassion-Tolerance Art Exhibit has toured more than 40 countries and 200 cities worldwide. The oil on canvas exhibit features world-renowned artists portraying the experiences, visions, and hope of Falun Dafa followers as they attempt to safeguard justice and peace while upholding their values in truthfulness, compassion, and tolerance. The paintings depict these timeless values, often taken for granted, but even more cherished in challenging times. An inspiring exhibition not to be missed!

title: Screening: Special When Lit (Pinball Documentary)
description:
Special When Lit rediscovers the lure of a lost pop icon--pinball. This American invention made more money than Hollywood through the '50s and '60s. Its success swept the world making it the epitome of "cool." Today, pinball is all but forgotten. This is the definitive story of the rise and fall of pinball as told by the fans, collectors, designers, and champion players from across the globe. A game, a sport, a lifestyle--pinball takes this eclectic bunch of self-confessed "pinheads" back to their youth as they open up passionately to reveal the attractions of the "world's funnest toy."

Now pinball is virtually nowhere. Kids don't even know what a pinball machine is. People stay home for their entertainment and kids hang out online, not at the arcade or corner store. The fate of pinball seems decided, yet there exists a passionate subculture keeping the dream alive. Whether it's down at their local bar for a game, or choosing which game to play from a basement collection, pinball is a reality trip to a universe in a box. The ball is wild and can't be controlled, but the challenge to tame it never stops. It's a world that's special when lit.

title: Gem Faire
description:
Gem Faire, established in 1989, has become a world-renowned marketplace for the finest in gemstones, beads, jewelry, minerals, fossils, meteorites, lapidary equipment, metaphysical items, and much more at the lowest prices in today’s market. Over the years, Gem Faire has produced over 40 shows a year, making it the largest gem & jewelry show circuit on the west coast.

Gem Faire has brought together some of the world’s finest jewelry designers, importers, manufacturers, beading instructors, gemstone miners & cutters, along with certified graduate gemologists. At Gem Faire, professional dealers can also help you assemble, design, and utilize the piece you have carefully chosen and purchased. Or better yet, sign up for a workshop or class and learn how to make your own jewelry!

Gem Faire takes place in Cal Expo Buildings A & B.

title: Cast & Crew Call: Place Called Sacramento Film Festival
description:
For the twelfth year, Access Sacramento launches “A Place Called Sacramento” (PCS), a scriptwriting and short film production project for local writers and producers. PCS challenges local scriptwriters to write ten-minute scripts about the people, places, and events that make our community such a unique place to live.

Script evaluation and judging have been completed. Dozens of scripts have been reviewed by local professionals and ten have been selected for production. Meet the ten scriptwriter/producers Wed, May 18, 6pm-9pm at the “Cast & Crew Call,:" which takes place in the courtyard of the Coloma Community Center (4623 T Street, Sacramento).

All potential actors and production teams experienced and inexperienced are invited to attend. Ten production teams shall be formed and production continues on the films during the summer months. Finally, after weeks of hard work and great fun, friends gather at the Crest Theatre on Sun, Oct 2, 2011 for the World Premier of all ten films. The PCS production format is unique to Sacramento. In the previous eleven years, 109 films have been successfully created.

To view the films completed for the 2010 & previous PCS film festivals, go to the website below. Access Sacramento is a nonprofit organization dedicated to using community media to build better communications between individuals and groups in Sacramento County.

title: Small World, Small Works Exhibit
description:
The Small World, Small Works exhibition was designed as an opportunity for local artists to show their work with other artists from around the nation and the world. Specifically, we hope to bring artists from all parts of the world together underone roof for our visitors to enjoy. We hope to enlighten our visitors about art made by people from regions of the world that they would not normally have an
opportunity to see. We value the diversity found in all cultures today and believe that this event will bring people closer to one another through art.

title: Art Exhibit: Senior Show & Art Ball

Sacramento State presents its annual exhibit of work from graduating art students. Works encompassing all disciplines of study will be highlighted in the exhibition.

Come celebrate with amazing art, music, and food at The Art Ball--three-hours of gallery tours through campus, live music (The Hot Tar Roofers perform at 6pm at Kadema Hall), and great food on May 13.

title: Bus Tour of Fred Ball's Wallpieces
description:
The Northern California Enamel Guild is sponsoring a bus tour to see Fred Ball's enamels in Sacramento. The Sacramento Metropolitan Art Commission's Art in Public Places program is providing docents. Susan Willoughby, who is in charge of Ball's estate, will lead the bus tour. The tour will break for lunch at the new Crocker Art Museum where you will see more of Ball's work and discuss the work with Willoughby. The tour will include stops at four sites besides the Crocker, where Ball's work has been installed.

The bus tour begins & ends at the 3rd & L Street entrance to the City Parking Garage.

title: Screening: Nasty Old People
description:
This is Mette's story. Member of a neo-Nazi gang, her day job is to take care of four seniors that are waiting to die. Her life becomes a journey into a burlesque fairytale, where the rules of the game are created by Mette herself. Mette is indifferent about her way of life, until one night she assaults a man, kicking him senseless. Waking up the day after, she realizes that something is wrong, and accompanied by the seniors, she longs for respect and love. Together, they create a world of their own. A world you never knew existed. Written and directed by Hanna Skold. In Swedish with English subtitles.

Nasty Old People is one of a handful of feature films created and released under a Creative Commons license (BY-NC-SA), allowing for sharing and remixing the film. The screening at MOBS has been approved by writer/director Hanna Skold.

title: Film Screening: Play Again
description:
One generation from now most people in the U.S. will have spent more time in the virtual world than in nature. New media technologies have impacted our lives in countless ways, but what are we missing when we are behind screens? And how will this impact our children, our society, and eventually, our planet?

At a time when children play more behind screens than outside, Play Again explores the changing balance between the virtual and natural worlds. Is our connection to nature disappearing down the digital rabbit hole?

This emotionally moving and humorous documentary follows six teenagers who, like the "average American child," spend five to fifteen hours a day behind screens. Play Again unplugs these teens and takes them on their first wilderness adventure--no electricity, no cell phone coverage, no virtual reality.

Through the voices of children and leading experts including journalist Richard Louv, sociologist Juliet Schor, environmental writer Bill McKibben, educators Diane Levin and Nancy Carlsson-Paige, neuroscientist Gary Small, parks advocate Charles Jordan, and geneticist David Suzuki, Play Again investigates the consequences of a childhood removed from nature and encourages action for a sustainable future.

There will be refreshments and post-film discussion.

In this year-long series, they will explore how artists have taken the concept of light, to create a unique visual experience using both traditional and nontraditional media. Forrest Robinson's art is like a trip to a freak show, the kind that hardly exists anymore but which still lives in the moldy corners of the American subconscious. There's some strange stuff inside this tent. Over there, now—that's not the Gerber Baby, that's a Pickled Punk. Step right up and take a peek. Admission is free—and that's the weirdest thing of all.

title: Save the Music & Exquisite Inflorescence
description:
José Luis Villegas is a working photojournalist, currently with the Sacramento Bee. This project, Save the Music, is the story of keeping music alive. Blues music. Music born in slavery. The music that begat rock n’ roll. The music touched by God and the devil. The music that lives within rap and soul, but is dying on its own.

This is the story of America’s purest music at a cross roads, a time when the Prophet’s of soul are dying and only the great B.B. King can claim mass acceptance. For the rest, a living audience can be found in Europe. While in America, the voices of slaves and Negro spirituals grows ever fainter, the culture of the south fades away.

In Exquisite Inflorescence: Studies in Movement, Shape, and Color, photographers Ruth Henderson and Richard Ashby come together from different approaches to amaze, confound, and astound us, with their images of flowers. Brilliant, compelling imagery abounds, and forms both precise and mysteriously obscured dazzle us.

Richard Ashby, using a variety of orchid specimens, seems to have created an alternate universe. We find ourselves wandering in it while we marvel at this extravaganza of shape and color. Ruth Henderson, using her combination of multiple light sources, slight camera motion, and brief time lapse, compresses what amounts to a tiny motion picture into a single image, all in camera.

title: Screening: The Seventh Python with Producer & Director Q&A
description:
Director Burt Kearns and Producer Brett Hudson will be in attendance at the screening for a Q&A session.

You may remember Brett Hudson from the '70s pop group, The Hudson Brothers, who also were the stars of the 1974-75 Saturday morning show, The Razzle Dazzle Show which was on CBS.

A nonfiction musical feature film based on the life, work, and unplanned career of musical satirist Neil Innes, The Seventh Python traces one man’s winding path of whimsy as he flirts with destiny at the edge of fame with incredibly influential and unusually lasting work that keeps one foot each planted in the worlds of comedy and rock ‘n’ roll. From the Bonzo Dog Doo Dah Band to Monty Python's Flying Circus and The Rutles, to his Ego Warrior campaign, and his insistence on wearing a plastic duck on his head, Neil Innes has proven to be the greatest musical comedy satirist of the past fifty years. Yes, Neil Innes wears a duck on his head and he refuses to be famous. And it is his stubborn, brave resistance to celebrity culture and consumerism that is at the heart of this film that one early reviewer has called “touching, hilarious, and inventive!”

Featuring John Cleese, Eric Idle, Michael Palin, Terry Jones, Matt Groening, Emo Philips, and Aimee Mann.

title: Screening: My Heart is an Idiot + Q&A with FOUND's Davy Rothbart & director David Meiklejohn
description:
A screening of My Heart is an Idiot with FOUND Magazine's Davy Rothbart in attendance, along with director David Meiklejohn!

My Heart Is An Idiot is a romantic documentary that spans two years and over a hundred cities. The film captures the road-tripping lifestyle of Davy Rothbart (FOUND Magazine, This American Life, and frequent GQ contributor) who looks for love in all the right places, and in all the wrong ways.

Climb in the van with Davy as he tours North America promoting his magazine FOUND, a virally popular and iconic printed collection of discarded notes and photographs. Along the way, Davy seeks advice on his tortured love life from people he meets (Zooey Deschanel, Ira Glass, Newt Gingrich, Davy’s mom, and others), and attempts to follow that advice, with comic and surprising results.

The first feature-length film project from filmmaker David Meiklejohn, My Heart Is An Idiot weaves together multiple stories to illustrate the joys and dangers of romantic pursuit.

title: Mark Emerson: The Color of Rhythm & Penny Olson: Flowers and Water
description:
JAYJAY is proud to present The Color of Rhythm, new paintings by Sacramento artist, Mark Emerson and Flowers and Water photographic images by Penny Olson, an artist new to the gallery from Vallejo, CA.

Mark Emerson is a Sacramento favorite, at least for those of us drawn to abstraction with color, and its mysterious attributes, as a primary motive. A master at making paint shift and vibrate in his well-planned rectangles, which are most often squares, Emerson once again displays his virtuosity in these new paintings on panel, canvas and paper! The show title The Color of Rhythm refers to Mark’s love of jazz and how the music correlates with the paintings he makes; the colors moving slowly and then fast and in patterns. This new body of work is challenging---just like a modern jazz tune can be. They sometimes border on being too active, too bright, while seducing us with combinations of tone that are dissident and then they turn and please with resolve.

Penny Olson is making some amazing photographs of her own Vallejo garden and Northern California waterways, but the images do not resemble the subjects, other than the tone and color. These are abstractions created digitally and are primarily presented laminated between acrylic, which magnifies the image giving dimension to the photograph. All in square format, these very contemporary objects have the nuance of great painting, and the graphic quality of a photo. This is Olson’s first exhibit at JAYJAY.

title: Miráme: 21st Century Self-Portraits for Latino/a  America
description:
Selfless? Selfish? You looking at me?? If you’ve ever even once compared the number of “friends” you have on your Facebook page, looked at the photos (never mind the names), whipped out your iPhone to take 17 shots at the bar, the concert, the store, the sidewalk, the bathroom, let alone talked to your screen at night for your YouTube Channel, this bud's for you.

Miráme: 21st Century Self-Portraits for Latino/a America is a collection of various self-portraits, profile pics, and other representations of  “self.” “Selfish or selfless?” wonders curator Ella Diaz. “In the 21st century, portraits are everywhere, and they are as meaningful or as meaningless as the time it takes to create them.” Driven by the vast social media networks that occupy a new generation, this is high concept in low brow art form—complete with a karaoke machine on site set to Billy Idol’s “Dancing with Myself.”

The modern launch point for this focus on the self portrait, according to Diaz, lies with the revolutionary portraiture artist, Frida Kahlo. “Imagine it,” Diaz suggests, “a woman artist brazen enough to paint herself and from a subject position that looks her viewers right in the eye and boldly asks, “So what are you looking at?”

So, as fun as Miráme: 21st Century Self-Portraits for Latino/a America is intended to be, its historical antecedent is clear. “In the late twentieth century, Latino/a, Chicano/a, and Native American artists re-staged the self portrait,” Diaz writes. “They poked fun at its implications and the troubling stereotypes of savage warriors, mythic mulattas, and exotic native guides, all of which abound in the genre and the western imagination---the self-portrait has been thoroughly dismantled, revised, and re-hung on the wall of the master’s house. Meticulously staging oneself in a bathroom mirror; striking a pose with drunk friends at a bar; earnestly attempting irony through shadows, silhouettes, or a favorite pet; each of these is an accidental allegory for a larger social malaise and alienation in the virtual photo albums that we carefully create in our online shrines to self.”

Exhibiting artists are: Rio Yañez, Kelly Donahey, Francisco Gomez, Karissa McHurd , Erick Andino, Flaco Seagulls , Rye Purvis , Erika Romero, and Deborah Roberts.

title: Thekla Hammond: Paintings
description:
Bay Area painter and writer Thekla Hammond evokes ethereal, dreamlike spaces in her recent body of atmospheric paintings, Holding It Lightly. She addresses issues of tension and balance; and the formal relationship of line to form, of surface to deep space, of drawing to color, of structure to mark-making. These dramatic works suggest sky, ocean, and celestial images in a wondrous palette of passionate color.

Also showing:
Fred Martin: Abstract Paintings and Works on Paper
Gregory Kondos: Drawings and Limited Edition Prints

title: Painting for Paws
description:
The Happy Tails cats and dogs are once again busy with their creative endeavors, painting one-of-a-kind pieces of original artwork for this year’s Painting for Paws. With great artistic talent and enthusiasm, our talented four-legged residents are prancing their paws and swishing their tails through water-based, non-toxic paint to create colorful and exciting works of art. Pieces are matted and framed, and accompanied by a photo and bio of the furry artist. Proceeds from the artwork will benefit Happy Tails Pet Sanctuary of Sacramento.

title: Teaching Artist Workshop Series: Poetry Off the Page
description:
The Teaching Artist Workshop Series Poetry Off the Page: Crossing boundaries and expanding imaginations with words features performance/praise poet and writer Glenis Redmond, Kennedy Center Presenter. Refreshments are served. Parking is plentiful and free.

Glenis Redmond's love of words has carried her across the country for over thirteen years. Glenis logs over 35,000 miles a year bringing poetry to the masses. This Road Warrior Poet, though steeped in Afro-Carolinian roots, speaks a universal tongue of love, loss, celebration, sorrow, and hope. Her verse uplifts family, culture, and community. Glenis is a gentle pen pusher as she encourages others to find their voice at diverse venues across the country from prisons, universities, festivals, conferences, theaters to schools. Her poems soothe, illicit, and inspire others to pick up their pen and travel their own poetic road.

The Teaching Artist Workshop Series (TAWS) is a series of distinct workshops on a variety of topics of interest to artists who also want to teach and build careers as teaching artists. The series is developed and presented by the Arts Commission’s Education staff with regional and national presenters from the visual and performing arts and education fields.

title: Five More Plutos (Brave New World, New Insights into the Outer Planets)
description:
This talk is about the outer area of our Solar System, called the Kuiper Belt. This region is a metaphor for our expanding human consciousness and holds many surprises in terms of how it describes the issues for humankind in the future.

British astrologer and author Alison Chester-Lambert will be speaking on the dwarf planets. They’re the same classification to which Pluto was demoted and the former asteroid Ceres was promoted in recent years. The dwarfs are unusual in their naming. Some, like Makemake and Haumea, are named from the legends of the South Pacific, rather than the usual Greek myths. This isn’t the only thing that makes them exotic, as you’ll soon learn! Alison will give keywords for each dwarf planet and look at the inter-action between Neptune, Pluto, Makemake, Haumea, Ixion, Orcus, and Eris including the amazing connection with Ceres in the Asteroid Belt.

title: Relationship Astrology Workshop: Beyond the Myths of Sun-Sign Compatibility
description:
"Your task is not to seek for love, but merely to seek and find all of the barriers within yourself that you have built against it. It is not necessary to seek for what is true, but it is necessary to seek for what is false."

Astrological compatibility goes far beyond simple comparisons of Sun-signs between two individuals. Assessing true compatibility astrologically involves investigating both the potential for openness and the potential for blockage toward love in each individual.

It is only through conscious awareness of our differences in terms of values, romantic approach, and communication style that we can begin to accept one another in the form of “relationship.”

In this interactive workshop we will uncover your "unconscious" preferences and styles in relationships and learn to build your relationships "in love" rather than "in fear" based on your birth charts! This is a lot of fun and the epiphanies are very revealing.

Sign-up before the day of the event with your birth information and receive a freechart. Or, just bring your birth information (date, time & place) with you on the day of the event to participate in the interactive portion of the workshop without a chart.

Preview videos of some of the information that is covered in this workshop.

title: The Real Mayan Calendar: An Introduction to the Mayan Underworlds
description:
The Universal Co-Creation Cycle started on March 9 and it is off with a bang! Timeline for the Universal Co-Creation Cycle is here...But what does that even mean? While interest in the Mayan’s grand calendar systems has increased as we approach 2012, the confusion surrounding the implications of this information has hit an all time high. Is the world ending? Is the calendar just re-starting? What will happen after 2012?

These are just a few of the common questions surrounding this very misunderstood topic. Join for a class where instructor Christopher Robert Taylor briefly explores the work of Carl Johan Calleman and Ian Lungold in unraveling the mysteries of the Mayan calendar.

In this class you will learn how to distinguish the parts of the calendar that are re-calibrating from the parts that are actually terminating. You’ll learn about evolution through the “Mayan Underworlds” which form the backbone of the Mayan calendar system and which explain the increase in the frequency of change over time. Finally, you’ll learn how the process of creation has been occurring according to a timeline and that it is this process that is actually ending.

After the process of creation is complete…what will be the creation? Finally, according to the work of Calleman and Lungold the calendar system representing the process of creation does not actually end on December 21, 2012! Join and find out when it actually does end and what this may mean for humanity as a whole.

title: Wellness Workshop: What Does Freedom Mean to You?
description:
Here’s to a healthier 2011! What does “wellness” mean to you and to your family? The term “wellness” may mean something different to each of us. Is it physical, financial, or environmental wellness that means the most to you? How about all of the above?

This workshop is designed specifically to target all three areas of wellness:
Physical Wellness: We will show you what horrifying toxins may be currently in your home and how they could be affecting your health and the health of your family. They are there!

Women wear cosmetics an average of 145,600 hours during their lifetime. Learn what store-brand cosmetics are really doing or not doing to your skin and how they affect your health.

Moms and Dads, do you know that the foods we grow or that are grown for us are not delivering the nutrients needed to live a healthy life? In fact the vitamins and nutrients received in fresh fruits and vegetables have decreased substantially over the past 50 years. With fast food as our society’s main diet, what are our options? We are over-fed and under-nourished--sad, but true.

Financial Wellness: Learn how you can save money on your monthly necessities, along with saving time finding exactly what you need, not what you don’t need. No more trial and error at your expense. Who doesn’t want to save money?

Environmental Wellness: Find out what you can do to help prevent our beautiful environment from turning into a toxic brew. This topic is about being responsible with what you put down your drains, in your homes, or anywhere, for that matter.

The workshop is about an hour. That’s it! Think about it…isn’t your health and the health of your family worth this time. There are no products for sale at this seminar, just loads, information, and perhaps a prize or two.

title: An Adult Evening of Shel Silverstein
description:
Welcome to the darkly comic world of Shel Silverstein, a world where nothing is as it seems and where the most innocent conversation can turn menacing in an instant.

A bag lady in training? 60 words for boobs? Auctioning of a woman at her own request? A dead pony for a birthday present? The punishment for not reading the fine print?

Eight talented actors in ten imaginative scenes.

title: You Can't Take It With You
description:
At first the Sycamores seem mad, but it is not long before we realize that if they are mad, the rest of the world is madder. In contrast to these delightful people are the unhappy Kirbys. The plot shows how Tony, attractive young son of the Kirbys, falls in love with Alice Sycamore and brings his parents to dine at the Sycamore home on the wrong evening. The shock sustained by the Kirbys, who are invited to eat cheap food, show Alice that marriage with Tony is out of the question. The Sycamores, however, though sympathetic to Alice, find it hard to realize her point of view.

Meantime, Tony, who knows the Sycamores are right and his own people wrong, will not give her up and in the end Mr. Kirby is converted to the happy madness of the Sycamores, particularly since he happens in during a visit by an ex-Grand Duchess, earning her living as a waitress. No mention has as yet been made of the strange activities of curtain members of the household engaged in the manufacture of fireworks; nor of the printing press set up in the parlor, nor of Rheba the maid and her friend Donald; nor of Grandpa's interview with the tax collector when he tells him he doesn't believe in the income tax.

title: Dearly Departed
description:

They've got a funeral to plan and--between the feuds, marital flings, and Macaroni and Ham Loaf Surprise--it may escalate into a multiple-coffin memorial service. By the time the Turpins sort through the hangovers, money problems, and headstone engraving options, they've learned that coping with life's losses can turn out to be drop-dead funny.

title: Poetry Reading: Lawrence Dinkins and Josh Fernandez
description:
The Poetry Night Reading Series is proud to welcome poets Lawrence Dinkins and Josh Fernandez.

Lawrence Dinkins a.k.a. NSAA (pronounced en-sah-ah) is a dynamic and expressive Sacramento poet whose poems attack injustice and inhumanity. NSAA explores the African American experience, commenting on youth movements, musical rhythms, and social justice. He makes up half of the jazz-performance duo Electropoetic Coffee. He has just released a new book, Sub American, a collection of poems dealing with the concept of being a hyphenated American. In the book he explores a broad range of topics ranging from President Bush and Hurricane Katrina to the Civil Rights Movement.

Josh Fernandez was born in Denver, raised in metropolitan California and now lives and works in Midtown Sacramento where he attends Sacramento State as a master's candidate in the English Department. He writes for Spin.com, Boulder Weekly, San Antonio Current, and the Sacramento News and Review. His poetry is widely published, and he is often asked to speak on ethnic diversity, abuse and addiction, and his background as a writer and poet. Fernandez was recently nominated for a Pushcart Prize for his poem "The Last Thing He Said." Josh Fernandez's first, full-length collection of poems, Spare Parts and Dismemberment, was released May 1 on R.L. Crow Press, and it was reviewed in this week’s Sacramento News and Review.

Attendees are encouraged to arrive early at the John Natsoulas Gallery to secure a seat, and to sign up for a spot on the Open Mic list. The Poetry Night Reading Series, organized and hosted by Andy Jones and produced by Brad Henderson, occurs on the 1st Wednesday of the month at Bistro 33, and 3rd Thursday of every month at the John Natsoulas Gallery.

title: Free e-Waste Recycling in the Name of Charity
description:
Veterans of Foreign Wars Post 4607 has teamed up with All Green Electronics Recycling to host this electronics recycling collection event. Both members of the community and businesses can take this opportunity to clean out their garage or store room and donate their unused electronics to a good cause.

The event is designed to give residents and businesses the opportunity to properly dispose of electronic waste, which includes computers, laptops, monitors, keyboards, copiers, VCRs, fax machines, cell phones, printers, scanners, hard drives, stereo equipment, cables and cords, shredders, microwaves, and more. All Green Electronics Recycling recycles everything it accepts and nothing ever goes into a landfill. More importantly, materials are NEVER sent to be processed in developing nations–everything is done right here in North America!

Certified Data Destruction is available for a small fee at all of our events.

title: Hornet Car & Bike Show
description:
The Engineering and Computer Science Alumni Chapter will hold its annual Hornet Car & Bike Show in Parking Lot 8 at Sacramento State. (see a map of the location on campus).

The show, first held in 2009, is a fundraiser for student clubs, with residual funds allocated toward future scholarship through the ECS Alumni Chapter. The idea for the event was spawned by a need for funds to travel to the Society of Automotive Engineers competition, in which students design, build, and race a small, Formula-style race car against entries from other universities.

The ECS Alumni Chapter is running the event this year after the Hornet Racing Club spearheaded the first two. The show will feature music and door prizes that can be won by entering a raffle. Details on prize vendors are not finalized, but the main prize will be an iPad 2. Admission and parking are free for spectators; barbecue and beverages will be available for purchase.

Attendees who make a donation will have the chance to meet with prospective customers. All donations and gifts to the ECS Alumni Chapter, a nonprofit, are tax-deductible. Residual funds will go toward scholarships.
